<term>CAPNIO.</term> As far as I can see, no Christian ought to despise these numbers, which are strengthened as much by the testimonies of Holy Scripture as by Talmudic traditions. Rather, one should embrace and cherish them above gold, topaz, and every precious stone. For nothing more concise, nothing more effective, and nothing more necessary can be found to demonstrate against the Jews that these 70 weeks of Daniel were completed in the death of Christ. For in these numbers, the royal comparison of the solar and lunar cycles—which is so often ridiculed by the Jews—is not required, nor are many other things by which even a skilled theologian is often confused. Through these numbers, the stubborn impiety of the younger Jews is criminally convicted of both lying and theft—to such an extent that they can defend themselves with no evasion. Therefore, I ask that you proceed more clearly with what you have begun.

<term>GALATINUS.</term> We have learned, therefore, from the words of Holy Scripture—specifically from Jeremiah chapter 52 and 2 Kings chapter 25—that in the 19th year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, the first Temple was destroyed and leveled to the ground. Since, therefore, Nebuchadnezzar himself reigned 45 years, as has already been proven, it follows that he reigned for 27 years after the destruction of that same Temple. Nor is it an obstacle that the first year was incomplete. For the Talmud teaches that it was the custom of Scripture not only to count 7 months (excluding 10 days) which that year had as one whole year, but even sometimes to put one day for a year, as in the book *Rosh Hashanah* <note>original Hebrew: ראש השנה; "Head of the Year."</note>, in the chapter "There are four beginnings of the year" <note>original Hebrew: אר בעה ראשי השנה הן</note>. For there it is read: "The Master said: One day in a year is sometimes counted as a year" <note>original Hebrew: אמר מר יום אחד בשנה נחשב לפעמים לשנה</note>. If, therefore, to these 27 years (during which it is shown that Nebuchadnezzar reigned after the destruction of the first Temple) are added those 23 years in which his son Evil-Merodach reigned after him—as is proven by their Talmudic tradition—there are precisely 50 years. If you proceed in this same way with the remaining years of the aforementioned tradition—

<column-break/>

namely, the three years in which Belshazzar reigned afterward, and the two years of Darius; also the three years of Cyrus (whom they call *Koresh*) according to them, and 14 of Ahasuerus, and six of Darius (under whom the second Temple was completed)—when these are connected to the fifty years mentioned before, 78 years will be counted from the destruction of the first Temple to the completion of the second. From this, it is so manifest that they steal 8 years from us according to their own computation, that they can deny it with no excuse. And just as they strive to imperceptibly snatch away those 8 years in the eyes of men, so too they attempt to stealthily subtract 27 years from us out of the 30 years in which Cyrus reigned, asserting that he reigned for only three. For since Eusebius of Caesarea, Paulus Orosius, Jerome, and Bede, and all other historians, both Greek and Latin, have said that Cyrus himself reigned for thirty years, it is plainly evident that the Jews themselves are liars and thieves, and that they cast the nets of their falsehood in vain before the eyes of those with wings and vision.

<term>CAPNIO.</term> So that they may be more fully caught in the guilt of this theft, I would like you to prove through their own historians as well that Cyrus himself reigned for thirty years.

<term>GALATINUS.</term> Josephus—whom they call Joseph ben Gorion <note>Referring to the "Josippon," a medieval history of the Jews often attributed to Josephus.</note>—openly asserts that very thing among them. Likewise, the "Little Josephus" <note>An abridgment of the Josippon.</note>, the abbreviator of Josephus himself, clearly shows it while speaking thus in Hebrew: "Then when Cyrus heard that a certain eunuch had killed Belshazzar, the King of Babylon, he made a vow to build the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem and to return the vessels of the Temple." And a little later, he says: "It happened that Darius, King of the Medes, fell sick unto death. And he called Cyrus, his son-in-law and kinsman, and appointed him King in his place. And so it happened that the Kingdom of the Persians and Medes became one." And further down: "Moreover, Cyrus fought in the East, and took those who are beyond India, and in the Southern region, and all the land of Ethiopia, and all those dwelling in the ends of the South, and in the West even unto the land of *Sepharad* <note>original Hebrew: ספרד</note>, that is, of Spain. And in the North, all the land of Macedonia, and Cappadocia, and Scythia, and all the land of Elam, and Elazar, and the mountains of Eltahu and Hazar, even to the mountains of snow, which cannot be crossed. Are not the rest of the deeds of Cyrus written in the Book of the Kings of the Medes and Persians? And in the book of Joseph, son of Gorion, whom Titus the son of Vespasian took captive?" And a little later: "Cyrus fought further against the King of the Setim <note>The Scythians.</note>, that is, of Scythia. And the men of Setim turned their backs, and their King fell, and all their brave men. The others fled to the cities with Queen Tomyris <note>Tamyra in the text.</note> and her son. When Cyrus saw this, he feigned flight. Seeing this, the men of Setim went out after him into the plain. But Cyrus, turning back upon them, killed many of them. Thus the remaining men of Setim fled with the Queen to the mountains. And when Tomyris saw that her son was dead, she grieved vehemently and caused the mountain passes to be occupied. And when Cyrus, now fearing no adversary, was departing securely and confidently from the borders of the land of Setim, the whole army came out. He himself, remaining with a few men, stayed that night between two mountains. Tomyris, therefore, exposing herself to death, suddenly rushed into the camp of Cyrus and struck down two hundred thousand men..."

<margin>A</margin>
...of the brave Persians; and he captured King Cyrus. But the Queen <note>This refers to Tomyris, Queen of the Massagetae, a Scythian people.</note> girded herself, and like a wild beast whose cubs have been snatched away, she came to the corpse of Cyrus. Having cut off his head, she threw it into a pit full of the blood of the slain, saying: "Drink, Cyrus, and be satisfied, and drench yourself in the blood for which you thirsted. For thirty years you shed blood without measure." Thus King Cyrus found the end of his life in the land of the Scythians, and his son Cambyses reigned in his place. All these things are recorded by Iosephon the Hebrew <note>original: "Iosephon Hebræus"; referring to the *Josippon*, a 10th-century history of the Jews often attributed to Josephus in the Middle Ages.</note>. From these accounts, it is clearly evident that Cyrus reigned for thirty years after Darius, during which—according to the word of Queen Tomyris—he devoted himself to the shedding of blood. For it is neither possible nor likely that in the space of three years, which the Jews say he reigned, he could have subjected to himself so many kingdoms of the East, West, South, and North. From where, then, do the Jews take the occasion for such a great error as to attribute only three years to Cyrus?

GALATINUS: In the same way it is written in Daniel, chapter 11, that in the first year of Darius, the Angel Gabriel spoke these words to the same Daniel: "Behold, three more kings shall stand up in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than them all," and so forth. According to the Hebrews, the first of these three kings was Cyrus, who was also called Darius and Artaxerxes, as it is said in the book *Rosh Hashanah* <note>original: ראשׁ הַשָּׁנָה; a Talmudic tractate regarding the New Year.</note>, that is, "Of the Head of the Year," in the chapter beginning with "There are four heads of the year" <note>original Hebrew: אַרְבַּע רָאשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה הֵן</note>. There it is read word-for-word: "Cyrus is Artaxerxes, and he is also Darius. He was called Cyrus because he was a righteous king. He was called Artaxerxes because of his kingdom. And what was his proper name? Darius was his name." The second of these kings was Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther, who was also called Artaxerxes and Cambyses. The third was Darius, who was also called Artaxerxes, just as several other Persian kings were named Artaxerxes. The Jews, therefore, say that Cyrus reigned for only three years because they have not found him reigning for more in the book of Daniel. For this reason, they are to be judged much like a fisherman who, having caught three fish in the sea with a hook, asserted and contended that there were no more fish in the sea, simply because he himself did not know how to find more there. Let them grant, therefore, that Cyrus reigned for thirty years, even if all of them are not contained in the text of Scripture, just as they affirm that his son Ahasuerus reigned for fourteen years, although only twelve of them are found in the text.

CAPNIO: You have indeed demonstrated excellently that the Jews have begun the count of these seventy weeks poorly, deduced it worse, and concluded it worst of all. Nevertheless (forgive me), I would say you have accomplished very little unless you teach from their own scriptures how that same number begins well, proceeds better, and finishes best.

GALATINUS: It is necessary, then, for one who wishes to correctly begin the count of these 70 weeks of Daniel without the false accusations of the Jews, to attend more diligently to what the word of God sounded in the ears of Daniel from the mouth of the Angel Gabriel, when he said: "Know therefore and perceive, from the going forth of the word to return," or concerning the return, "and to build," or concerning the building of Jerusa-

<column-break/>

-lem, "unto the Messiah the Prince, shall be seven weeks, and sixty-two weeks." Here it is greatly to be noted how diligently Gabriel exhorts Daniel to know and perceive the time of the "going forth of the word" concerning the return of the people of God from the Babylonian captivity, and to begin the count of those same weeks from that time. Nowhere is the "going forth" of this word found more expressly—indeed, nowhere can it be found so evidently—than in Jeremiah chapter 29, speaking thus: "For thus says the Lord: after seventy years are completed at Babylon, I will visit you and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place" <note>original Hebrew: כִּי כֹה אָמַר יְהוָה כִּי לְפִי מְלֹאת לְבָבֶל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה אֶפְקֹד אֶתְכֶם וַהֲקִמֹתִי עֲלֵיכֶם אֶת דְּבָרִי הַטּוֹב לְהָשִׁיב אֶתְכֶם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה</note>. And again a little later: "And I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you, says the Lord; and I will bring you again into the place from where I caused you to be carried away captive" <note>original Hebrew: וְקִבַּצְתִּי אֶתְכֶם מִכָּל הַגּוֹיִם וּמִכָּל הַמְּקוֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר הִדַּחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם שָׁם נְאֻם יְהוָה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִי אֶתְכֶם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר הִגְלֵיתִי אֶתְכֶם מִשָּׁם</note>. And finally, after many words, he says in chapter 30: "Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring back the captivity of Jacob's tents, and have mercy on his dwelling places; and the city shall be built upon her own heap, and the temple shall remain after the manner thereof" <note>original Hebrew: כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה הִנְנִי שָׁב שְׁבוּת אָהֳלֵי יַעֲקוֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָיו אֲרַחֵם וְנִבְנְתָה עִיר עַל תִּלָּהּ וְאַרְמוֹן עַל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ יֵשֵׁב</note>. If anyone takes notice of these three authoritative quotes and the words of Gabriel spoken a little above, and compares them with one another, he will by no means be able to deny that the "going forth of the word" from the mouth of Jeremiah concerned the return of the people and the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple. He shows that the count of these 70 weeks was to be started from this going forth of the word. If anyone wished to deny this, I do not see how he could be a defender of the truth without being either devoid of mind or a shameless imitator of the mindless. 

Moreover, whoever wishes to know at what time this word went forth from the mouth of Jeremiah, let him read the 28th chapter of the same Prophet's book, which begins thus: "And it came to pass in that same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month" <note>original Hebrew: וַיְהִי בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִיא בְּרֵאשִׁית מַמְלֶכֶת צִדְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה בַּשָּׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁי</note>. And since he can find no other count of years closer than this in the aforementioned passages, it will be clearly open to him that in the fourth year of King Zedekiah, this word concerning the return of the people and the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple went forth from the mouth of Jeremiah. Now, the fourth year of Zedekiah was the 12th year of Nebuchadnezzar. For Zedekiah reigned 11 years, as is held in 2 Kings 24 and Jeremiah 52, when the city of Jerusalem and the temple were captured and burned in the 19th year of Nebuchadnezzar (as is evident in the same places). If, therefore, we follow the Talmudic tradition, which in the book *Megillah* <note>original: מְגִלָּה; the Talmudic tractate regarding the scroll of Esther and Purim.</note>, chapter 1, gathers from the words of Holy Scripture that Nebuchadnezzar reigned 45 years—in whose 19th year and 5th month (as was said) the temple was destroyed—we will surely have Nebuchadnezzar himself from that time in which the word concerning the return of the people and the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple went out from the mouth of Jeremiah...

Next, following the aforementioned tradition more diligently, let us add to these 34 years of Nebuchadnezzar himself the 23 years in which his son Evil-merodach reigned, and we shall have 57 years. If the three years of Belshazzar <note>original: "Balthafar"</note>, the son of Evil-merodach, are joined to these, we have 60 years. Since things are so, it has been made sufficiently clear, I believe, through the Jewish scriptures, that these 70 weeks of Daniel were precisely completed in our Lord Jesus Christ, as will appear far more clearly in what follows.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->That according to our own histories as well, both Greek and Latin, the prefixed time of the Messiah contained in these 70 weeks was precisely fulfilled in the death of Christ.<-

#### CAPNIO.

<margin>A</margin> Indeed, by following the reckoning of the Talmudists <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note>, we conclude our proposition against the modern Jews using their own scriptures: namely, that the time of these weeks was completed in the death of Christ (as you have now proved). But I think we will hardly be able to achieve this if we choose to follow our own histories, both Greek and Latin, in the calculation of these weeks. For we and they are quite different regarding the histories of the Medes, Persians, Greeks, and Romans. Therefore, I will consider that you have done no small thing if you can show through our histories as well that the prefixed time of the Messiah contained in these 70 weeks was fulfilled in the passion of Christ. GALATINUS: We and the Talmudists are indeed far apart in the calculation of years (as you say). For from the fourth year of Zedekiah <note>The last king of Judah before the Babylonian captivity.</note> until the passion of Christ, according to their histories, 486 years and six months passed (as we have shown), which complete 69 and a half weeks. But according to our own histories, both Greek and Latin, 125 more years elapsed. Likewise, according to their calculations, the Second Temple is found to have stood for 420 years from the time 

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> it was completed until its ruin. According to our own reckonings of time, however, that Temple lasted about 559 years. Therefore, those who wish to convince the Jews through their own scriptures ought to begin the calculation of these weeks from the time when the word of God, promising the return of the people, issued from the mouth of Jeremiah—namely, from the fourth year of Zedekiah, as we have shown most extensively in the preceding sections. But those who desire to reach this truth through our histories as well <margin>B</margin> must begin this calculation from another time. They will be able to do this more easily if they more diligently examine the words of the Angel, when he says: *From the issuing of the word that Jerusalem should be built again, until the Messiah the Prince.* It is as if he wanted to say: The beginning of these weeks will be at that time when the word concerning the rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem goes forth, and they shall reach until the Messiah. Since mention is made in these words of the rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem, <margin>C</margin> these weeks ought to begin precisely from that time when the word concerning the rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem issued forth. It is well established that this happened in the 20th year of the reign of Artaxerxes Longimanus <note>Artaxerxes I, King of Persia (reigned 465–424 BC), nicknamed "Long-handed."</note>, King of the Persians, who gave the Jews the power and liberty to rebuild Jerusalem. For so it is read word-for-word in the second chapter of the Book of Nehemiah: "It happened in the month of <term>Nisan</term> <note>The first month of the Hebrew calendar, corresponding to March/April.</note>, that is, March, in the 20th year of King Artaxerxes: and wine was before him, and I (namely, Nehemiah) lifted my hand and gave it to the King. Now I was as if languishing before <margin>D</margin> his face, and the King said to me, 'Why is your face sad, since I do not see that you are sick? This is not for nothing, but some evil I know not what is in your heart.' And I feared greatly and exceedingly, and said to the King, 'O King, live forever. Why should my face not mourn, when the city of the house of my father's sepulchers lies waste, and its gates are consumed by fire?' And the King said to me, 'For what thing do you make request?' And I prayed to the Lord of heaven, and said to the King, 'If it seems <margin>E</margin> good to the King, and if your servant finds favor in your sight, I beseech you to send me into Judea, to the city of my father's sepulcher, and I will build it.' And the King and the Queen, who sat next to him, said to me, 'Until what time shall your journey be? And when will you return?' And I was pleasing before the face of the King, and he sent me." Thus far the text. And then for the first time was liberty and power given to the Jews to build the city of Jerusalem again. For although they had previously received from Cyrus the liberty both to return from captivity and to construct the Temple, they had not yet received the power to build <margin>F</margin> the aforementioned city anew, nor had they been able to finish the Temple which they had begun to erect under Prince Zerubbabel. From this it clearly appears that, according to the Angel’s instruction, the counting of these weeks ought to have begun from the 20th year of Artaxerxes Longimanus, from which the word first went out that Jerusalem should be built again. That these weeks reached until the passion of Christ <margin>G</margin> can easily be seen from the harmony and connection of Greek and Latin histories. CAPNIO: This is exactly what I would most like you to do. GALATINUS: Therefore, after this Artaxerxes sent Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem, he reigned for twenty more years. After him...

Indeed, in the middle of the final week, the Messiah was to be killed. From these things, it has certainly been shown openly that the determined time of the Messiah revealed by the Angel to Daniel was precisely fulfilled in our Lord Jesus Christ.

### CHAPTER XVII.

->*Against the obstinate temerity and insanity of Rabbi Solomon, Rabbi Levi, and other younger men, who most impudently attempt to pervert the words of Daniel.*<-

### CAPNIO.

ALTHOUGH the more recent Jews, defeated by their own scriptures as if by their own weapons, are by no means able to deny that the Messiah has already come and that he was our Lord

<column-break/>

Jesus, they are nevertheless so blinded by a desire for slandering and contradicting that they hardly notice how absurd, how impossible, and how inconsistent with the divine scripture are the things they chatter about in various ways against this prophecy of Daniel. They attempt with all their might to show that the things Gabriel said to Daniel about the Messiah should be understood not as the true Messiah promised in the Law and the Prophets, but as some other person. For some say the Messiah expressed in Gabriel's first speech—when it is said, "Until the Messiah the Leader"—was Cyrus; among these is Rabbi Solomon <note>This refers to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo itzhaki), the famous 11th-century commentator.</note> in the exposition he published on Daniel.

<margin>*Various errors of the Jews regarding the acceptance of the Messiah.*</margin>

But others say the Messiah himself was Nehemiah; among these is Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra, as his exposition on Daniel shows. Others, however, assert that the Messiah himself was Joshua the High Priest; among these is Rabbi Levi <note>This refers to Gersonides (Ralbag).</note>, as his writings on Daniel indicate. Furthermore, others affirm that the Messiah himself was Zerubbabel; many today follow their opinion. Others again explain the Messiah placed in the second instance—namely, where it is said, "And after sixty-two weeks the Messiah shall be cut off"—as being Agrippa; Rabbi Solomon also followed these. Therefore, so that their insanity may appear more clearly, I would like you to refute the delusions of each one with a truthful response.

<margin>*Refutation.*</margin>

GALATINUS: You rightly judge them to be insane in this, as in other things. For what else does such absurd diversity in contradicting so evident a testimony of Gabriel show, other than that the grim omen of Moses has happened to them? It was prophesied of them in Deuteronomy, chapter 28: <note>original: "יכך יהוה בשגעון ובעורון ובתמהון לבב והיית ממשש בצהרים כאשר ימשש העור באפלה ולא תצליח את דרכיך"</note> *That is, God will strike you with insanity, and blindness, and stupor of heart. And you shall grope at midday, just as a blind man gropes in the darkness. And you shall not direct your ways.* 

Therefore, where it was said by the Angel to Daniel, "Until the Messiah the Leader, 7 weeks and 62 weeks," it is manifest that whoever asserts there is another Messiah there than the true Messiah promised in the Law and the Prophets has incurred both insanity and the other curses mentioned just before. For no one is ever found in Holy Scripture called "Messiah" <note>The word *Messiah* (Mashiach) literally means "Anointed One."</note> who was not anointed either with that holy physical oil with which Kings and priests were anointed, or with the spiritual oil—that is, the grace of the Holy Spirit (which the holy David in Psalm 45 calls the "oil of gladness"). 

However, neither Cyrus, nor Nehemiah, nor Joshua the High Priest himself, nor Zerubbabel, nor Agrippa, nor anyone else of that time can be said to have been anointed with the aforementioned physical oil, since that oil was never in the final Temple. This is best proved in the Jerusalem book of Sanhedrin <note>The Talmudic tractate dealing with law and the high court.</note>, where in the chapter <note>original: "אלו הן הגזולים"</note> *Elu hen haggolim*—that is, "These are the captives"—Rabbi Samuel says: "Five things were missing in the last Temple which were in the first." And from where is this proved? From what was said in Haggai, chapter 1: <note>original: "עלו ההר והבאתם עץ ובנו הבית וארצה בו ואכבד"</note> *Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house, and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be honored.* For here, the word <note>original: "ואכבד"</note> *ve-ekkavda* ("I will be honored") is written in a diminished way, without the letter <note>original: "ה"</note> *He*, which signifies "five," to designate the five things in which the final sanctuary was lacking.

...was diminished from the first, namely the fire, the ark, the *Urim and Thummim* <note>original Hebrew: אורים ותומים; these were sacred objects used by the High Priest to determine God's will</note>, that is, the lights and the simplicities—which is the breastplate of judgment—the oil of anointing, and the Holy Spirit. This same point is also clearly shown in the *Midrash Shir HaShirim* <note>A Jewish homiletic commentary on the Song of Songs</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Song of Songs, regarding that saying in chapter 8: *We have a little sister, and she has no breasts* <note>original Hebrew: אחות לנו קטנה ושדים אין לה</note>. For there it is said: "We have a sister"; these were those ascending from the captivity. "Little," because they were few in their armies. "And she has no breasts"; these are the five things in which the latter holy house was diminished from the first: namely the fire, the ark, the *Urim and Thummim*, that is, the lights and simplicities in which future things were seen, the oil of anointing, and the Holy Spirit. Therefore, from the mouths of these two witnesses, it is clearly evident that the oil of sacred anointing—both physical and spiritual—was missing in the most recent temple, since they say that neither the Holy Spirit nor the oil of anointing was present in it at that time. From this it is concluded that neither Cyrus, nor Nehemiah, nor Joshua the High Priest, nor Zerubbabel, nor Agrippa, nor anyone else of that time, except Jesus of Nazareth—who, as the Psalmist says, was anointed with the oil of gladness—could truly be called the Messiah according to the truth. For the Messiah must be anointed with the oil of anointing, either physical, or spiritual, or both together.

<margin>Objection of the younger Jews.</margin>
**Cap.** At this point, the Jews could object to us that sometimes in the sacred scriptures, those anointed with neither oil were called "Messiah." For it is said in Psalm 105: *Do not touch my Messiahs* <note>original Hebrew: אל תגעו במשיחי; usually translated as "my anointed ones"</note>. <margin>Refutation.</margin>
**Gal.** The ancient Talmudists answer them and show that they are speakers of falsehood in this matter as in others. For the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>An ancient commentary on the Book of Psalms</note>, that is, the exposition of the Psalms, says regarding that statement, "Do not touch my Messiahs," that in that place the "Messiahs" are understood to be the ancient patriarchs: namely Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, whom no one denies were anointed with spiritual oil—that is, the spirit of prophecy. However, when Isaiah said, "Thus says God to his Messiah Cyrus, whose right hand I have strengthened," I believe it must be Catholicly affirmed that God was speaking there not to Cyrus, the King of the Persians, but to the true Messiah. This is stated in the Talmud, in the book called *Megillah* <note>A tractate of the Talmud concerning the festival of Purim</note>, where it is read word for word: "What is this that is written in Isaiah, 'Thus says God to his Messiah, to Cyrus'? Was Cyrus the Messiah? No: but the Holy and Blessed God said to the Messiah: 'I place you against Cyrus, whose right hand I have strengthened,'" and the rest which follows in the same chapter of Isaiah. Also, Rabbi Solomon <note>Referring to Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator</note>, explaining this passage of Isaiah, says: "The masters said that the Holy and Blessed God said to the King Messiah, *kobel* <note>original Hebrew: קובל</note>, that is, 'I place you against Cyrus,' just as it is said in the book *Megillah*." Therefore, whichever of the Jews says the contrary rages like a madman against the authority of those whom he contends are truth-tellers.

But if he says he means the sins which the Jews committed during the time of the Second Temple, certainly by saying so, he asserts that God is unjust. 

For those most grave and intolerable sins committed by the Jews at the time of the First Temple—namely idolatry, the slaughter of so many prophets, and so many unspeakable crimes—He wiped away with only seventy years of Babylonian captivity; and during that captivity, He also bestowed many benefits upon them, namely prophets, miracles, and other honors. Yet the sins committed during the time of the Second Temple, which were light in respect to those others, He has not yet wiped away through so long a captivity and so many calamities, nor has He ever granted in this current captivity any of the benefits He had granted them in the Babylonian captivity. Therefore, it must necessarily be concluded that the Angel spoke to Daniel about a different sin than those which this treacherous Rabbi mentioned.

The third error is when he affirms that the Ark and other vessels of the sanctuary ought to be understood by the phrase "Holy of Holies" or "Sanctuary of Sanctuaries." This is expressly against the meaning of Holy Scripture, which says thus in Jeremiah, while speaking of the redemption of the Jews: <term>In those days, says the Lord, they shall say no more, The Ark of the Covenant of the Lord: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more.</term> <note>original: בימים ההם נאם יהוה לא יאמרו עוד ארון ברית יהוה ולא יעלה על לב ולא יזכרו בו ולא יפקדו ולא יעשה עוד; Jeremiah 3:16</note> This is because, as we shall say in another place, all ceremonies of the Old Testament were to cease entirely after the passion of the Messiah. From this it is clearly evident that the phrase "Sanctuary of Sanctuaries" or "Holy of Holies" cannot be understood as the Ark or the other vessels of the sanctuary.

The fourth error is when, regarding that phrase, "Know therefore and understand, from the going forth of the word," he wants this proposition—<term>from the going out of the word</term> <note>original: מן מוצא דבר</term>—to be treated as a general preposition. He does not want it to signify the specific "starting point." But we clearly see the opposite through the Angel's own words, who subsequently placed the "ending point" when he added "unto Messiah the Prince."

The fifth error is when he said that by this "Messiah the Prince," King Cyrus of the Persians is to be understood. That this is indeed false is manifest for multiple reasons. First, because when the Angel said "unto Messiah" <term>the Prince</term> <note>original: נגיד (Naghid); a term meaning leader or commander</note>, he excluded both Cyrus and everyone else besides the Principal Messiah. Second, because he did not say there would be only seven weeks until the Principal Messiah, but seven and sixty-two. Third, because even according to their own calculation, it is established that those seven weeks, containing forty-nine years, were completed not at the time of Cyrus, but at the time of Belshazzar, as was shown above through Talmudic tradition. According to which it is said that after the destruction of the first temple—from which they themselves begin to count these weeks—Nebuchadnezzar reigned for twenty-seven years, and Evil-merodach his son for twenty...

...tribes: all of whom number fifty. Then Belshazzar himself reigned for three years; after him, Darius for two; and then Cyrus himself began to reign. For this reason, it is evident that, according to the calculation of the Talmudists, the Angel was by no means speaking of Cyrus when he mentioned "Messiah the Prince" <note>original: "Messiam Ducem"</note>. 

The sixth error is when he says this Messiah who was to be killed was Agrippa <note>King Agrippa II, the last of the Herodian line</note>, asserting that he was killed by the Romans during the destruction of the second temple. Josephus reports the opposite in his book *The Jewish War*, stating that Agrippa himself went to Rome and, while that war was ongoing, struck a treaty with the Romans. 

Finally, the seventh error is when he says that specific phrase—"And he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week, and in the half of the week he shall cause the slaughter and the offering of sacrifices to cease"—should be understood as referring to Titus, the son of Vespasian. He claims that Titus himself, having struck a treaty with the Princes of the Jews, was supposed to dissolve and destroy it in the middle of that same week. This completely contradicts the truth. For as Josephus says in the same book, Titus himself approached the destruction of the city of Jerusalem and the temple not willingly, but reluctantly. For this reason, he strove many times—now by himself, now through others—to persuade the Jews not to be the cause of that place’s destruction.

### CAPNIO. 
My excellent Galatinus, you have uncovered the errors of Rabbi Solomon’s <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105)</note> perverse exposition, to which the rest of the more recent Jews strongly adhere, by using the writings of their own ancestors. ### GALATINUS.

For he thought this could lawfully be done because their sins had already been erased by the punishments they had endured. However, the Angel notified him that the matter would not proceed according to his thought. For that temple was not meant to remain except for seventy weeks starting from the destruction of the first temple, which are 490 years. 

Or perhaps by this, the Angel wished to signify that Daniel had not extended his prayer to such a long time just to know that the structure of the second temple ought not to exceed the established time of seventy weeks—because it had been so ordained by God—but rather so that through this long-lasting captivity, the sin of Israel might reach an end. This would be to the extent that it might deserve to receive the "everlasting righteousness" <note>original: "iustitiam sempiternam"</note>, which was interpreted by Daniel to Nebuchadnezzar as the Fifth Kingdom. This "everlasting righteousness" is the Messiah himself, through whose coming every vision and prophecy will be fulfilled. "And to anoint the Holy of Holies" <note>original: "sanctuarium sanctuariorum"</note>. For then the holy things will be anointed with the oil that was hidden in the second temple. If these things are inspected correctly, two things in particular are found against him within them. <margin>E</margin> The second is that while he approves of an inconsistency he strives to avoid, he falls into several other inconsistencies. <margin>F</margin> and for the satisfaction of the common people, having omitted the first exposition, he arrived at the second. ...The claim that the Angel did not care how the mysteries were verified is undoubtedly ridiculous. For these two dignities—the royal and the priestly—are usually attributed to no one in the Sacred Scripture except the Messiah. For that which was said by David in Psalm 110: <margin>A</margin> **"You are a priest forever"** <note>original Hebrew: *atah kohen l'olam*</note>; and that which is written in Isaiah 55: **"Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the nations"** <note>original Hebrew: *hen ed le'umim netativ nagid umetzaveh*</note>; both are spoken concerning the Messiah. Finally, what he says regarding that clause, "The Messiah shall be killed, and shall have nothing," directly contradicts him. From this, it necessarily follows that the priestly office also ended then, since he understands the "Messiah the Prince" to be the High Priest. He also confirms this through the final part of the prophecy, when he says the Jewish people were destined to be laid waste by Titus in the ultimate desolation. Since these things are so, anyone can easily judge the extent of the treachery and perversity of the younger Jews <note>The author uses "younger Jews" to refer to medieval and contemporary Rabbinic commentators who disagree with earlier traditions that Christians saw as more compatible with their faith.</note>, who involve themselves in so many contradictions rather than confess the truth.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

-> *The true and universal explanation of the prophecy of Daniel itself, through the scriptures of the Jews.* <-

-> CAPNIO <-

<margin>B</margin> It now remains for you to undertake the true and universal exposition of this vision or prophecy, according to their own [the Jews'] opinions. GAL. I think it should first be noted that the fifth Kingdom—that of the Messiah, which was never to have an end—had been revealed to Daniel through both the dream of Nebuchadnezzar and the visions he himself had seen. Furthermore, Daniel himself had foreseen the wars of Gog and Magog (that is, of the Antichrist), after which the remnants of Israel are to be saved. As he turned over in his mind the words of God Himself in the 29th and 30th chapters of Jeremiah, promising the return of Israel from the Babylonian captivity, he desired above all else to understand the progression of these mysteries. For this reason, he gave himself to prayer, beseeching God with his whole heart that, in His mercy, He might deign to satisfy his desire. He surely deserved to be heard in this vision. For he was not only praying for the return of the people and for the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple (as the more recent Jews assert); rather, his prayer 

<column-break/>

extended itself to higher mysteries and to longer spans of time (as Rabbi Levi says). Daniel himself hints at this at the beginning of this chapter, while he says, "I, Daniel, understood by the books," which is to say, I meditated on the mysteries contained in the books. And for this reason, the Angel said to him, "Daniel, I have now come forth"—namely, from the presence of God—"to teach you understanding," specifically of the mysteries you so greatly desire to know. "From the beginning of your prayers the word went forth," that is, a definitive sentence went out from God. "And I have come to show it to you, for you are a man of desires." Take note of the "word," namely, that it went out from God, and "understand the vision," this vision which encompasses great mysteries: "Seventy weeks," that is 490 years, "is the time shortened," that is, predetermined or predestined (by God) "upon your people and upon your holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sin, and to wipe out iniquity." 

Since this (as was seen a little earlier while disproving the errors of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105).</note>) can in no way be verified concerning the sins committed during the time of the first or second temple, it must necessarily be understood regarding the transgression of the first parents, and regarding Original Sin, and the iniquity of the whole human race, which were to be destroyed through the death of the Messiah. This is also clearly hinted at by the Angel's way of speaking, when he does not say "sins" [plural], but "sin" in the singular. For as Rabbenu Hakkadosh <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, though here the author cites a later work attributed to such figures.</note> excellently testifies in the book called **The Revealer of Secrets** <note>original Hebrew: *Gale Razia*</note>, the Messiah was to come to release Original Sin and to bring souls into paradise. 

Then the Angel adds, "And to bring in everlasting righteousness," <margin>C</margin> <margin>D</margin> <margin>E</margin> <margin>The Gospel Law.</margin> <margin>F</margin> <margin>G</margin> <margin>The Messiah is called the Holy of Holies.</margin> that is, the Gospel Law, which was to contain the righteousness of all ages and was to be given by the Messiah. Indeed, as Rabbi Moses Hadarsan and Rabbi Levi explain in this place, "everlasting righteousness" is nothing other than the Messiah, of whom it is written in Isaiah chapter 56: **"Keep justice and do righteousness, for my salvation is close at hand to come, and my righteousness to be revealed."** <note>original Hebrew: *shimru mishpat ve'asu tzedakah ki kerovah yeshuati lavo vetzidkati lehigalot*</note> On this, Rabbi Berachiah says: "Keep justice and do righteousness; these are the commandments and good works. Because my salvation is close at hand to come, and my righteousness to be revealed; this is the Messiah, of whom it is written in Daniel chapter 9: 'And to bring in everlasting righteousness,' that is, the Messiah." Thus he says. 

"And to seal up the vision and the prophecy," namely those which spoke of the Messiah, by whose arrival (according to the gloss of Rabbi Levi) every vision and prophecy was to be fulfilled. "And to anoint the Holy of Holies," which, according to the opinion of the ancient Talmudists, is nothing other than the sanctified Messiah. Following them, Rabbi Moses son of Nahman of Gerona <note>The famous commentator Nahmanides, also known as Ramban (1194–1270).</note> says in this place: **"The Holy of Holies is the Messiah... the Sanctuary from the sons of David."** <note>original Hebrew: *Kodesh Kodashim hu ha-Mashiach... Mikdash mi-benei David*</note> Nor is the Messiah called the "Holy of Holies" in this place without reason, since it was destined that in him, according to his humanity, all the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge of God would be hidden.

**CAP.** Here the Jews of our time object, because the word *iccareth* <note>original Hebrew: יכרת</note> which is placed here, comes from the word *carath* <note>original Hebrew: כרת</note>, which does not mean "to kill," but properly "to cut off." **B** **GAL.** Although the word *iccareth* primarily signifies "to cut off," it is nevertheless very frequently used in Sacred Scripture to mean "to kill." For example, in Genesis 9: "And I will establish my covenant with you, and all flesh shall not be *iccareth*" <note>original Hebrew: ולא יכרת כל בשר</note>, that is, all flesh shall not be *killed* anymore by the waters of the flood. For the Sacred Scriptures frequently call the Law a "covenant." This was for the "many" who would believe in him and receive his law. "In one week," that is, in seven years. For those three and a half years in which Christ taught, and the other three and a half years in which the Apostles preached in Judea after him, complete the one week in which the Messiah was to confirm his law by deed and word, first by himself and then through his disciples. Concerning this law, it was predicted in Jeremiah 31: <note>original Hebrew: הנה ימים באים נאם יהוה וכרתי את בית ישראל ואת בית יהודה ברית חדשה לא כברית אשר כרתי את אבותם ביום החזיקי בידם להוציאם מארץ מצרים אשר המה הפרו את בריתי ואנכי בעלתי בם</note> "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will strike a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—a new law. Not like the covenant I struck with their fathers, that is, not like the law I gave to their fathers on the day I strengthened their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, for they voided my covenant, and I rejected, or neglected, or abandoned them." Therefore, when it is said here, "He shall confirm the covenant for many in one week," "covenant" is understood to mean "law." For although **Berith** <note>Hebrew: ברית</note> means a league or a pact, in many places in Holy Scripture it is understood as "law," as is clearly evident in the aforementioned words of Jeremiah. This is also openly proven in the book **Mechilta** <note>A collection of Jewish rabbinic interpretations (midrash) on the Book of Exodus.</note> regarding the passage in Exodus 12, "On the tenth of this month," where it is said: <note>original Hebrew: אינו ברית אלא תורה, כמו שכתוב באלה הדברים אלה דברי הברית אשר צוה יהוה את משה לכרות את בני ישראל בארץ מואב מלבד הברית אשר כרת אותם בחורב</note> "It is not a covenant (*berith*) except for the Law (*Torah*), just as it is written in Deuteronomy 29: These are the words of the *berith*, that is, of the covenant, which is to say the law, which God commanded Moses to strike with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant he struck with them at Horeb." Thus far the quote. From this it is clearly evident that "covenant" is taken to mean "law." Furthermore, that the Messiah would teach with his own mouth for three and a half years is clearly shown through the Talmudists. For it is read in the *Midrash Tehillim* (that is, the exposition of the Psalms) that Rabbi Johanan said: <note>original Hebrew: שלש שנים ומחצה היתה שכינה עומדת בהר הזיתים ורשו אומר את יהוה בהמצאו קראוהו בהיותו קרוב</note> "For three years and a half the Divine Presence <note>The *Shekhinah*, or the manifest presence of God.</note> stood upon the Mount of Olives, crying out and saying: Seek

<margin>
The Messiah taught for three years and a half.
</margin>

<column-break/>

the Lord while he may be found, call upon him while he is near." This is also confirmed in the *Bereshit Rabba* (that is, the exposition of the book of Genesis), where Rabbi Moses Hadarsan speaks thus: "What did Solomon mean to say in the Song of Songs when he said, 'We will exult and rejoice in thee'?" <note>original Hebrew: אימתי אנו שמחים כשעמדו רגלי שכינה על הר הזיתים</note> "When shall we rejoice? When the feet of God stand upon the Mount of Olives." These are the words of Rabbi Johanan, son of Zakkai. From these things it manifestly appears that these three years and a half are those in which, according to the word of the Angel, the Messiah was to confirm his law through himself by deed, word, and miracles. It is certain that it happened exactly in this way. For the Savior himself, at thirty years of age, received baptism, and from then until his passion, nearly three and a half years passed. In this time, traveling through Galilee and Judea, and frequently staying and teaching upon the Mount of Olives, he confirmed his law by deed and word. Rightly, therefore, did the Angel place this week—in which these and many other divine works were to occur—in the final position as the completion of all things. And because in the middle of this most recent week the Messiah was to undergo death by divine decree, through which all the sacrifices of the Old Law were to have an end (because they prefigured that true sacrifice which the Messiah himself was to make by offering his most holy body to the Father on the altar of the cross for the remission of the sins of the human race), the Angel therefore added: "And in the middle of the week he shall cause the sacrifice" (referring to animal sacrifices) "and the offering" (meaning all other things offered in the temple) "to fail," all of which were destined to cease in their significance at the death of the Messiah. As a sign of this, at the very hour of Christ’s death, the veil of the temple was torn from top to bottom, and all the miracles that used to happen in the temple came to an end, as we have argued abundantly above. Finally, concluding, he says: "And upon the abominations," that is, because of the abominations committed against the Messiah, "there shall be desolation. And it shall persevere until the consummation and the pre-determined end," namely, desolation upon desolation. From this it is clear that the Jews are never to return to Jerusalem from this most recent captivity, unless perhaps after the war of the Antichrist, when they have received the faith of Christ. Therefore, reducing all that we have said at great length in the five preceding chapters regarding this prophecy of Daniel into a logical form, we finally conclude: Since the Angel Gabriel told Daniel that from the going out of the word concerning the people’s return until the principal Messiah there would be 7 and 62 weeks, and this number was completed 40 years before the burning of the second temple; and since no one besides the Lord Jesus existed then or has since appeared who possessed the signs of the principal and true Messiah (as is even conceded by our adversaries), and who was killed after those 7 and 62 weeks after both teaching and performing works possible only for God—it necessarily follows, for all who are not devoid of reason, that he was truly the principal and true Messiah.

<margin>A</margin> *For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee.* <note>original Hebrew: "Asher nishbati me-avor mei Noach..." from Isaiah 54:9</note> That is to say: "Just as the days of Noah are to me, so I have sworn that the waters of Noah shall no longer pass over the earth: thus I have sworn that I shall not be angry with you, nor shall I rebuke you." ### CAPNIO.

All these things you have said are excellent indeed, and of such a nature that they can by no means be denied by the Jews of our time. I cannot understand these things unless you explain them.

The Hebrews have a double form for the letter *mem*. One is the "open" form, characterized as מ, which is never placed at the end of a word, but always at the beginning or in the middle. The other is the "closed" form, which they shape as ם, and they are accustomed to writing it only at the end of a word. In this word *lemarbe*, since the letter is in the middle, it ought to be open and not closed; yet, contrary to custom, it is placed there as a closed letter. This is truly found nowhere else. Therefore, one must by no means believe that this was done without a mystery. For as it is said in the book *Sabbath* <note>Tractate Shabbat, a volume of the Talmud concerning the Sabbath</note>, in the chapter *Habbone* <note>The chapter "The Builder"</note>: "An open and a closed [letter] signifies a closed word or a closed thing," <margin>E</margin> <gloss>original Hebrew: "Petuch u-stum davar stum remez"</gloss> which is to say, it signifies something hidden. For Isaiah himself wished this to be understood by the wise, but to remain hidden from the wicked. Nevertheless, as the ancient Jews, enlightened by the Holy Spirit, have said, many secrets are designated by the closed *mem* in this place. Chief among them, as we shall prove elsewhere, is that the Messiah himself was to be born from a "closed" virgin—who was to be called Mary—beyond the common manner of birth and beyond the order of nature. Now, however, we shall show that the appointed time of the Messiah's coming is signified by that very closed *mem*. Because this type of closed *mem* designates the number six hundred among the Jews, it shows without a doubt that from the time of this prophecy un-

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin>til the birth of the Messiah, there were to be six hundred years. This was later proven by the event itself. This is demonstrated as follows: for that prophecy came forth from the mouth of Isaiah at the same time the Prophet prophesied, saying: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive," along with the rest. For both of these prophecies are in one and the same context. This prophecy was made in the fourth year of the reign of King Ahaz, as Rabbi Solomon says. He proves this in his commentary on the Fourth Book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Kings in modern Bibles</note>, chapter 15: "When it is written," he says, "in the twentieth year of Jotham <margin>B</margin> son of Uzziah, it should have said in the fourth year of Ahaz. For as it is said in 2 Kings 15, Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years. Thus says Rabbi Solomon. That six hundred years passed from the going forth of this prophecy until the <margin>C</margin> birth of Christ is shown in this way: If Ahaz reigned for 16 years (as held in 2 Kings 15), and this prophecy was made in the 4th year of his reign (as Rabbi Solomon says), it follows that after this prophecy, Ahaz himself reigned for 12 years. Amon reigned for two years, as said in 2 Kings chapter 21. <margin>D</margin> Josiah reigned for thirty-one years, as is clear from 2 Kings 21. Jehoahaz reigned for three months, as reported in 2 Kings 22. Jehoiakim reigned for eleven years, as gathered from 2 Kings chapter 23. Jehoiachin reigned for three months, as held in the same place. When these are added to the aforementioned 151 and a half years, there are 675 and a half years from the fourth year of King Ahaz until the destruction <margin>F</margin> of the second temple. If forty-two years are taken from these (which passed from the Passion of Christ until the overturning of the city of Jerusalem and the temple), and nearly 33 and a half years in which Christ himself lived among men, there will be found from that time in which Isaiah <margin>G</margin> prophesied concerning the conception and birth of the Messiah until the birth of Christ himself, precisely six hundred years, which the aforementioned closed *mem* designates. To prove this, a saying of the same Prophet in the fifty-fourth chapter is very much to the purpose: *For this is as the waters of Noah unto me...* <note>Galatinus begins to link the 600 years of the prophecy to the 600 years of Noah's life at the time of the flood</note>

# BOOK FOUR.

<margin>A</margin>"For this is like the waters of Noah to me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so have I sworn that I would not be angry with you, nor rebuke you." <note>original Hebrew: Asher nishbati me-avor mei Noach... from Isaiah 54:9</note> That is to say: "Just as the days of Noah are to me, for I swore the waters of Noah would no longer pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you nor rebuke you." Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the purported author of the Aramaic Targum</note> translates this into Aramaic <note>referred to here as Chaldean</note> as follows: "For as the days of Noah this is before me, when I established in my word that the waters of the flood which were in the days of Noah should no more pass over the earth, so I have established in my word that my fury shall not descend upon you." <note>original Aramaic: ari k'yomei Noach da kodami...</note>

In this matter, one must observe with great diligence of mind that, according to the exposition of Rabbi Nachman in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helec*, the "days of Noah" are to be referred to the "days of the Messiah." Therefore, when the Prophet says, "This is like the days of Noah to me," the pronoun "this" must refer to what he said in the preceding passages—namely, to everything the Prophet said from the fifty-second chapter, beginning with <margin>Isaiah 53</margin> "Behold, my servant shall understand," up to this point. Almost all of that section is accepted by the ancient Jews as being spoken about the Messiah. For those words of the chapter—"Behold, my servant shall understand"—Rabbi Jonathan translated and explained in Aramaic as: "Behold, my servant the Messiah shall prosper." <note>original Aramaic: Ha yitzlach avdi Meshicha</note> Rabbi Solomon <note>the famous commentator Rashi</note> also testifies to this when, explaining this passage, he says quite aptly: "Our masters affirm these things are said of the Messiah."

Now, when the flood ceased, the days of Noah had reached six hundred years. From the time Isaiah uttered this word until the coming of the Messiah, there were to be six hundred years. All of this is perfectly proven through the Hebrew scriptures. That Noah was six hundred years old when the flood ended is clear first from what is said in *Beresith Rabba* <note>Genesis Rabbah, a collection of ancient interpretations of Genesis</note> regarding the verse: "Noah was a son of six hundred years when the flood of waters was upon the earth." There, Rabbi Nehumia says: "The year of the flood is an ascending year in the count," that is, it is part of the count including intercalations and calculations.

Furthermore, the same thing is shown by what is written in the ninth chapter of Genesis: "And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years. And all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died." <note>original Hebrew: Vayechi Noach achar ha-mabul...</note> If all the days of Noah's life were nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood, it necessarily follows that the year of the flood itself was the last of the aforementioned six hundred. Thus, it is clearly shown that the "days of Noah" at the end of the flood were six hundred years.

That there were also exactly as many years from the time Isaiah spoke those words until the coming of the Messiah has been clearly shown by what was said in the explanation of the "closed mem" <note>The Hebrew letter 'm' normally written at the end of a word, but found here in the middle of 'lemarbe' in Isaiah 9:7</note> placed in the word *Lemarbe* <note>למרבה - 'to the increase'</note>. For Isaiah (as was shown) began to prophesy about the conception and birth of the Messiah at the end of the fourth year or the beginning of the fifth year of the reign of Ahaz, saying, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son," and so on. From that time until the birth of Christ (as was proven in that same place), exactly six hundred years passed. And just as many years—as we have shown—marked the days of Noah when the flood ceased. Therefore, it must be conceded that the Messiah has already come, and that he was our Lord Jesus (since no one else has been born who fits the description of the Messiah given by the Prophets).

### CAPNIO.

<note>Capnio is the character representing Johannes Reuchlin, the famous 16th-century Hebraist.</note> Although in the preceding sections you have abundantly proven that the Messiah has already come according to the interpretations of the Hebrews—using the specific time determined by the Prophets—it would nevertheless be very useful if you could show this even more clearly. ### GALATINUS.

I will gladly do this as well. First, I will bring forward what is written in the book <margin>Tradition of the disciples of Elijah.</margin> *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helec*: "The tradition of the house of Elijah: The world is to exist for six thousand years, and then it shall be destroyed. Before I say more to prove this, I will provide Rabbi Solomon’s <note>Rashi's</note> gloss, which explains those same words thus: "The world shall be for six thousand years," meaning it will endure only that long. Of these, two thousand were "emptiness." Scripture teaches us how there were two thousand years from Adam until the fifty-second year of Abraham. After these two thousand years were completed, Abraham applied himself to the Law; as it is written in the twelfth chapter of Genesis: "And the souls they had made in Haran," which they interpreted as, "And the souls they had made with the Law in Haran." The masters said, in the book *Hauoda zara* <note>Avodah Zarah, a Talmudic tractate</note>, that at that time Abraham was fifty-two years old.

The two thousand years of the Law until the coming of the Messiah are reckoned in this way: there were forty-eight years until Isaac was born. Then sixty years from the birth of Isaac until the birth of Jacob, which makes one hundred and eight years. Next, the one hundred and thirty years of Jacob’s life when he entered Egypt. This makes two hundred and thirty-eight years. Then two hundred and ten years during which the children of Israel stayed in Egypt. This makes 448 years. ### BOOK FOUR.

...the first holy house <note>The First Temple of Solomon</note> was built, four hundred and eighty years passed, as it is written in the last book of Kings in the sixth chapter: "And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year," and so forth, "and the house of the Lord was built." Therefore, one hundred and seventy-two years before the completion of four thousand years from the beginning of the world, the house of God was destroyed. And at the end of the aforementioned 172 years, the two thousand years of the Law were completed. Yet the Law was not to be abolished then, as my Master used to say. It follows: "And two thousand years are the days of the Messiah." For after the two thousand years of the Law, his judgment shall be that the Messiah should come, and the wicked Kingdom—that is, the Kingdom of the Romans—should be abolished. Thus far the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator</note>. Although he erred not a little in the computation of years, even according to the Talmudists (as is easily evident through what has been said previously), it nevertheless follows necessarily from his words that the Messiah has already come. For if, according to his exposition of the opinion or tradition of Elijah and his disciples, the Messiah was to come at the end of four thousand years of the world, and according to the Jewish computation from the beginning of the world until the present year (which is the year of Christ 1516), five thousand two hundred and seventy-six years have passed—though according to ours, many more, as will be proven a little further down—it is certainly concluded by necessity that the coming of the Messiah has already passed by one thousand two hundred and seventy-two years according to them.

<margin>Objection of the younger Jews.</margin>
**Cap.** The younger Jews <note>The author uses "younger" or "recent" Jews to refer to contemporary Jewish scholars who differ from the "ancient" authorities he respects</note> indeed confess that according to this Talmudic tradition, the Messiah was to come at the end of the fourth millennium, but they say that because of their sins, he has not yet come. This they strive to prove by the same tradition, because at the end of that same tradition, it follows immediately: "But because of our sins, which have increased, there have gone out from them those that have gone out" <note>original Hebrew: be-avonotenu she-rabu yatz'u me-hem mah she-yatz'u</note>. This means: "On account of our sins, however, which have increased, there have departed from them—namely, from the years—those which have departed." Where the gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: "Truly, on account of our sins which have multiplied, the Messiah did not come at the end of four thousand years."

**Gal.** They are plainly lying. Therefore, so that they may be convicted of lying, we give them a double response. And first, indeed, we say that these words are not part of the same tradition, since they belonged neither to Elijah nor to his disciples. This can be made sufficiently clear from the nature of the words themselves; rather, those very words were added to the tradition by someone wishing to protect Jewish faithlessness. The greatest evidence of this is that in the book *Avodah Zarah* <note>term: Avodah Zarah: A tractate of the Talmud concerning "strange worship" or idolatry</note>, where this same tradition is placed, this kind of "tail" is not inserted into the tradition in exactly the same words. For there, in the chapter *Lifnei Eidehen* <note>term: Lifnei Eidehen: "Before their festivals," the first chapter of Avodah Zarah</note>, it reads: "The house of Elijah taught: The world is to exist for six thousand years. Two thousand of these are of vanity or emptiness, two thousand are of the Law, and two thousand are the days of the Messiah. But because of our sins, which have multiplied, there have departed from them seven hundred and fourteen." This is the tradition word for word. Therefore, it is clear in itself that these last words, by which the more recent Jews try to veil their faithlessness, are not the same here and there, but are far different. For there, no certain time is set, but here, a certain number of years which had already passed is added. This is an effective argument for Jewish falsehood. Next, we object to them that the coming of the Messiah could indeed be accelerated, but by no means delayed. This is excellently proven in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helek*, where it reads: "Rabbi Alexandri said, Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: It is written in the sixtieth chapter of Isaiah (concerning the salvation that was to come through the Messiah's arrival): 'I the Lord in its time will hasten it.'" <note>original Hebrew: Ani YHVH be-itah achishenah, from Isaiah 60:22</note> If they merit it, I will hasten it; if they do not merit it, in its time—supply "I will bring it to pass." From these things, the Jews say that the Messiah's coming could by no means be delayed so as not to occur in its time, but it could well have been accelerated, provided there were those who merited it. Likewise, upon the same words of Isaiah, "I the Lord in its time will hasten it," the *Perush* <note>term: Perush: A commentary or explanation</note>—that is, the gloss—says: "If they are good, before its time; and if not, in its time." <note>original Hebrew: im yihyu tovim lifnei zmano ve-im lo be-zmano</note> But that gloss, according to the Teachers of the Hebrews, speaks of the salvation to be wrought by the Messiah. Therefore, if the Jews were good, on account of their goodness God ought to have accelerated the coming of the Messiah. If, however, they were evil on account of their sins, He ought not to have neglected to send him at his determined time. Wherefore, the Jews must necessarily concede that, their sins notwithstanding, he has already come at least at the determined time.

**Cap.** Still, Jewish perversity objects that if the Messiah was to come at the end of the world’s four thousand years, we can by no means infer from this that our Lord Jesus was the true Messiah, since these four thousand years were completed—according to Rabbi Solomon—172 years after the destruction of the last Temple, or according to others, 136 years; as can be gathered from the calculation of times which you made a little earlier through the scriptures of the Hebrews. Yet the Lord Jesus suffered in the forty-second year before the destruction of the same Temple.

**Gal.** This flight of theirs can help them not at all. First, because as we have just said, while the coming of the Messiah could not be delayed, it could and should have been accelerated, provided there were those who merited it. Wherefore we can say, not incongruously, that many things merited the acceleration of the Messiah's coming: namely, the pitiable captivity of the holy Fathers existing in hell <note>Refers to the "Limbus Patrum," where the righteous of the Old Testament waited for Christ</note>, and the already foreseen goodness of the Apostles and other disciples of Christ. But most especially the holiness and humility of the Virgin Mary, as well as the most holy and singular...

**children of Israel** <note>original: "בני ישראל"</note> **Therefore he will give them up until the time that she who is in labor has given birth. Since, therefore, the Messiah was supposed to come when the Romans had ruled over the Jews and the whole world for nine months, and since the Romans ruled both the Jews and the entire world most significantly in the times of Caesar Augustus—under whom Christ was born—it is manifest and certain that the Messiah came then. Since, then, no one else (to conclude everything stated previously) appeared at the end of the world’s fourth millennium, or was born under Caesar Augustus, who possessed the signs of the true Messiah, and to whom the oracles of the Prophets—especially those determining His arrival and describing Him and His deeds—rightly apply, it necessarily follows for all those not blinded by treachery or hatred that the Lord Jesus was undoubtedly the true Messiah.

### CHAPTER XXI.

> *Regarding two false Messiahs whom the Jews received after the Passion of Christ, because the pre-appointed time for the Messiah’s coming had passed. And for what reason they were so severely punished, first by Vespasian and Titus, and later by Hadrian.*

### CAPNIO.

<margin>1</margin>
**FOR THIS** reason, I believe, the Jews received two false Messiahs, one after another, following the Passion of Christ: because they saw that the determined time for the Messiah's arrival, handed down both by the Prophets and by the ancient Talmudists, had already passed. Therefore, you will provide no small benefit if you reveal to everyone the wicked path by which they went astray after our Savior’s ascension, by recounting how they received those false Messiahs. For **Bar** <note>original: "בר"</note> is a Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note> name, and **Ben** <note>original: "בן"</note> is Hebrew; both mean the same as "son" among us. **Kozba** <note>original: "כוזיבא"</note>, however, is interpreted as a "lie." Therefore, *Bar-Kozba* or *Ben-Kozba* is exactly the same as 
<margin>*Bar (the son of) the false Messiah received by the Jews.*</margin>
"son of a lie" or "son of falsehood." This man, thrusting himself forward as the Messiah, was accepted by the Jews; as is read in the book...

### BOOK FOUR.

In the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter titled *Helec* <note>Referring to "Perek Chelek," the eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, which discusses the afterlife and the Messiah.</note>, it is said of him among other things: *Barcozba* <note>Simon bar Kokhba, leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–135 AD).</note> reigned for thirty and a half years <note>Though historical accounts usually cite three and a half years, the text here records "30. cum dimidio."</note>. For he said **to the Rabbis** <gloss>original: "לברבנן Lerabbanan"</gloss>, **"I am the Messiah"** <gloss>original: "אנא משיחא Ana Messia"</gloss>. And according to the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> in that same place, this coincided with the reign of Herod Agrippa. Therefore, that word of the Lord spoken in the 5th chapter of John was then fulfilled: *I have come in my Father's name, and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.* Thus *Barcozba*, the "son of a lie" <note>The author uses a common pun: while "Bar Kokhba" means "Son of a Star," his detractors called him "Bar Koziba," meaning "Son of a Lie."</note>, came in his own name and was received by them. Indeed, they certainly ought to have recognized him by his very name (had they possessed any sense). For it was not only the common people who received him, but also the greatest part of their wise men. Among these was Rabbi Akiba, who was considered one of the wisest of the Talmud. Nor did they seek any sign to be performed by this false Messiah, just as they both sought and saw from Christ, as is read most extensively in their own scriptures.

For Rabbi **Moses ben Maimon** <gloss>original: "בן מימון," meaning the son of Maimon, also known as Maimonides.</gloss> records the following in his rulings on Kings: "Rabbi Akiba was a wise man, and indeed one of the wisest of the Talmud. He himself bore the arms of King *Barcozba* and said that he was the Messiah. For he judged him to be so, and all the wise men of his generation thought he was the Messiah, until he was killed because of his crimes. And the wise men did not ask him for a sign or a miracle." These are the words of that Rabbi Moses. Therefore, Rabbi Akiba, in order to suggest to the people that this *Ben-cozba* was the Messiah, interpreted the sayings of the Prophets regarding him, especially that saying from the 2nd chapter of Haggai: *Yet once more, in a little while, and I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land, and I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come.* This is found in the book *Sanhedrin*, chapter *Helec*. But while this Rabbi Akiba did very well to interpret those words of the Prophet Haggai as referring to the days of the Messiah—since they can be more fittingly applied to no one else—he acted most wickedly in referring them to the false Messiah *Ben-cozba*. Thus, through the persuasions of this man and the other teachers, the Jews received the aforementioned false Messiah and revolted against the Roman Empire. 

<margin>Why Vespasian and Titus came against the Jews.</margin> On account of this, Vespasian was sent against them with his son Titus. Just as they had denied the Son of God along with the Father, saying, "We have no king but Caesar," so they were deservedly delivered to a father and son—namely, Vespasian and Titus—to be exterminated. These men, during the Feast of Unleavened Bread <note>Passover.</note>—the very time when those faithless Jews perpetrated the death of Christ—hemmed in the almost innumerable crowds of people who had gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate that feast. And just as they had despised the grace of God during the three and a half years in which the Savior of the world had taught, so for three and a half years those Roman Princes afflicted them with a most cruel and harsh siege.

<margin>The death of the aforementioned false Messiah.</margin> And when they were first being besieged, they asked for a sign of their liberation from *Ben-cozba*, their false Messiah, for whose sake they had risen up against the Romans. Finally, seeing that he could perform no miracle for their liberation, they delivered him to death. Concerning his death, it is read in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helec*,

that the Rabbis finally said to him: "It is written in the 11th chapter of *Isaiah* concerning the Messiah, *That he shall be of quick understanding and judging* <note>Based on a traditional interpretation of Isaiah 11:3, where the Hebrew word for "smell" or "breath" is linked to intuitive judgment.</note>; that is, he shall perceive by scent who is innocent and who is guilty. Let us see, therefore, if you are able to judge by scent." When they saw that he could not judge by scent, they killed him. This is from the Talmud. When they were finally captured—with God undoubtedly disposing it—they were measured with the same measure by which they had measured Christ. 

As is contained more extensively among them in the book of the exposition of the Lamentations of Jeremiah, which is called **Echa Rabbethi** <gloss>original: "איכה רבתי"</gloss>, where it is written concerning that passage in the first chapter: **Her adversaries have become the head, her enemies prosper.** <note>original: "היו צריה לראש אויביה שלו"</note> Among other things, it is read: *Her adversaries have become the head*—this is Caesar Vespasian; *Her enemies prosper*—this is the wicked Titus, his son. Others, he says, were reserved for sport, in addition to the two hundred thousand who were led into captivity. Such great worthlessness is said to have existed among the people that a person could buy thirty Jews for a single silver coin. No one can doubt that this was done by the will of God; so that they who sold their God and Lord as a cheap slave for a low price, were themselves sold at an even lower price. 

Indeed, while Vespasian was pressing the Jews hard with the siege, he so pleased the Romans (through God's working) that upon the death of Otho, they chose him as Emperor in his absence by common consent. Therefore, leaving his son Titus at the same siege, he returned to Rome. Titus, however, on the fifth day before the Ides of July <note>July 11th.</note>, having captured and leveled the city and the temple to the ground, and having established peace with those who remained in Judea, decreed that no Jew should henceforth observe the Sabbath, nor should any woman abstain during her menstruation; as is abundantly contained in the Talmud, in that book called **Meghilla** <gloss>original: "מגילה"</gloss>, which means "History" <note>The tractate Megillah specifically deals with the Scroll of Esther, but the author uses it here for historical context regarding Roman decrees.</note>.

Thus, even Rabbi Akiba himself, despite having been shamefully deluded by the aforementioned false Messiah in Jerusalem, did not shrink from imprudently receiving this one; rather, he attempted to persuade the people through the authority of Holy Scripture that he was the true Messiah.
