### CHAPTER XXII.

*The fifth reason, by which it is shown that the time of the first coming of the Messiah has already passed, based on the punishment of the Israelite people. Also, that the Jews, at the coming of the Messiah, were to be fined with a manifold penalty because of the death they intended to inflict upon him.*

### CAPNIO <note>The scholar Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), known by his Greek-derived name "Capnio."</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial V featuring a floral and scrollwork design.</image-desc>THERE can be no argument against Jewish **perfidy** <term>perfidia — in this context, the historical Christian term for Jewish refusal to accept Jesus</term> as effective as proving through their own scriptures that this most recent captivity in which they find themselves happened to them as a punishment for the death of Christ. For that reason, it would be quite appropriate now to prove that those slaughters which were committed against them—both by **Vespasian and Titus**, and later by **Hadrian**—as well as the wretched calamities by which they are dispersed throughout the world and never cease to be more cruelly afflicted day by day, were suffered because of the death of the Messiah, which they were to carry out so unjustly and cruelly. **Gal.** <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), the author of the work.</note> All these things were foretold by the Prophets long ago. For that the Jews, at the first coming of the Messiah, were to be punished with many penalties and many scourges because of the death they would inflict on him, was not only revealed by the Angel to Daniel—as was said above in the exposition of the **seventy weeks**—but many of the Prophets also predicted it. Especially **Isaiah** says this in his 28th chapter:

<note>original Hebrew: "כי אמרתם כרתנו ברית את מות ועם שאול עשינו חוזה..."</note>
"Because you have said: We have entered into a league with death, and we have made a covenant with hell. When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come upon us: for we have placed our hope in lies, and by falsehood we are protected. Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will lay a stone in the foundations of Zion, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a foundation of foundations. He that believes, let him not hasten. And I will set judgment in weight, and justice in measure: and hail shall overturn the hope of lies: and waters shall overwhelm the protection: and your league with death shall be abolished..."

<column-break/>

"...and your covenant with hell shall not stand. When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, you shall be trodden down by it. Whenever it passes through, it shall take you away: because in the morning, early in the morning, it shall pass through, by day and by night, and there shall be nothing but commotion and trembling to understand the report. For the bed is narrowed, so that one falls out, and a short covering cannot cover both. For as in the mountain of divisions, the Lord shall rise up; as in the valley which is in Gibeon, he shall be angry: that he may do his work—his work is strange; that he may perform his work—his work is foreign. And now, do not mock, lest perhaps your scourges be made stronger. For I have heard from the Lord the God of hosts a final destruction upon all the earth." <note>Isaiah 28:14-22</note> And so forth, until the end of the twenty-ninth chapter. Concerning this prophecy, whatever the younger Jews may say—excepting **Rabbi Solomon** <term>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator</term>—they all wander in delusion, since it can rightly be applied to nothing but our Lord Jesus. For although the rest of the prophecy is easily revealed of itself through those words: *Behold, I will lay a stone in Zion, a strong stone, a corner stone, precious, a foundation of foundations*, nevertheless, **Rabbi David** <term>Radak (David Kimchi, 1160–1235)</term>—as one who does not care if he perverts all prophecies from their true sense as long as he avoids the mystery and truth of Christ—attributes this part to **King Hezekiah**, saying: *Behold I will lay a stone in Zion*, that is, a good king, namely Hezekiah, whom he likened to a strong stone placed as a corner foundation; by whose hands the people shall be delivered from the enemy, because he will lead the people back to good and destroy the impious and the wicked. 

<margin>
The false exposition of Rabbi David.
</margin>

<margin>
Refutation.
</margin>

He also adapts and explains that clause, *He that believes, let him not hasten*, in this way: "Since," he says, "the greater part of them in the days of **Ahaz** did not give credit to the words of the Prophet, he therefore wished to use these words; as if he were to say: If there is anyone among you who desires to see this prophecy verified, let him not hasten, that is, let him not think it will come so soon, even if he sees it entirely fulfilled." These are the words of that treacherous Rabbi David. The falsehood of his exposition clearly appears from the progression of the prophecy itself: for it is gathered from it that the Jews were to suffer innumerable evils through this king. Yet through Hezekiah, as he himself asserts, it happened that they suffered no evils, but were even liberated from the enemy **Sennacherib**. For which reason, it can by no means be said that this prophecy speaks of Hezekiah himself. Furthermore, when he says that clause, *He that believes, let him not hasten*, meant the prophecy would not be verified soon, he seems to openly contradict himself. For if it was spoken in the days of Ahaz (as he says), and Hezekiah himself succeeded immediately after, was it not to be fulfilled soon enough? It is certain, therefore, that this part of the prophecy must necessarily be understood not of Hezekiah, but of the Messiah. This is first clearly evident through the **Targum of Rabbi Jonathan** <term>An ancient Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Prophets</term>, who translated and explained this place in Aramaic as follows: 

<note>original Aramaic: "אמר יהוה אלהים הא אנא ממני בציון מלכא משיחא מלכא תקיף וגיבר"</note>
That is: "The Lord God said, Behold, I appoint in Zion the **King Messiah**, a King powerful, robust, and strong." Furthermore, it is evident through **Rabbi Solomon**, who explained the prophecy itself as referring to the Messiah...

# BOOK FOUR

<center>...continuing, he says: "Behold, it is I who have founded in Zion"—that is, in my mind I have decreed—"to establish the Messiah as king, who shall be a strong stone, the foundation of foundations." Thus, "he who believes" that this prophecy will come to pass "shall not hasten"—that is, he should not long for his arrival <note>The author is interpreting "not hastening" as a warning that the Messiah's coming would bring judgment rather than immediate earthly glory for the Jews.</note>. So he says. With this exposition standing, we see without a doubt that this prophecy foretold that this final destruction of the Jews would follow from the coming of the Messiah. Therefore, the prophecy itself cannot be verified concerning the Messiah whom the Jews falsely expect to come, since they hope to receive infinite blessings from him. However, so that the perversity of **Rabbi David** <note>David Kimchi (1160–1235), known as Radak, a famous Jewish commentator.</note> and other more recent writers—who strive to subvert this prophecy—may be seen more clearly, their opinions will be recited and refuted here and there in the true exposition of the prophecy itself, which I will now undertake.

<margin>The true and Catholic exposition of this prophecy.</margin>
I say, therefore, that through this prophecy, the entire mystery of Jesus Christ was narrated in summary. For when the Prophet rebuked the wicked works of the Jews living in the time of **Ahaz**, wishing to preach this mystery to them, he spoke to show them that their successors, following their way of life, would eventually reach this end. He said: "Hear the word of the Lord, you scoffers, who rule this people in Jerusalem. Because you have said: We have struck a covenant with death, and with the grave we have made peace." This means: because you are the cause of evil for others, refusing to keep God's commands or obey the warnings of his Prophets, saying "We have struck a covenant with death... so that we care for no one," therefore thus says the Lord God: "Behold, I will found in Zion a stone," that is, the King Messiah (as **Rabbi Jonathan** <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, to whom the Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Prophets is attributed.</note> explains from the ancients, and **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Solomon ben Isaac (1040–1105), known as Rashi, the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> from the more recent ones). This Messiah will indeed be a cornerstone, precious, and the "foundation of the foundation"—that is, the foundation of all foundations. "He who believes shall not hasten": that is, according to the gloss of the same **Rabbi Solomon**, he who believes this prophecy is to come will not hasten—that is, he will not desire his arrival. This means that whoever among the Jews believes the Messiah is coming, understanding the evils that will arise over them at his arrival, will not desire to hasten his coming, but rather will ask God to delay it. The Prophet immediately enumerates these evils, saying: "And I will place judgment in measure, and justice in weight," along with the rest that follows. He says these things to denote that the boundary of their salvation or damnation was to be set then, in such a way that the hope of a lie would deceive them. For at the coming of the Messiah, retribution—either grace or punishment—was to be rendered to each according to their merits. And since the Prophet saw that they would, for the greater part, turn toward the worse, he wished to assign the cause of the evils they were to suffer (which was to be none other than the death of the Messiah) before coming to the description of those evils. Thus he added: "And your covenant with death shall be abolished, and your peace with the grave shall not stand." It is as if he were saying: The covenant which I entered into with your fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and their seed, will be abolished and dissolved by the death (specifically the death of the Messiah) which will be perpetrated by you. For by the death which you yourselves will inflict upon the Messiah, you make that covenant void.

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin>
In a similar way, your peace, which I promised to you, will not stand with the grave—namely, the grave of that same Messiah. For because of this, you will suffer infinite calamities, and war will be waged against you continually. The truth of this exposition is greatly confirmed by the fact that if the prophecy were explained otherwise, it could not be fitted together so well without many inconsistencies and contradictions following. Moreover, he used this manner of speaking to show that they had in some way prophesied this mystery
<margin>B</margin>
by their own words. It is as if he were saying: "Since you said, 'We have struck a covenant with death, and with the grave we have made peace,' etc., therefore I say you have spoken correctly. For thus says the Lord God: 'Behold, I will found in Zion a stone,' that is, I will establish the Messiah, through whom your words will be verified. For because of him, you will suffer all evils and the scourges which you said could not come upon you, and infinite others besides." Therefore he immediately added: "When the overflowing
<margin>C</margin>
scourge passes through, you shall be trodden down by it," along with the other things that follow. The truth of this exposition is most evident from what is said: "As on the mountain of divisions the Lord shall rise up; as in the valley which is in Gibeon he shall be angry, that he may do his work—his work is strange; that he may perform his deed—his deed is foreign." From these words it is clearly gathered that (as **Rabbi David** testifies from his father's opinion) that work which he was going to do against Israel is called "strange" and "foreign" to
<margin>D</margin>
God because God himself, by his own will, ought not to have come to that, since his purpose tended mostly toward founding that stone for their good and not for their evil. But if the opposite effect followed, the cause is to be ascribed not to God, but to them. And lest they think these words were of no consequence (as he had rightly called them "scoffers"), he subsequently added: "Now therefore, do not mock, lest perhaps your bonds be made stronger. For I have heard from the Lord God of hosts a final destruction—namely,
<margin>E</margin>
yours—upon the whole earth." It is as if he were saying plainly: "Do not mock and ridicule my words to your greater punishment. For I confess and promise to you that I have heard of your final ruin from God for this reason—not only in Jerusalem or Judea, but in the whole earth." For the scourges will never allow you to rest, even when you are dispersed throughout the entire world. This agrees with that saying
<margin>F</margin>
of **Moses** in **Deuteronomy 28**: <note>original: "וּבַגּוֹיִם הָהֵם לֹא תַרְגִּיעַ וְלֹא־יִהְיֶה מָנוֹחַ לְכַף רַגְלֶךָ"</note> That is: "Among those nations also you shall not rest, nor shall there be rest for the sole of your foot." Through this prophecy, then, it is clear—both from what has been explained according to the Hebrew glosses and from the rest that is introduced up to the end of chapter 29—that the Jews, because of the death they were to inflict on the Messiah, were to be punished with a manifold penalty and dispersed through the world in a final destruction. Since, therefore, the Prophet spoke of this most recent captivity, which it is certain
<margin>G</margin>
happened to them because of the death of **Jesus of Nazareth**, it is necessarily concluded not only that the time of the Messiah’s coming has already passed, but also that Jesus of Nazareth himself was the true Messiah.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

*On the sins of the Jews committed during the time of the first and last temples. Also on the deaths of the Prophets Zechariah and Isaiah. And what was the cause of this most recent captivity of theirs. Regarding the* hatred for no reason <note>original: "odio gratis"</note> *with which they persecuted Christ.*

-> CAPNIO <-

The Jews of our age, utterly denying this, say that this most recent captivity happened to them not as a punishment for the death of Jesus of Nazareth, but because of the sins of their fathers.

GALATINUS. It is easy to convict them in this and show them to be speakers of falsehoods if their crimes perpetrated during the times of the first and last temple are considered. Therefore, I will first relate those things written in the Jerusalem Talmud, in the book *Yoma* <note>original: יומא - "The Day," referring to the Day of Atonement</note> (that is, of the Days), in the chapter *Seven Days* <note>original: שבעת ימים (Sabbat iamin)</note>. For there it is read that Rabbi Yohanan spoke thus: We find that Shiloh <note>A significant religious center for the Israelites before the Temple was built in Jerusalem.</note> (which is the proper name of a place near the Jordan river) was not destroyed except because they profaned the sanctuaries and despised the solemnities. And we find this occurred only because they worshipped idols, practiced sexual immorality <note>original: "reuelauerunt pudenda," literally "uncovered the shameful parts"</note>, and shed blood. In the second holy house, however, we know they were all laboring in the Law, taking care to observe the precepts and the tithes. Every custom and habit among them was good, except that they were lovers of money and hated one another with a hatred for no reason <note>original: "odio gratis," translating the Hebrew concept of "sinat chinam."</note>. Oh, how grave is hatred for no reason, which outweighs sexual immorality, idolatry, and the shedding of blood! It is said, moreover, that Rabbi Ezra, Rabbi Jacob, and Rav Huna were sitting and saying: What was first was rebuilt; but what was second has not been rebuilt. This is because those of the first period performed penance, but those of the second did not. Rabbi Eleazar said: The earlier ones performed penance, therefore their sin was revealed, and the end of their captivity was also revealed. The most recent ones did not perform penance; therefore, neither was their sin revealed, nor has the end of their captivity been revealed. He sought for them the testimony of their chosen house <note>The Temple.</note>. For the house itself proves this. For our fathers removed the roof from there, but we have torn out the walls from the foundations. As it is said in Psalm 137: *Raze it, raze it, down to its foundation* <note>original: ערו ערו עד היסוד בה (Ar’u ar’u ad ha-yesod bah)</note>. All this is from tradition. In the same book *Yoma*, in the chapter *Seven days before the Day of Atonement*, it is said: Why was the first Sanctuary destroyed? Because of three things that were there: idolatry, sexual immorality, and the shedding of blood.

<margin>
*The sins of the Jews of the first temple.*
*Idolatry.*
</margin>

I say there was idolatry there, as it is written in Isaiah 28: *The bed is too short for stretching out, and the covering is too narrow to wrap oneself in* <note>original: קצר המצע מהשתרע והמסכה צרה כהתכנס (Katzar ha-matza me-hishtarea...). Galatinus uses this to argue that the Temple "bed" could not accommodate both God and idols.</note>. Rabbi Jonathan said: The bed was narrowed,

<column-break/>

meaning that two companions could not stretch out there together. And the covering was shortened, so that it could not cover them. Do you make a short covering for Him of whom it is written in the thirty-third Psalm, "He gathers the waters of the sea as in a bottle"? And concerning them, it is also said in Ezekiel chapter 23: "Even their sons whom they bore to me, they roasted for them to eat." They did this to me; they polluted my sanctuary on that day. The Gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> says: "On the day in which they sacrificed their sons to idols." And this is also what is said in Jeremiah 7: "And they built the high places of *Tophet* <note>original: תופת</note> which are in the valley of the son of *Hinnom* <note>original: הנם (Gehenna)</note> to roast their sons and daughters in the fire. Which I did not command, nor did it enter my heart." There was also sexual immorality there, as was said in Isaiah chapter 3: "And the Lord said, because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with extended necks, and beckon with their eyes," and so on. Rabbi Joshua said: It was said of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin what was not even said of the Sodomites. For of the Sodomites it is written in Genesis chapter 18: "And their sin has become very heavy." But of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin it is written in Ezekiel chapter 9: "And he said to me, the sin of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great." Rabbi Tanhuma said: We have another scripture that says in Lamentations chapter 4: "The sin of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and no hands reached out to her." Where the Targum (that is, the Chaldean translation) says: "And no Prophets reached out to her to prophesy, who might lead her back through penance." Finally, there was the shedding of blood in the first sanctuary, as it is written in 2 Kings chapter 21: "And Manasseh shed very much innocent blood." And Jeremiah also says in chapter 2: "Your sword has devoured the Prophets like a destroying lion." The aforementioned tradition places all these things word for word, along with many other things relevant to the purpose. Concerning the shedding of the blood of the Prophets, we read in the book of 2 Kings: "They filled Jerusalem with the blood of the Prophets up to the mouth." And among the others, they killed Zechariah and Isaiah, the most holy Prophets of God, with a cruel death.

HOGSTRATUS. Tell me, I pray, in what manner did they kill these Prophets? For regarding Isaiah, I have often read that he was sawn in half. And I find it said by our Lord Jesus Christ in Matthew chapter 23 that Zechariah was killed between the temple and the altar. Nevertheless, I have not been able to find until now how Isaiah was sawn, nor how Zechariah was killed. For even if Jerome says much about this Zechariah, he does not assert who he was, but remains doubtful. If, therefore, you have found anything certain in the ancient books of the Jews concerning the death of either, please reveal it.

GALATINUS. I will, therefore, relate what I have found among the ancient Hebrews regarding the death of these Prophets. Concerning the death of Zechariah, I will say what I have read in various books, and especially in the Jerusalem Talmud in the book *Taanit* <note>original: תענית - "Fasting"</note> (that is, on Fasting). And in the commentary on the Lamentations of Jeremiah, regarding that which is said in the second chapter...

<margin>
*Sexual immorality.*
*Shedding of blood.*
*On the death of Zechariah.*
</margin>

# BOOK FOUR

The Lord has destroyed, and has not spared all the precious things of Jacob. And in the *Midrash Kohelet* <note>original: "Midras coheleth," a Rabbinic commentary on the book of Ecclesiastes</note>, that is, in the exposition of Ecclesiastes, regarding that passage in the 10th chapter, it is written: *If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you*, among other things. In all these places it is read as follows: It is written, *If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, do not leave your place*. This means: If dominion has been given to you from above, do not abandon the habit of your humility; so that you may be taught that everyone who abandons his humility brings death upon himself and sin upon his lineage. And from whom do you learn this? From Zechariah, of whom it is said in the 2nd book of Chronicles, chapter 24: *And the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest: and he stood above the people*. And what then? Was he walking above the heads of the people? No, but because he saw himself as greater than all the people. For he was the son-in-law of the King, and a Priest, and a Prophet, and a Judge. He therefore began to speak grand words, saying: *Thus says the Lord: Why do you transgress the commandments of the Lord? Therefore you shall not prosper: because you have forsaken the Lord, he also will forsake you*. For this reason, they immediately killed him; as it is said in 2nd Chronicles, chapter 24: *And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king, in the court of the house of the Lord*. However, they did not kill him in the court of Israel, nor in the court of the women, but in the court of the priests. And they did not observe in the case of his blood the ritual for the blood of a doe, nor the ritual for the blood of a deer. For regarding the deer and the doe, it is written in Leviticus chapter 17: *And he shall pour out its blood, and cover it with earth*. But regarding his blood, it is written in Ezekiel 24: *For her blood was in the midst of her; she set it upon the smoothest rock*. He did not pour it out upon the ground, so that it might be covered with earth. And why all this? To bring up indignation and to take vengeance, he placed the blood upon the smoothest stone, so that it would not be covered. Israel committed seven transgressions on that day. They killed a Priest, and a Prophet, and a legal Judge, and they shed innocent blood, and they polluted the court of the house of the Lord, and it was the Sabbath, and it was the Day of Atonement. Thus far the tradition. But regarding the death <margin>The death of Isaiah the Prophet.</margin> of Isaiah, in the book *Yevamot* <note>original: "ieuamoth," the Talmudic tractate dealing with levirate marriage</note>, that is, of Brothers-in-Law, in the chapter that begins *Hacholetz* <note>original: החולץ - "The one who removes the shoe"</note>, that is, "The Unshoeing," I found it written exactly thus: Rabba said, Manasseh, in judging Isaiah, passed judgment. This is how he killed him: for he said to him, "Moses your Master said concerning God in Exodus 33: *No man shall see me and live*; but you said in the 6th chapter: *I saw the Lord*. Likewise, Moses your Master said in Deuteronomy chapter 4: *What great nation is there that has gods approaching it, as the Lord our God is to all who call upon him?* But you said in the 55th chapter: *Seek the Lord while he may be found: call upon him while he is near*. Furthermore, Moses your Master said in Exodus chapter 23, in the person of God: *I will fulfill the number of your days*; but you said in 2nd Kings chapter 20: *And I will add fifteen years to your days*." Isaiah then said, "I know he is such a man that he will not listen if I say anything to him." Therefore, he invoked the name of the Lord, and was swallowed up by a certain cedar tree. They brought the cedar, therefore, and sawed him apart together with it. And when the saw reached his mouth, he gave up his soul; because he had said in the sixth chapter: *I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips*. These things are found there.

<column-break/>

CAPNIO. Proceed now with what remains to be said concerning the crimes of the Jews perpetrated during the time of the first temple. <margin>On the avarice and other crimes of the Jews of the first temple.</margin> GALATINUS. Concerning avarice, then, and the other innumerable crimes in which the Jews of the first temple were immersed, in *Eicha Rabbati* <note>original: "Echa rabbethi," the Midrashic commentary on Lamentations</note>, that is, in the exposition of the lamentation of Jeremiah, regarding that saying: *Your iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion*, it is said among other things: Rabbi Simon said, the terror of the seal of Ahasuerus in Media was better than the preaching of 60,000 Prophets who prophesied in the days of Elijah, namely, rebuking the avarice and other crimes of the Jews. For they cast away the law of God, according to that which is said in Isaiah chapter 5: *They have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel*. Because of this, the indignation of the Lord against the people was increased. They also gave nothing to the poor, but rather took away from them their own possessions; according to that said in Isaiah chapter 3: *The spoil of the poor is in your houses. What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the face of the poor?* And that they loved money too much is held in Jeremiah chapter 6, saying thus: *From the least of them even to the greatest, everyone is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even to the priest, everyone deals falsely*. And infinite other things concerning the crimes of the Jews of the first temple are found in the books of the Prophets. But lest I say more myself, I will bring forward Ezekiel, chapter 22, uttering these things concerning their outrages: *Behold, the princes of Israel, every one according to his power, have been in you to shed blood; they have despised father and mother in you; the stranger they have dealt with by oppression in your midst; the fatherless and the widow they have wronged in you; you have despised my holy things, and have profaned my sabbaths. Slanderers have been in you to shed blood; they have committed lewdness in your midst. A father’s nakedness has been uncovered in you; they have humbled her who was set apart for uncleanness in you; and every one has committed abomination with his neighbor’s wife. And every one has lewdly defiled his daughter-in-law. Every one also has humbled his sister, his father’s daughter, in you. They have taken bribes in you to shed blood. You have taken usury and increase; you have greedily gained of your neighbors by extortion, and have forgotten me, says the Lord God.* And after a few words: *The conspiracy of her prophets,* he says, *is in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing the prey. They have devoured souls; they have taken treasure and precious things; they have made many widows in her midst. Her priests have violated my law and profaned my holy things; they have put no difference between the holy and the profane, nor have they shown the difference between the unclean and the clean. Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain.* And again, after a few things interspersed, he says: *The people of the land have used oppression and committed robbery, and have vexed or afflicted the poor and needy, and they have oppressed the stranger without justice. And I sought for a man among them who should make up the wall, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it...*

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between Galatinus and Capnio, moving from the specific martyrdom of Zechariah to a broader comparison between the sins of the First Temple period and the Second Temple period. The author uses Rabbinic sources to argue that because the punishment for the Second Temple's destruction (the current long exile) is so much greater than the 70-year Babylonian captivity, the underlying sin must be proportionally greater—specifically, the rejection of Jesus as Messiah.</meta>

# BOOK FOUR

...would be lost, and I did not find it. All these things are recorded there, translated word for word from the Hebrew. Regarding the phrase *They have devoured the soul*, the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note> says: "Because they were receiving secret bribes, strengthening the hands of the wicked to kill, plunder, and strip away." Furthermore, regarding the phrase *That greed might be treasured up*, Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the reputed author of the Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Prophets.</note> translated and explained it thus in the Chaldean language <note>Referring to Aramaic.</note>: "That they might take riches greedily and deceitfully." From all these things it is clearly evident how manifold, how great, and how enormous were the crimes committed by the Jews at the time of the First Temple.

<margin>What was the cause of this most recent captivity.</margin>

For all these sins, they were punished with only 70 years in the Babylonian captivity. However, the Jews of the Second Temple, who did not commit so many or such great crimes (for as it is said in the book *Yoma* <note>A tractate of the Talmud; the name means "The Day," referring to the Day of Atonement.</note>, in the chapter titled *Seven Days*, they were diligent in the Law, in the commandments of God, and in works of mercy), have been punished by this longest and lasting captivity without mercy. Therefore, since before God—who is most just—the punishment must correspond to the sin, our modern Jews must necessarily assign another cause for this most recent captivity of theirs than the sins of their fathers. For if the earlier Jews, whose crimes were the cause of the First Temple's destruction, were (as has been said) idolaters of the highest degree, killers of prophets, despisers and rejecters of the divine law, full of lust, greed, hatred, and innumerable other crimes, and devoid of works of piety and other good actions (as has now been proven through their own scriptures); yet the later ones who lived during the time of the Second Temple were clearly neither idolaters, nor murderers of prophets, nor so lustful, nor so greedy, nor infected by such great crimes—on the contrary, they were most studious in the Law, endowed with virtues, and adorned with all good character, as their own scriptures attest—therefore, they must provide another cause for the overthrow of the Second Temple than the crimes of those later Jews. This is especially true since divine justice repays each according to his works, and this most recent captivity is almost infinite compared to the Babylonian one. For that one, on account of all the crimes of the earlier people, lasted only 70 years; but this one has lasted over 1460 years until now, nor does any sign of its end or completion yet appear. For this reason, they can rationally assign no other cause for it than the death of Jesus the Nazarene, the true Messiah, who was God and man. For if he had been a mere man, they would not have been struck with such a great and long-lasting punishment on account of his death. This, Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides (1138–1204), also known as Rambam.</note> openly confesses, saying in the book *Shofetim* <note>The "Book of Judges," part of Maimonides' code of law, the Mishneh Torah.</note>: *Jesus the Nazarene appeared to be the Messiah and was killed by the house of judgment, and he was the cause for Israel being destroyed by the sword.* <note>original Hebrew: "Yeshua ha-Notzri nir'ah Mashiach ve-neherag... ve-hayah sibah she-Yisrael neherag be-cherev."</note>

<margin>An objection of the younger Jews.</margin>

**CAPNIO.** Against these points, the Jews object, saying that the cause of this destruction and their most recent captivity was not the death of Jesus the Nazarene, but "hatred without cause" <note>term: *odium gratis* / *Sinat Chinam*. A rabbinic concept explaining the Temple's fall through internal strife.</note>—that is, hatred for no reason—which existed among them, and which outweighed all the aforementioned crimes of their ancestors. To prove this, they bring forward Talmudic authority. For in the book *Yoma*, that is, *The Days*—

<column-break/>

<page-num>274</page-num>

—in the chapter that begins: *Seven days before the Day of Atonement* <note>original Hebrew: "Shevat yamim lifnei Yom ha-Kippurim"</note>, it reads as follows among other things: "The Second Sanctuary, concerning which we are certain that they were diligent in the Law, the commandments, and in works of mercy—why was it destroyed? Because of hatred without cause <note>original Hebrew: "bishvil sinat chinam"</note>. This is to teach you that hatred without cause, which was among them, outweighs the three aforementioned crimes: which were idolatry, sexual immorality <note>literally: "revelation of shameful parts"</note>, and the shedding of blood."

<margin>Refutation.</margin>

**GALATINUS.** This objection of theirs certainly cannot help them. For hatred without cause existed among those earlier people as well, in which both the leaders and the common folk attacked one another and killed one another. For in the same book and the same chapter, it follows immediately: "And in the First Sanctuary, was there not hatred without cause? For behold, it is written in Ezekiel chapter 21: *They were delivered to the sword, my people.* Rabbi Eleazar said: 'These were the sons of Adam who ate and drank with one another, yet transfixed one another with the swords of their tongues.' And perhaps you will say: 'Was this also among the Princes of Israel?' Yes. For it is written (as cited above): *Cry and wail, son of man, because that which was in my people, the same is in all the Princes of Israel.*" Here the gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: "The same sword or blade that was in the people is now also in all its Princes." From these things it clearly appears that hatred without cause was also sharply present among the earlier Jews at the time of the First Temple.

<margin>The hatred without cause with which the Jews persecuted Christ.</margin>

Furthermore, no hatred without cause that is directed toward mere men can be compared with that hatred without cause with which the earlier Jews (as has been said) both stoned Zechariah the Prophet and sawed Isaiah in half—despite the miracle of the tree receiving him—and cruelly afflicted Jeremiah, and slew countless other Prophets of God with the sword. Therefore, it must be said that there was another "hatred without cause" among the later Jews, for which the last Temple was overthrown and the Jews were dispersed into this most recent captivity—a hatred that could outweigh both the aforementioned double hatred without cause and all the other crimes of the earlier people. Indeed, the severity of the vengeance argues for the severity of the offense. It is impossible (as has been made clear from the preceding) for there to have been any other such hatred without cause among the later Jews than that by which (as the previously mentioned tradition cited at the beginning of this chapter testifies) the most recent Jews persecuted and continue to persecute our Savior and his disciples "gratis"—that is, without cause. For the Messiah whom they killed was God and man. Therefore, the hatred with which they treated him without cause, and still treat him, deservedly outweighs all the hatreds and all the crimes of the earlier Jews. Since they refuse to repent for this, as long as they remain obstinate in their perfidy, God will never have mercy on them. Wherefore it is quite clear that what God brought forth through his Prophet (as Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an Early Church Father known for his preaching.</note> attests) has been fulfilled, when he said in Psalm 35: *Let not my enemies rejoice over me deceitfully, those who hate me without cause wink with the eye: for they do not speak peace, and they devise deceitful words against the quiet of the land; and they opened their mouths wide against me.* <note>original Hebrew: "Al yismechu li oyvai sheker, shon'ei chinam yikretzu ayin..."</note> That is: Let not my enemies exult over me mendaciously, hating me without cause...

Because of the selling and buying of the Messiah—who is true God and man—it is best proven from the words of the Prophet Amos that the Jews underwent this most recent captivity. Thus he says in chapter 2: *Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back (or I will not bring him back, or I will not transform him), because he sold (or bought) the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes* <note>original Hebrew: כה אמר יהוה על שלשה פשעי ישראל ועל ארבעה לא אשיבנו על מכרם בכסף צדיק ואביון בעבור נעלים; see Amos 2:6.</note>. <margin>The objections of the Jews.</margin> CAPNIO. Since the Jews of our time are greatly forced to admit the truth by this prophecy, they strive to pervert the true understanding of the prophecy itself with many quibbles in order to escape that truth. Therefore, I would wish for you to refute their false objections with truthful responses, as you are accustomed to doing. GALATINUS. I will indeed do so most willingly. So that their false claims may be better exposed, you shall report their objections one by one, and I will attempt to refute each of them using the opinions of the ancient members of their own nation. <margin>The first objection.</margin> CAPNIO. First, they object in this way: Since the Prophet first mentions the crimes of Judah and then speaks of the crimes of Israel—and the crime committed against Jesus the Nazarene was not perpetrated by Israel but by Judah <note>Likely referring here to the tribe of Judah or the region of Judea.</note>—they say that surely nothing can be inferred against them from this text. <margin>The response.</margin> GALATINUS. This objection is surely of no weight. For even if Israel was separated from Judah during the time of the First Temple, nevertheless, during the time of the Second Temple, both were united among themselves and gathered together. This is because the opportunity to return from the Babylonian captivity was given to everyone from both Israel and Judah by Cyrus, King of the Persians, as is clear in Nehemiah chapters 7 and 8. And all those who returned lived in their cities during the time of the Second Temple and were all called "Israel," as is found at the end of the second chapter and the beginning of the third book of Ezra. Therefore, what is placed first in the text of the prophecy regarding the "crimes of Judah" refers to the Jews who existed before the destruction of the First Temple, since they were not "of Israel" at that time <note>Referring to the split into the Northern Kingdom (Israel) and Southern Kingdom (Judah).</note>. However, what is added regarding the "crimes of Israel" regards the times and destruction of the Second Temple, since everyone from Israel and Judah existed there then, and everyone was called by the single name "Israel." Furthermore, a sin that Judah alone committed is called the "sin of Judah," but what Judah and Israel committed together is called the "sin of Israel." Since a large part of the children of Benjamin and Levi were then in Jerusalem with Judah—indeed, people from every part of Israel had flocked there for the celebration of Passover—the part rightly ought to take the name of the whole. Therefore, since almost all consented to the death of Christ, the perpetration of this crime is not without reason attributed to all Israel, and all Israel is destroyed, and all are dispersed throughout the world, never to return.

# BOOK FOUR.
### M iiij

...sold him for silver, or rather bartered for him, and delivered him to death. Because of this crime, they were taken captive by the Romans in this most recent exile, from which the Lord will never lead them back so long as they remain as they are. Since the selling of Joseph was the first crime in chronological order—for which they later underwent the very harsh slavery of Pharaoh—it can hardly be called the "fourth" reason for which they sustain this long-lasting captivity; especially since divine justice never punishes twice for the same crime.

<margin>Fourth objection.</margin> 
CAPITO. Some, moved by this reasoning, do indeed concede that the "righteous one" for whose selling they undergo this irrevocable captivity was not Joseph; however, they do not admit the truth because of this, but rather deny it even more. For they say that this righteous person was not Jesus of Nazareth, but some other righteous man whose name is unknown.

<margin>Response.</margin> 
GALATINUS. Surely this statement is as hollow and irrational as can be. This is clear primarily because, although that crime was so grave and so abominable to God above all others—to the point that no forgiveness has followed it yet, and divine indignation rages unappeased against all Israel for so long because of it—nevertheless, the person against whom it was committed remains hidden from all mortals.

<margin>Fifth objection.</margin> 
CAPITO. Some others also say that in this passage, "justice" should be understood instead of "a righteous man." For in those days, the judges and ministers of justice, corrupted by money (as they say), sold the justice of poor men everywhere for a small price.

<margin>Response.</margin> 
GALATINUS. That interpretation is also perverse: first, because "righteous man" and "justice" are different nouns among the Hebrews. For a righteous man is called <term>tsadic</term> <note>Hebrew: צדיק, meaning a person who is just or godly</note>, while justice is called <term>tsedec</term> <note>Hebrew: צדק, meaning the abstract quality of righteousness or justice</note. And the text does not say *tsedec*, that is, justice, but *tsadic*, that is, a righteous man. Furthermore, the Prophet mentions the selling or bartering of this righteous man and the oppression of the poor separately. He placed the selling or bartering of the righteous man first to clearly suggest that the Jews would suffer this final captivity because they were going to sell, or rather barter for, that Righteous One. Moreover, if "the justice of the poor" (which was to be for sale) were to be understood as this "selling of the righteous," such a great vengeance would by no means have followed as a punishment for this crime. For if punishment is to be inflicted according to the measure of the fault, then graver crimes ought to be punished more severely, while lighter ones should be treated with a lighter penalty. It is well established that the selling of a brother, idolatry, and the murder of the Prophets were graver crimes than the selling of justice for the poor. Therefore, if the fourth crime was (as they assert) the selling of justice for the poor, it should not have been punished more severely than the first three—especially by God, who by His very nature is more inclined and ready to show mercy than to punish. If, therefore, the Israelites were punished far more severely, far more bitterly, and far longer for the commission of the fourth crime than for the commission of the preceding three, it follows necessarily that the fourth crime was something other than the selling of justice for the poor, and much more grave, since its punishment exceeded the punishments of the others almost to infinity. For even if under human law smaller sins are sometimes punished more severely, in divine law the measure of the blows is according to the measure of the sin, as it is said in Deuteronomy 25 <note>The text says 24, but refers to the principle in Deut. 25:2.</note>. But what sin could be greater than the selling of a brother, or idolatry, or the 

<column-break/>

killing of the Prophets? Certainly none other than the selling or bartering unto death of the Messiah himself, who was God and man. This is also evident because, in the Hebrew language, guilt of this kind is described with a word such as is applied to one who has denied God; but the selling or bartering of a mere man unto death cannot be equated with the denial of God. Therefore, it necessarily follows that this Righteous One—for whose selling or bartering they were to incur this greatest of all punishments—was to be God as well as man.

<margin>Sixth objection.</margin> 
CAPITO. Finally, they ask: if by the "righteous man" to be sold for silver we understand the Messiah, who then was that "poor man" whom the Prophet says in the same place is to be sold for a pair of shoes? For he immediately added: <term>and the poor for a pair of shoes</term> <note>Hebrew: ואביון בעבור נעלים, v-evyon ba'avur na'alayim</note>.

<margin>Response.</margin> 
GALATINUS. Neither is anyone else but one and the same true Messiah, whom the Prophets predicted would come in his first advent as both "righteous" and "poor," and especially Zechariah in chapter 9, saying: <term>Behold, your King will come to you, the righteous one and the savior; he is poor and riding upon a donkey.</term> <note>Hebrew: הנה מלכך יבוא לך צדיק ונושע הוא עני ורוכב על חמור</note> So that no one would think highly of that silver for which that Righteous One was to be sold, the Prophet immediately added, *And the poor for a pair of shoes*; as if to say, "The silver for which they will sell or barter that righteous and poor man will be of such a value that it can be compared to the price of a pair of shoes." 

<margin>Confirmation.</margin> 
What more evident testimony do we seek that the Jews underwent this captivity because of the selling, bartering, and death of the Messiah, the true God and man, than that which they themselves read in their own books? For as is read in the Talmud, at the very beginning of the captivity, Hadrian Caesar took ten men of Israel—who excelled others in learning, dignity, and lineage—and cast them into prison, asking whether they had sold a righteous man. "For your Law," he said, "has decreed that whoever sells a Jew shall be punished with a sentence of death. And you, therefore, according to the judgment of your own law, shall die." Wherefore, by the decree of that same law, he ordered them to be killed by various tortures. For he did not restrain them all with one punishment, but different types of death were set before each individual. For one was flayed alive, another was torn by the claws of an iron comb, another was burned with fire, and various deaths consumed the rest. The Talmudic book explains those deaths, and the book <term>Machazor</term> <note>A prayer book used for Jewish festivals.</note> testifies to them in the prayers they make <term>on the Fast of Atonement</term> <note>Yom Kippur; Hebrew: בצום כפור, be-tzom kippur</note>, which they solemnly celebrate on the tenth moon of the month they call <term>Tishri</term> <note>The first month of the Hebrew civil year (September/October).</note>, <term>regarding the ten killed of the kingdom by Caesar; from which I have excerpted these things:</term> <note>Hebrew: על עשרה הרוגי מלכות</note>

# BOOK FOUR.

<margin>Those killed by Hadrian Caesar for the sale of the righteous one.</margin>
**And you shall bear the iniquity of your fathers** <note>original Hebrew: *v’atem tisa’un avoteichem*</note>. That is, at the beginning of the captivity of Israel, Caesar <note>Referencing the Roman Emperor Hadrian</note> took ten of the elders, who were: Rabbi Ismael, son of Elisha, the High Priest; Rabban Simeon, son of Gamaliel, the Prince; Rabbi Akiba; Rabbi Hanina, son of Teradion; Rabbi Huspith the Interpreter; Rabbi Eleazar, son of Shammua; Rabbi Judah, son of Dama; Rabbi Yeshebab the Scribe; Rabbi Judah, son of Hachinai; and Rabbi Judah, son of Baba. And he said to them, "Judge a judgment of true justice. If a man is found who has stolen the soul of his brother from the children of Israel, betrayed him, and sold him, what shall his penalty be?" They answered, saying, "That thief shall die." Caesar replied and said, "And where are your fathers, who sold their own brother? Therefore, you must receive the judgment of heaven upon yourselves. If they were still alive, I would bring their judgment before you; you, therefore, shall bear the iniquity of your fathers." All this is recorded there. And so, because of the crime committed by their fathers in the selling of a righteous man, he caused them to perish by various tortures, as is contained more extensively in that same place. 

Here it is greatly to be noted that Caesar, wishing to convict them by their own law, proposed to them the words written in the twenty-fourth chapter of Deuteronomy, saying: "If a man is found who has stolen a soul from the children of Israel and sold him with treachery, what shall happen?" They, condemning themselves with their own mouths, answered with the words immediately following in that same place in Deuteronomy: "That thief shall die." Since, however, the name of this "righteous one"—for whose sake they were so punished—is not placed there (partly because the Talmudists <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law</note> perhaps kept it silent, and partly because the more recent Jews, which is more likely, deleted it from there), the commentaries of their younger scholars say in that same place that this righteous one was Joseph, the son of Jacob, whom his brothers sold into Egypt. They claim that for this reason, Caesar demanded his blood from them and afflicted them with such punishments. 

Thus, rather than confess the truth, they are forced to fall into a most wicked heresy. For while they ask among themselves, "Why should these men, rather than others, pay the penalty for the sin of Joseph's brothers?" and knowing no other reason to give, they claim there was a **cycle of souls** <note>original Hebrew: *gilgul neshamot*</note>, that is, a reincarnation of souls. They assert that they suffered for the crime of Joseph’s brothers because the souls of those brothers were within them. This is surely so absurd that it requires no refutation; for it is not only against the true faith and Holy Scripture, but also against natural reason. It also lacks all reason to think Caesar would demand from them payment for something done at least fifteen hundred years earlier, especially at a time when Caesar could have convicted them as guilty of a [more recent] death. Therefore, it is necessary to conclude that this "righteous one," for whose sale and death they were punished with such a cruel slaughter, was none other than Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah, true God and man. In vengeance for him, nearly 40 years after his death, Jerusalem was utterly overturned, and this most recent captivity of the Jews followed. 

<margin>Why the Jewish [exile] followed. CHAPTER: Why did the vengeance not follow immediately after the death of the Messiah, but only after 40 years had elapsed? GALATINUS: It is certainly not to be thought that this happened without cause.</margin> 

CHAPTER: Why did the vengeance not follow immediately after the death of the Messiah, but only after 40 years had elapsed? 
GALATINUS: It is certainly not to be thought that this happened without cause. For God 

<column-break/>

# BOOK FOUR.

<margin>They were punished, but after 40 years.</margin>
acts patiently, not wishing for anyone to perish, but for all to return to repentance so that they may finally be saved. Therefore, so that the Jews might have time for repentance after committing such a great crime, He willed to delay this vengeance for 40 years. This the ancient Talmudists, who preceded the coming of Christ, both perceived and, enlightened by the Holy Spirit, foretold. For Rabbenu Haccados <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah</note>, in the book which he called **The Revealer of Secrets** <note>original: *Gale Razia*</note>, in the eighth petition, says thus: "Forty years after his passion, God will postpone the destruction to see whether they will turn back to Him." 

And a little later, wishing to give the reason why God would accept the number forty rather than any other number to prolong the time of punishment, he added these same words: "God will take the number forty by reason of those 40 days in which a man, having been made, remains in his mother's womb for the composition of his limbs in original sin. And because the King Messiah is to come to release this sin and to bring souls into paradise, he will therefore wait 40 years, one year for each day. Just as the scouts whom Israel sent to investigate the Promised Land and to seek out the truth delayed 40 days on their journey, saying that whatever God had said was false, and therefore they did not wish to enter it. All that was a figure of Israel, who would speak against the King Messiah and say that his promises about bringing them into paradise were false. And therefore He will wait 40 years, just as He waited for Israel for another 40 years in the desert so they would not enter Jerusalem, one year for each day. Nevertheless, just as those who came after them entered the lower Jerusalem—those who did not harden their hearts like their fathers—so also those who stain themselves with the death of the King Messiah shall not enter the heavenly Jerusalem, except for those who follow afterwards, if they turn to him and wait forty years." 

All these are the word-for-word sayings of that Rabbenu Haccados, whom the Jews call "Our Holy Master." If, therefore, the Jews were to undergo this most recent captivity in which they now remain as punishment for the death of the Messiah (as has been abundantly proved in the preceding three chapters), it is surely concluded from what has been said that not only has the time of the Messiah's first coming already passed, but also that the Messiah himself has already come, and that he was none other than Jesus of Nazareth.

# BOOK FOUR.

It is necessary to show this.
<margin>A</margin> GALATINUS: This is first proved most beautifully through the vision of Nebuchadnezzar, the King of the Chaldeans <note>The Babylonians</note>. For this King (as written in the 2nd chapter of Daniel) saw a very large statue, which was composed of various metals. Its head consisted of the finest gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, its legs of iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly clay. Then indeed Daniel, both the pointer and interpreter of the King's dreams, continues thus in Chaldaic <note>original: "Chaldaice"; this refers to Aramaic, the language used in portions of the Book of Daniel</note>:

<margin>B</margin> You were watching until a stone was cut out, but not by human hands, and it struck the statue upon its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them. <note>original: "חזה הוית עד די התגזרת אבנר די לא בידין, ומחת לצלמא על רגלוהי די פרזלא וחספא והדקת המון"</note>
This means: You were watching until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands, and it struck the statue upon its iron and clay feet, and shattered them. Afterward, Daniel himself, wishing to explain to the same king what the statue itself designated, added these things among others:

<margin>C</margin> You are the head of gold. And after you shall rise another kingdom, inferior to you. And another third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over all the earth. And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and shatters and tames all things, so shall it crush and tame all these. And whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters' clay and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; and there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, <note>original: "אנת הוא ראשה די דהבא..." etc. This is the Aramaic text of Daniel 2:38-44, describing the succession of four world empires.</note>

<margin>D</margin> just as you saw the iron mixed with miry clay. Furthermore, as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly fragile. And whereas you saw iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men, but they shall not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay. And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed. And its kingdom shall not be left to another people. It shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever. In these words, the great God indicated to King Nebuchadnezzar through Daniel four kingdoms that would succeed one another in the world. For the golden head of the statue he had seen signified himself and his kingdom, that is, the Kingdom of the Chaldeans. The chest and arms of silver signified the kingdom of the Persians and Medes. The belly and thighs of bronze represented the Greek Monarchy.

<margin>G</margin> Furthermore, the iron legs designated the Roman Empire. Then, the mixture of iron and clay in the feet and toes of the statue suggested the alliance of two kingdoms—namely, the strong and the weak—that is, the Roman

<margin>A</margin> and the Jewish kingdoms, arising from the "iron seedling," that is, by the permission and association of the Roman Empire. Finally, by the stone cut from the mountain without hands, which, striking the iron and clay feet of the statue, crushed it and reduced it to dust, he showed that the Messiah was designated, who was to bring the Roman Empire under his authority. Moreover, the mountain from which that stone was cut figured the mother of the Messiah herself, who, on account of the excellence of her virtues, is not inaptly compared to a mountain.

<margin>B</margin> But because the Messiah was to be born of a virgin mother, he therefore said this stone was cut from the mountain by itself without hands—that is, without human embraces—to designate that the Messiah’s body was to be formed without male seed, by the operation of the Holy Spirit alone, from the purest blood of the virgin. He showed that the birth and arrival of this Messiah would occur while the mixture of iron and clay lasted—that is, while the alliance of Roman and Jewish power remained—when he said:

<margin>C</margin> And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven shall raise up or establish a Kingdom, which shall not be dissipated for ages—that is, for eternity. And its kingdom shall not be delivered to another people. It shall crush and confound all those kingdoms, and it itself shall stand—that is, endure—throughout the ages, which means forever. <term>The Gloss of Rabbi Abraham</term> <note>Referring to Abraham Ibn Ezra, a famous 12th-century biblical commentator</note> says: This is the kingdom of the Messiah. Finally, Daniel, concluding, says:

<margin>D</margin> Inasmuch as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain without hands, and it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what is to come hereafter. And the dream is true, and its interpretation is faithful. <note>original: "כל קבל די חזית די מטורא אתגזרת אבן..." etc. Daniel 2:45.</note> These things are clearly evident from the explanation of the aforesaid. Moreover, these things are excellently confirmed by what is in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>A Jewish homiletical commentary on the Psalms</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Psalms, upon the title of Psalm 17, where it is said:

<margin>E</margin> "When the Messiah comes with speed, there shall be none singing a song." And below: "Until he falls before him who has toes—namely, the wicked Kingdom, which is the Roman," of which it is said in <term>Daniel 2</term>: "And the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, and the kingdom shall be partly solid and partly fragile. And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven shall raise up or establish a kingdom, which shall not be dissipated for eternity. It shall crush and consume all those kingdoms, and it itself shall stand forever. Just as you saw, that a stone cut itself from the mountain without hands, and crushed the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold." This is the King Messiah, just as it is said in <term>Bereshit Rabbah</term> <note>An early Jewish commentary on Genesis</note>.

<margin>F</margin> All these things are tradition. These are also approved by the opinion of <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Rashi, the most influential medieval Jewish commentator</note> regarding that saying in Isaiah 8: "And he shall be for a sanctuary, and for a stone of stumbling"; when he says: "He shall be a savior to Israel for preparation, and a stone of stumbling. And the iron and clay feet of the statue shall stumble against him—that is, the Kingdom of the Romans and the Jews."

<meta>This page continues the interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar’s vision from Daniel 2. The previous page established the four kingdoms (Gold/Babylon, Silver/Persia, Bronze/Greece, Iron/Rome). Now, the author explains the meaning of the "feet of iron and clay" as a specific prophecy regarding the alliance and eventual conflict between the Roman Empire and the Jewish people.</meta>

<margin>The alliance of the Romans with the Jews.</margin>
...namely, that the Messiah was to come while they were still in their own land and possessed power. Furthermore, regarding the phrase, *And the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay*, and *the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly fragile* <note>Daniel 2:41-42</note>: this should be understood as the Kingdom of the Romans and that of the Jews. These two nations entered into a partnership after the Maccabees <note>The Hasmonean dynasty who led a Jewish rebellion against the Greeks</note> wrestled the Kingdom of the Jews from the hands of the Greeks. This is evident from what is said in the book *Avodah Zarah* <note>original: עבודה זרה; a tractate of the Talmud concerning "Strange Worship" or idolatry</note>, in the chapter *Liphne edehen* <note>original: לפני אידיהן; meaning "Before their festivals"</note>. There it is read: "Rabbi Jose Dimi said: For thirty-two years the Romans waged war with the Greeks and did not prevail against them until they allied themselves with Israel. This was the pact: when there were kings from the Romans, there would be governors from the Jews, and when there were kings from the Jews, there would be governors from the Romans." Rabbi Kahana said: "When Rabbi Ishmael was ill, they sent to him, saying: 'Rabbi, explain to us two or three words which you told us in the name of your father.' He sent word back to them, saying: 'My father said that for 180 years before the destruction of the Holy House <note>The Second Temple</note>, the Wicked Kingdom <note>original: "Regnum nequam"; a common Rabbinic code for the Roman Empire</note> held power over Israel.'" This is found there. In the Talmud, the "Wicked Kingdom" is understood to be the Roman Empire. 

The first book of Maccabees (chapter 8) records this alliance between the Romans and the Jews more extensively. Just as the days of those Kings began when the Roman-Jewish alliance was first made, and later when they were joined "by the seed of man but not of woman"—which occurred when Herod committed a foul crime involving a dead girl of the Maccabean line (as was discussed above in chapter 6 of this book) and therefore they did not cling together <note>Referring to Daniel 2:43; Galatinus interprets Herod’s illegitimate rise to power as the "clay" that won't bond with the Roman "iron"</note>—so too the days of those same Kings ceased to be when the Jews, following their false Messiah, rose up against the Roman Empire. This was explained at length in chapter 21 of this book. 

There is no doubt that the Roman Empire is designated by "iron." For as was predicted by Daniel in the explanation of the vision, just as iron tames all metals, so the Roman Empire tamed all kingdoms. That the Jews are called "potter’s clay" is found in Lamentations 4, where it is said: *The precious sons of Zion, once clothed in gold, how they are now regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands!* <note>original: בני ציון היקרים המסלאים בפז, איכה נחשבו לנבלי חרש מעשה ידי יוצר</note>. This is also clearly seen in Isaiah 45, where it says: *Woe to him who strives with his Maker, a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth!* <note>original: הוי רב את יוצרו חרש את חרשי אדמה</note>. 

From all these things it is openly shown how elegantly it was revealed to King Nebuchadnezzar not only that the Messiah was to subject the Roman Empire to himself, but also how the Messiah himself was to be born according to the flesh from a mother without a father. This was shown under the figure of the stone cutting itself from the mountain without hands, along with the time he was to be born, and what sort of things he would do. If, therefore, the Messiah was to subject the Roman Empire to himself, and Jesus of Nazareth subjected it to himself, it follows by necessity that the Messiah has already come, and that it was Jesus of Nazareth himself, to whom the Roman Empire has been subject until now.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

->*That the Messiah was to rule the entire world, and concerning the universal Kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ.*<-

### CAPNIO. <note>The persona of Johann Reuchlin, the famous Christian Hebraist</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial Q featuring a landscape with a building and foliage inside a circular frame.</image-desc> ALTHOUGH it is sufficiently suggested by what has just been said that the Messiah was to rule the entire world, nevertheless, so that it may be more clearly established that this was fulfilled in our Lord Jesus Christ, this same point must be more openly proved. 

GALATINUS: This is first proved from the commentaries of Rabbi Moses Hadarsan <note>An 11th-century preacher from Narbonne</note> on the book of Genesis, regarding that saying in chapter 49: *The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the scribe from between his feet, until Shiloh comes* <note>Genesis 49:10</note>; that is, the Messiah. *And to him the peoples shall be gathered.* For there the same Rabbi says: "He said 'scepter' and not 'king.' For it was revealed and known before Him that kings would not stand forever, but only until Shiloh comes—that is, the Messiah—who is the 'little son' who is to be his in the end of many days, as Onkelos <note>The author of the Targum, an Aramaic translation of the Torah</note> explained concerning his infancy and his smallness. For he is the one to whom all nations shall gather, and he shall have a complete kingdom over them, like the kingdom of Solomon <note>The name Solomon is related to the Hebrew word for peace, 'Shalom'</note>, which is a kingdom of peace. As it is written in Psalm 72: *And all kings shall bow down to him, all nations shall serve him.* And thereafter, he himself shall bow to no one; rather, all shall bow and fall prostrate before him. And this is what is written in the same Psalm: *Before him the Ethiopians shall fall prostrate, and his enemies shall lick the dust.*" These are the words of Rabbi Moses Hadarsan. 

From these words the proposition is clear. The same thing is then most clearly shown by what is added to the aforementioned vision of Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel, chapter 2. For it is read there: *And the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.* <note>original: ואבנא די מחת לצלמא הות לטור רב ומלת כל ארעא</note>. The ancient Talmudists wished this to be understood as the universal dominion of the Messiah. For in *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>An ancient commentary on Genesis</note>, on the passage in Genesis chapter 42 which says, *And Joseph himself was made powerful over the land*, it is read literally: "The Masters have handed down that ten Kings have ruled from the beginning of the world until its end. The first of these is God, holy and blessed, who spoke and the world was—that is, who created the world by the power of His word. The second King was Nimrod the impious. The third King was Joseph. The fourth King was Solomon, King of Israel. The fifth King was Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon. The sixth King was Darius, who reigned over the Kingdom of the Chaldeans..."

It uses Rabbinic sources to support the idea that the Messiah's reign would be global and peaceful, succeeding the great earthly empires.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the interpretation of the "Four Kingdoms" prophecy from the Book of Daniel, moving from the historical succession of empires to the final triumph of the Messianic kingdom. It focuses on the transition from the Roman Empire to the spiritual and temporal reign of Christ.</meta>

### BOOK FOUR

The seventh king was Cyrus, who ruled from one end of the orb to the other, as stated in the first chapter of Ezra and the last of Chronicles: "Cyrus King of <margin>A</margin> **Persia** <note>original: פרס (Paras)</note> said: The Lord has given me all the kingdoms of the earth." The eighth king was Alexander the Macedonian, who ruled over the entire world, as stated in the 8th chapter of Daniel: "And I was observing, and behold, a male goat coming from the west across the face of the whole earth." The ninth king is Augustus Caesar himself, who commanded the entire world, as stated in Daniel chapter 2: "And the fourth kingdom <margin>B</margin> shall be as strong as iron, because as iron it will crush and break all these things." The tenth king, however, is King Messiah, who shall reign from one end of the world to the other, as stated in Psalm 72: "He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth." Likewise, another scripture says in Daniel chapter 2: "And the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth." And again in the same place: "And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven shall raise up (or <margin>C</margin> establish) a Kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall it be left to another people. It shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever." Through this tenth Kingdom, the Kingdom shall return to its Lord. And so He who was the first King shall be the last King, as it is written in Isaiah chapter 44: <margin>D</margin> **"Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and his redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last"** <note>original: כה אמר יהוה מלך ישראל וגאלו יהוה צבאות אני ראשון ואני אחרון</note>—namely, the King. And again that passage from Zechariah: <margin>D</margin> **"And the Lord shall be King over all the earth."** <note>original: והיה יהוה למלך על כל הארץ</note> All this is tradition, omitting a few things that are not pertinent to the matter. Since, therefore, it is said in this tradition that the tenth King is the Messiah, who was to reign from one end of the world to the other, let us say to the Jews that Christ our Lord dominates not only from the end of the world to its other end, but also in the Kingdom of Heaven insofar as He is God himself. Subsequently, that saying of David from Psalm 72 is placed there: <margin>E</margin> **"And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth"** <note>original: וירד מים עד ים ומנהר עד אפסי ארץ</note>. This is also to be understood literally regarding the Kingdom of Christians, which is well-known to have once spanned the entire world; but even today it can rightly be said to be "from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth." For even today this is true from sea to sea—that is, from the Mediterranean Sea to the Ocean, at least the English Channel <margin>F</margin>. And "from the river"—that is, from the Danube, which is the greatest among other rivers and descends beyond Greece into the Black Sea—unto the "head of the earth," which is to say Spain, which is the head <note>The Latin *caput* means "head" or "extremity," referring to Spain as the westernmost point of the known world, *Finis Terrae*</note> of the earth. And although the Saracens or Muslims occupy many and almost infinite Christian places, Christ does not cease to reign in those same places, since they themselves confess him to be the Messiah, conceived by the Spirit of God and born of a virgin without male seed, even if they deny his divinity. As for what is said in the same tradition following Daniel's prophecy—"And the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth"—this was certainly fulfilled when, through the preaching and doctrine of the Apostles and other 

<column-break/>

saints who followed in their footsteps, the idols of the Romans, the Greeks, and many other nations throughout the whole world were cast out. Therefore, without a doubt, that stone—which is the Messiah—became a great mountain. Not, indeed, that He was greater than He was before, but because He became better known to the Nations who converted to Him.

### CHAPTER XXVII

#### That Christ truly subjected the Roman Empire to Himself. And concerning the universal dominion of the Roman Pontiff and the Emperor.

-> CAPNIO <-
<note>Capnio is the Greek-derived nickname of Johann Reuchlin, the famous humanist scholar who is a speaker in this dialogue</note>

<margin>G</margin> Although all these things are so true that they can hardly be denied by the Jews, yet for their greater confusion, it must be proved by some testimony of the Prophets that the Roman Empire itself was to be subjected to our Lord Jesus Christ. GALATINUS: Isaiah predicted long ago that both Rome itself and the Roman Empire must be subjected to the Lord Jesus, the true Messiah, when he says in the twenty-sixth chapter: **"The city of our strength is Jesus; he shall set walls and a bulwark. Open the gates, and let the righteous nation enter, which keeps the faiths. The joined creature shall keep peace, because in you is hope. Hope in God forever, because in the Lord God is the strength of ages. For he shall bring down those who dwell on high. He shall humble the lofty city, he shall humble it even to the ground, he shall bring it even to the dust; the foot of the poor shall tread it down, the steps of the needy."** <note>This is a Christian interpretive translation of Isaiah 26:1–6</note> Let us seek no other explanation of these words than that of **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator</note>. For he himself explains it thus: "The city of strength shall be for us **Jesus** <note>original: ישוע (Yeshua)</note>, that is, the Savior or salvation." And further: "He shall humble the lofty city"—that is, Rome and Italy; "he shall humble it," I say, "even to the ground; the foot of the feet of the poor shall tread it"—that is, the King Messiah, of whom it is said in Zechariah 9: "Poor, and riding upon an ass." "The steps of the needy"—that is, Israel. This gloss of Rabbi Solomon brings much strength to our faith. For then "the foot of the feet of the poor"—that is, the King Messiah—humbled Rome and Italy even to the ground, when the loftiness of the Roman Empire, almost touching the sky, humbly submitted its neck to the yoke of the Christian faith, even to the point of kissing the feet of the poor and humble ones who act in Christ's stead. Then, however, "the steps of the needy" (that is, Israel, according to Rabbi Solomon's gloss) trampled Rome itself, when at the preaching of Christ's Apostles, Peter and Paul, they subjected themselves to Christ, utterly abandoning the cult of idolatry, the pleasures, and the delights which the Christian religion rejects. CAPNIO: When, I ask, did Christ subject the Roman Empire to himself? GALATINUS: Certainly most especially when Constantine, the Roman Emperor and Monarch of the world, [received] baptism...
