<meta>This page continues the argument that the Roman Empire is the fourth kingdom mentioned in the prophecy of Daniel. Having established the historical lineage of empires, the text now transitions to the reign of Constantine the Great and the transition of authority to the Church, framed through the "Donation of Constantine"—a document widely accepted as genuine in the author's time.</meta>

### BOOK FOUR

<margin>The Emperor Constantine subjected himself and the Roman Empire to Christ. His donation was made to the vicar of Christ.</margin>Having received the sacrament <note>This refers to Constantine’s baptism, which legend says cured him of leprosy.</note> and been cleansed of leprosy, and having recovered his health through divine power, Constantine recognized that Jesus Christ himself is the redeemer and savior of the world, the true King of Kings, and the sole Lord of heaven and earth. He voluntarily subjected himself and the entire Roman Empire to him. As a sign of this subjection, he granted as a gift to the blessed Sylvester—then the vicar of Christ—and to all his successors: the Imperial Lateran Palace; the crown from his own head, constructed of purest gold, precious stones, and pearls; the *phrygium* <term>phrygium: a tall, conical cap that evolved into the papal tiara</term>, that is, the miter; the *superhumerale* <term>superhumerale: an imperial shoulder-collar or pallium</term>, which used to encircle the imperial neck; the purple cloak; the scarlet tunic; and all the imperial garments. He also gave the dignity of the imperial presiding knights, the imperial scepters, and all the standards and banners, various imperial ornaments, and all the glory and power of the imperial height used in processions. Placing the *phrygium* upon the Pope’s most sacred head with his own hands, and holding the reins of the horse upon which the Pontiff sat, he performed the office of a groom for him. And lest the sacred Senate of Christ should shine with less glory than the Imperial one, he established many great dignities for the exalted fathers, the Cardinals of the holy Roman Church. Finally, having granted in perpetuity to the Supreme Pontiff Sylvester (as the vicar of Christ and successor to the most blessed Peter) and to his successors the city of Rome—which was both the head of the world and the seat of the empire—as well as many provinces, cities, and places in the western regions, Constantine departed for Byzantium. He transferred the Roman Empire, which he had subjugated to Christ, to the eastern regions, as all these things and many others are most extensively contained in his imperial edict <note>This refers to the "Donation of Constantine," a document later proven to be an eighth-century forgery, though the author here treats it as historical fact.</note>.

<margin>The Emperor of the Romans has dominion over the entire world.</margin>If, therefore, the Emperor of the Romans—who is over all kings and over all nations—is truly subjected to our Lord Jesus, the true Messiah, then who can rightly deny that our Lord Jesus Christ is the true monarch of the whole world? For the Emperor is the prince and lord of the world <note>The author cites Roman legal codes here, such as the *Digest* (ff. ad legem Rhodiam).</note>, whence the Greeks most aptly call him *autokratōr* <term>autokratōr: a Greek title meaning "self-ruler" or "absolute master"</term>, because he rules by his own right and his dominion depends on no one else. Since Jesus stands over both the Emperor and the entire Roman Empire, He is truly called and truly is the King of Kings and Lord of Lords. However, this ecumenical dominion of the whole world is shared: the Roman Emperor holds it in temporal matters, and the Roman Pontiff in spiritual matters. Concerning both, I think that passage written in Genesis chapter 1 is not inappropriately applied: "God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night." For what else is mystically designated by these two great lights other than the Supreme Pontiff and the Emperor? One of them, like the sun, rules and governs the "day"—that is, spiritual things; the other, like the moon, rules the "night"—that is, temporal things. From this it is clearly shown that both have universal dominion over the whole world. If, then, the Roman Empire was only to be subjugated by the Messiah, and it is certain that it was subjected to our Lord Jesus Christ long ago—

<margin>Conclusion.</margin>

288

—as has now been proven, it follows of necessity that our Lord Jesus Christ is the true Messiah.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.
->*Refutation of the Jewish opposition.*<-

### CAPNIO <note>Capnio is the Greek-derived nickname of Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous Christian Hebraist and character in this dialogue.</note>

**ALthough** the Jews are by no means able to contradict such manifest truth, they nevertheless do not cease to attack it. For they do indeed admit that the kingdom designated by "iron" is the Roman Empire, at the end of which they claim the Messiah will come and reign; but they altogether deny that the Roman kingdom has yet failed or come to an end. Since Rome itself is the head of that kingdom, and the seat of the Pope, and the head of the Christian Church, they call us Christians "Romans" after the name of the city itself. They say that the Roman kingdom will remain stable as long as Christians reign in the city of Rome. They believe the Roman nation is "Edom" <note>In medieval Jewish thought, "Edom" (the descendants of Esau) became a coded term for the Roman Empire and later for Latin Christendom.</note>. Because they believe Julius Caesar was of Edom, they say both those who reigned at Rome after him and the Romans themselves are of Edom. Therefore, since they call Christians "Romans," they also assert that they are of Edom. To confirm their error, they bring forward that saying of Jeremiah in Lamentations chapter 4: <term>Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz; to you also the cup shall pass, you shall become drunk and strip yourself bare. The punishment of your iniquity, O daughter of Zion, is accomplished; he will keep you in exile no longer; but your iniquity, O daughter of Edom, he will punish; he will expose your sins.</term> <note>original Hebrew: שישי ושמחי בת אדום...</note> From this they infer that they ought not to be redeemed from this latest captivity by the Messiah until the crushing and destruction of those of "Edom"—by whom they mean the Romans who keep the law of Jesus the Nazarene—first occurs. Whence, regarding the aforementioned words of Jeremiah, Rabbi Solomon <note>This refers to Rashi (Solomon ben Isaac), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> says that Jeremiah there predicted the destruction of the Roman Empire, which must happen to the Romans because they, in the time of Titus, overturned the temple and the city of Jerusalem and dispersed the Jews as captives throughout the world. And so, understanding "the daughter of Edom" to be Rome or the Roman people, they explain those words thus: *Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom*—as if he were saying, "That joy which you had in the subversion of the city of Jerusalem and the temple will be turned into sorrow for you." For <gloss>namely</gloss> the cup of divine vengeance shall also pass through you. Because of this, since they think the Roman Empire is not yet destroyed, they believe the Messiah has not yet come. This argument, among others, strengthens them greatly in the error of their perfidy. Thus it happens that they daily expect and desire the destruction of the Roman Empire all the more, because they believe themselves certain that immediately after the failing of the Roman Empire, the Messiah will come and they will be liberated from captivity. For this reason, my dear Galatino, especially in this place—

### BOOK FOUR

<margin>The first reason.</margin> In this place you must strive to ensure that their reasoning is utterly overturned. **Galatinus.** This will be easily done, my dear Capnio, if we first show that it is entirely false to understand "the daughter of Edom" in this context as Rome or the Roman people. For it is false that the Romans are the nation of Edom simply because a man who was from Edom <note>Referring to Herod the Great, who was of Idumean/Edomite descent.</note> reigned over them. Just as the Jews themselves are not called Romans or Edomites merely because Herod, who was from the nation of Edom, ruled over them.

<margin>The second reason.</margin> Furthermore, Edom was called by another name, Esau, as is held in Genesis 25. From this it is clear that Edom himself descended from Shem, the son of Noah, through Isaac, whose son was Esau. Since all of Europe, in which the city of Rome is situated, is said to have been first inhabited by the sons of Japheth, there is no reason why the Roman Empire could be signified by Edom.

<margin>The third reason.</margin> It is also certain that the land of Edom is that region which the Greeks named Idumea: to which the children of Israel came after departing from Egypt and passing through the desert; in which the mountains of Sinai and Hor are said to be; and where Aaron reached his final day. From these facts, therefore, it is clear that it is entirely false to say the daughter of Edom is Rome or the Roman people. **Capnio.** Why then do the Talmudists so very often call the Romans the "sons of Edom" and "Esau"? **Galatinus.** It is indeed true that in almost innumerable places in the Talmud, the Romans themselves are mystically called sometimes Edom, sometimes Esau, sometimes Seir, and sometimes even the sons of Edom or Esau; and Rome itself was once said to be Mount Seir and Mount Esau. This must be judged to have happened not without a mystery of our faith. To prove this point, I will add a few things. First, that which is written in Obadiah: <note>original: "ועלו מושיעים בהר ציון לשפוט את הר עשו והיתה ליהוה המלוכה"</note> "And saviors shall ascend" (that is, the Apostles, according to our gloss) "to Mount Zion, to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s." The gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), a preeminent medieval commentator.</note> says: "It teaches you," he says, "that His kingdom—namely, God’s—will not be perfect or peaceful until He has taken vengeance on the impious Esau." Indeed, Rabbi Jonathan interpreted "Mount Esau" in the aforementioned words of Obadiah into the Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note> as "the great fortress of Esau." The gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: "and this is Rome." Also, in the book called *Pesach Sheni* <note>original: "פסח שני", meaning "The Second Passover"</note>, it is written: "It shall come to pass that Egypt shall bring a gift to the Messiah." As it is said in Psalm 68: <note>original: "יאתיו חשמנים מני מצרים"</note> "Princes shall come out of Egypt." Ethiopia shall then take up an argument from the lesser—which the Hebrews call *Kal vahomer* <term>Kal vahomer: a logical method of "simple and grave," where a conclusion is drawn from a minor premise to a major one</term>—saying: "If these people, who made Israel serve them, act thus and are received by the Messiah, how much more shall we" (meaning, if we act likewise) "be received by him?" And this is what is written shortly after in the same Psalm: <note>original: "כוש תריץ ידיו לאלהים"</note> "Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God." The "wicked kingdom" too—that is, the Roman kingdom, according to Rabbi Solomon’s gloss—shall take up the same argument from the lesser for itself, saying: "If these who are not brothers are admitted by the Messiah for acting thus, how much more shall we, who are brothers?" For this is what is written in Micah 5: <note>original: "ויתר אחיו ישובון על בני ישראל"</note> "Then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel."

<column-break/>

### BOOK FOUR

<margin>A</margin> All this is tradition. From the end of which it is sufficiently held that the Romans were mystically called "sons of Esau" among the Hebrews because they are called the "brothers of Israel" here, and at the time of the Messiah they were to be converted to them. This was undoubtedly fulfilled when, through the preaching of the Apostles Peter and Paul, and especially in the time of Sylvester, they were converted to the faith of Christ.

<margin>B</margin> In the book which is called *Yoma* <note>original: "יומא", meaning "The Day," referring to the Talmudic tractate on the Day of Atonement.</note>, it is read thus word-for-word: "The Rabbi said, It is destined that Rome shall fall into the hand of Persia: as it is written in Jeremiah 49:" <note>original: "לכן שמעו עצת יהוה אשר יעץ אל אדום ומחשבותיו אשר חשב אל יושבי תימן אם לא יסחבום צעיri הצאן אם לא ישים עליהם נויהם"</note> "Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom, and his purposes that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out; surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them." This is the tradition. From which it clearly appears that the Romans are sometimes called "Edom" in Holy Scripture.

<margin>C</margin> <margin>Solomon’s exposition.</margin> Now, the gloss of Rabbi Solomon says that "the least of the flock" in the same tradition are the Persians, by whom the Romans were to be drawn out, because Perseus was the youngest among the sons of Japheth. <margin>The true exposition.</margin> But since this was by no means true, "the least of the flock" must be understood as the Apostles and the other disciples of Christ, who by the power of their preaching and miracles drew the Romans to the faith of Christ. For these were the "least," that is, the younger ones of the flock of the Jews.

<margin>D</margin> For the Jews were called "sheep," according to what was said in Ezekiel chapter 34: <note>original: "ואתן צאני צאן מרעیتי אדם אתם אני אלהיכם נאם אדני יהוה"</note> "And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God." From these things, therefore, it is plainly evident that it was not without reason that the Romans were once mystically and metaphorically called the sons of Esau and Edom.

<margin>E</margin> **Capnio.** Why were the Romans once metaphorically called Edom and sons of Esau? **Galatinus.** Because of imitation, I say. For not only they, but all others who persecuted the people of God and offered worship to idols, were called "Edom" and "Esau according to the flesh" by the ancient Jews, because they imitated their works. This is sufficiently seen from the fact that in the book *Avodah Zarah* <note>original: "עבודה זרה", meaning "Foreign Worship" or "Idolatry."</note>, it is read thus regarding that saying of Obadiah: <note>original: "ולace יהיה שריד לבית עשו"</note> "And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau"—that is, for those doing the works of Esau. It is also handed down thus: "And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau." Can this be said of everyone? It teaches that it should be said: "To the house of Esau," that is, to everyone performing the work of Esau.

<margin>F</margin> This is the tradition. From which it is manifest enough that the Jews of our time lie when they call Christians "Edom" or "sons of Esau," since they [Christians] do not imitate their works in the least. Rather, the Romans themselves ceased to be Edom and the sons of Esau when they were made Christians. For then that saying of Micah 5 was fulfilled: "And the remnant of their brothers shall be converted to the house of Israel."

<margin>G</margin> Therefore, to return to the previously mentioned prophecy of Jeremiah, we say that in the same, according to the truth, the "daughter of Edom" is the kingdom of Idumea, so named from the same Edom, and "Uz" is a city situated in the same kingdom. Therefore, Edom is said to dwell in the land of Uz: because that city of Uz was famous in that whole kingdom. **Capnio.** If a Jew should perchance say: "Since the daughter of Edom is properly the kingdom of Idumea, and you Christians say properly..."

### BOOK FOUR.

<margin>A</margin> Since this prophecy has been fulfilled, when exactly was it completed? **GALATINUS.** The ancient teachers of the Jews say that this prophecy was fulfilled in the time of King Hyrcanus the Maccabee <note>John Hyrcanus I, a Hasmonean leader and Jewish High Priest (reigned 134–104 BCE).</note>. At that time, all that land was destroyed. From there, Hyrcanus himself led out 4,000 captives, among others, to guard the walls of the city of Jerusalem. For this reason, as Josephus says, there was great joy in the temple on that day, because Bethsean and the other <gloss>his son Levi reports that no joy in the temple was ever greater than that one</gloss> cities of the <margin>B</margin> Idumeans <note>The Edomites.</note>, which could not be conquered in the time of Joshua, nor the Judges, nor in the time of the kings of Israel and Judah, were conquered in the time of this King Hyrcanus and brought under the rule of the Jews. Josephus further says that those of Edom, the sons of Esau, were converted to Judaism in the time of the aforementioned King Hyrcanus and were circumcised; they did not withdraw from the Jews in the time of Vespasian and Titus, but remained Jews ever after. Therefore, we say that the sin of the Jews, the children of Judah, was then remembered and they fell into captivity when the iniquity of the children of Judah—those who remained righteous at the coming of the Messiah, <margin>Conclusion.</margin> Jesus the Nazarene—was completed. From <margin>C</margin> all of this, it stands clearer than the sun that the interpretation of the aforementioned prophecy made by the younger Jews <note>Referring to contemporary Jewish scholars of the 16th century who associated "Edom" with Rome/Christianity.</note> is extremely distorted and entirely false; they wait for the destruction of the Roman Empire and the coming of the Messiah. It is also completely false that Christians (as they say) descended from Edom. On <margin>D</margin> the contrary, we say that the Jews themselves are from Edom—those who were converted to them from Edom—and those who are evil and sinners will receive perpetual punishment together with them, in which they are now and will remain until the end of the world. But we say that the Christians are the children of Sion and the good Jews who converted to Christ; in them, iniquity was completed—that is, sin and captivity ceased—and they themselves shall be free forever, as is clearly evident in the aforementioned prophecy. For the prophet says to those of Edom who converted to Judaism and to the other Jews who <margin>E</margin> deny Christ: "The cup also shall pass unto thee" <note>Lamentations 4:21</note>, that is, the penalty of divine vengeance. "Thou shalt be drunken," that is, you shall be punished to the full, "and shalt be made naked," that is, you shall be deprived of honor, dignities, and other goods. It is certain that this was done through Titus, the prince of the Romans. But concerning the good Jews who received Jesus the Nazarene as the true Messiah, and who are truly called the children of Sion, the prophet himself adds: "The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Sion" <note>Lamentations 4:22</note>, specifically at the coming of Christ. Because never <margin>F</margin> again was that people of Sion who believe in Christ subjected to any captivity—speaking of the people as a whole—as has already happened three times to the Jewish people. Therefore he says subsequently: "He will no more carry thee away into captivity," namely, from liberty into servitude. It follows concerning the evil Jews, the sons of Edom: "He will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom," namely, by punishing her justly. "He will discover thy sins," by bringing a punishment manifest to all; for their captivity and servitude are public throughout the whole world. For wherever the Jews dwell, whether among Christians or among Saracens <note>Historically used here to mean Muslims.</note>, they have always been captives and always held in abomination. From these points, the solution to the Jewish argument is clear. <term>CHAPTER.</term> <note>Original: "CAP." abbreviated for "CAPUT" (Chapter).</note> The Jews still insist: because the Roman <margin>An objection of the more recent Jews.</margin>

### BOOK FOUR.

<margin>A</margin> kingdom is the fourth among the other kingdoms foretold by Daniel, after which the kingdom of the Messiah (which would never have an end) was to follow, and since the Roman Empire still endures—because Roman emperors and kings have never ceased—they conclude that the Messiah has not yet come. **GALATINUS.** <margin>Response.</margin> Just as the intention of the prophet Daniel in predicting the destruction of the kingdom of the Chaldeans was not that no one would ever rule in Babylonia again, but that no one of the line of Nebuchadnezzar nor of his nation would rule there from then on (which <margin>B</margin> is why the kingdom of the Chaldeans was said to have failed then); and just as in the cessation of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, the prophet's intention was not that no one would ever rule in Media and Persia again, but that no one of the line or nation of Darius regarding the kingdom of the Medes, nor of the line or nation of Cyrus regarding the kingdom of the Persians, would rule henceforth; and just as in the failing of the kingdom of the Greeks, the same <margin>C</margin> prophet's intention was not that no one would ever rule in Greece again, but that no one of the line of Alexander nor of his nation would be king thereafter; so also it must be said regarding the dominion of the Roman kingdom, that the aforementioned prophet's intention was not that no one would rule in Rome any longer, but that no one of the line or nation of Julius Caesar, Octavian Augustus, Tiberius, and the others who worshipped idols would rule thereafter. Since, therefore, the Roman Emperors and kings in the seat of Julius Caesar and the other idol-worshippers do not believe in those idols at all, <margin>D</margin> but in the faith of Jesus the Nazarene, the true Messiah; and also because Constantine Caesar yielded the Roman kingdom to the servants of Jesus the Nazarene himself; and the Pope, who is the Lord of the city of Rome, was not called "Caesar" thereafter, nor did he come from Caesar's line or nation; and the Emperor of the Romans himself, to whom the whole world is rightfully subject, is a Christian and truly subject to Jesus Christ; it must necessarily be said that all those kingdoms foretold in the book of Daniel have already passed away and failed, except for the kingdom of Jesus the Nazarene, the true Messiah, which endures most firmly and shall endure forever. From this, it is necessary to concede that the Messiah has already come, and that Jesus the Nazarene was the true Messiah, as is abundantly gathered from what has been said in the four preceding chapters.

...to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob. And he will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths. From these passages, therefore, they raise six objections against us, wishing to prove that our Lord Jesus was not the Messiah, on the grounds that the Messiah himself has not yet come. 

<margin>First objection.</margin> And first, they argue thus: When the prophet says, "And it shall come to pass in the end of days," his saying is understood to be fulfilled in the days of the Messiah. Therefore, the Messiah was to come at the end of days. But your Christ did not come at the end of days, since many days have passed since his coming. Therefore, he himself was not the Messiah. 

<margin>Second.</margin> Then indeed thus: What the prophet says—"The mountain of the house of God shall be prepared at the top of the mountains"—has not yet happened. For we have not yet seen the mountain of the temple of the Lord raised above the tops of the mountains. Therefore, the Messiah has not yet come. 

<margin>Third.</margin> Thirdly, thus: When the prophet says, "And all nations shall flow to him," he predicted that all nations would flock together to the Messiah. Since, therefore, all nations have not flocked to him whom you say was the Messiah (for the <term>Saracens</term> <note>A medieval term for Muslims.</note>, the <term>Tartars</term> <note>A term used here for Central Asian and Mongol peoples.</note>, and many others do not run to him through faith), it follows that he was not the Messiah. 

<margin>Fourth.</margin> Afterward, what the prophet says—"And many people shall go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob"—was in no way fulfilled at the coming of Jesus of Nazareth. For some of those who believe in him say, "Let us go to the house of Peter." Others, "Let us go to the house of Paul." Others, "Let us go to the house of Francis." Others, "Let us go to the house of Anthony," and so on for the rest. But no one says, "Let us go to the house of the God of Jacob." Therefore, it is clear that Jesus of Nazareth himself was not the Messiah. 

<margin>Fifth.</margin> Fifthly, from what he says—"And they shall beat, or hammer, or crush their swords into plowshares," and the rest—it is evident that such great peace was to exist in the days of the Messiah that men would convert weapons of war into instruments of agriculture, and that nation would no longer lift up the sword against nation; and consequently, that peace would last without end. Since, therefore, such a thing has never happened—indeed, after he whom you assert to be the Messiah came, wars have been waged just as they were waged before; and perhaps it is established that many more, and much greater and sharper wars have happened after Jesus himself than happened before him—therefore, he himself was not the Messiah. 

<margin>Sixth.</margin> Finally, from what he says—"Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore"—they infer that the Messiah has not yet come, because peace without end has not yet been established in the world.

For the sun of the King Messiah shall rise; just as it is written in 2 Samuel chapter 23: *And like the morning light the sun shall rise* <note>original: "וכאור בקר יזרח שמש"</note>. In that hour their sun shall set, namely the sun of idolatry. Hence it is said: *And they shall be gathered* or joined. Thus far the tradition. <margin>E</margin> In which six most noteworthy points are placed. The first is that the Jews performed dark works, and that God darkened the world against them. The second is that they were destroyed by the "young lions," that is, by all the nations of the age, which are called "animals of the forest" there. The third is that humans are sometimes called by the names of irrational animals. The fifth is that their reward was to be the "sun," that is, the Messiah, who was to rise for them. <column-break/>

and dominion, and because Rome itself is under the zodiac sign of Leo (the Lion), could truly be called "young lions"—denied God through idolatry and ruled over all the nations of the world. They darkened the day of the Jews when Titus first utterly overturned their temple and city, and finally Hadrian destroyed them. But then they sought a reward from God when, in the time of Constantine and Pope Sylvester, they received the true faith. And then also the true sun, that is, the Messiah, rose for them, and the sun of idolatry set, as the preceding tradition excellently shows. Furthermore, in these things we have just said, it clearly appears that the "end of days" refers to the entire time of the last Temple up to its destruction. Indeed, among them, that letter is called *He ha-yedia* [ה ידיעה], that is, the "He of knowledge" or definition, because it makes the word it precedes known as referring not to an unknown thing, but to a known one. This is shown well enough where it is said through Moses in Deuteronomy 31: *I know that after my death you will surely become corrupt, and you will turn aside from the way which I commanded you. And evil will meet you in the end of haiamim* <note>original: "ידעתי אחרי מותי כי השחת תשחיתון וסרתם מן הדרך אשר צויתי אתכם וקראת אתכם הרעה באחרית הימים"</note>, that is, of *those* days, when you have done evil against God [YHWH] or the Messiah, to provoke him by the work of your hands. This evil met them, or occurred to them, when in the "end of their days," having rejected the Messiah, the Son of God, they were first through Vespasian and Titus, and then through Hadrian, either entirely destroyed or reduced to captivity. And thus the response to their first objection is given.

->Regarding the first objection of the Jews, that the Messiah was to come at the end of days.<-

### GALATINUS.

<margin>E</margin> Therefore, to the first of these objections, by which the younger Jews <note>Galatinus often distinguishes between "ancient" Jews (who he believes held truths closer to Christianity) and "modern/younger" Jews (his contemporaries).</note> try to conclude that the Messiah has not yet come, and consequently that our Lord Jesus was not the Messiah, because according to the aforementioned prophecies of Isaiah and Micah, the Messiah himself is to come at the end or in the last of days; we say that no <margin>F</margin> reason compels that by the "end" or "last of days" in the above-mentioned words, the end of mankind or of the world is designated, but rather the end of those to whom the prophets themselves were speaking. <margin>A</margin>An inevitable evil came upon them, as has been shown more extensively in the preceding pages. For then, when the day was finished, evening came—which is the end of the day—and their prosperity set; darkness fell over them, and baldness <note>symbolizing mourning or shame</note> descended upon their heads, because they denied the Messiah of the Lord. Furthermore, that evening and darkness came upon them as the day receded is found in the *Commentaries on Genesis* by Rabbi Moses Hadarsan, regarding that statement in the 30th chapter of the same book: <note>original Hebrew: ויבא יעקב מן השדה בערב ותצא לאה</note> "And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him." For it is said there:
<margin>B</margin> This is what is written in Psalm 104: <note>original Hebrew: תשת חשך ויהי לילה בו תרמש כל חיתו יער הכפירים שאגים לטרף ולבקש מאל אכלם : תזרח השמש יאספון</note> "You bring darkness, and it becomes night: in it all the animals of the forest creep about; the young lions roar for their prey, and seek their food from God. When the sun rises, they shall be gathered together." 

"You bring darkness," that is, the captivity of Israel, when their works were darkened, according to what was said in Isaiah 29: <note>original Hebrew: והיה במחשך מעשיהם</note> "And their works were in darkness." Therefore, God will darken the world against them. As it is said in Joel 2: <note>original Hebrew: שמש וירח קדרו וכוכבים אספו נגהם</note> "The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness." It follows, "and it will be night": These are the days of captivity, which are like night to Israel. "In it all the animals of the forest creep": These are the nations of the world, which are called animals of the forest because they creep about by trampling Israel; as it is said in Psalm 80: <note>original Hebrew: יכרסמנה חזיר מיער וזיז שדי ירענה</note> "The boar from the forest will destroy it, and the wild beast will feed upon it." It follows:
<margin>C</margin> "The young lions roar for their prey": These young lions are the Gentiles, who deny God, the Holy and Blessed One, and roar for prey. Rabbi Hanina said: These are the ones who deny God and roar for prey, and nonetheless, they will seek their reward from God in the future. Because it is said: "And to seek their food from God." And what will be their reward from God? This: because as it says in the same Psalm, "When the sun rises, they shall be gathered together." For the sun of the King Messiah shall rise; as it is written in 2 Samuel 23: <note>original: 2. reg. 23. cap.</note> <note>original Hebrew: וכאור בקר יזרח שמש</note> "And like the morning light, the sun shall rise." In that hour, their sun shall set—namely, the sun of idolatry. From this, therefore, it is said: "And they shall be gathered together," or joined. 

Thus ends the tradition, in which six points most worthy of note are placed. The first of these is that the Jews performed dark works, and that God darkened the world against them. The second is that they were destroyed by the young lions—that is, by all the nations of the world, who are there called animals of the forest. The third is that men are sometimes called by the names of irrational animals. The fourth, which is very notable, is that the nations who were to destroy the Jews would seek and receive their reward from God. The fifth is that their reward was to be the "Sun"—that is, the Messiah, who was to rise for them. Finally, the sixth is that in that hour, when the Sun—that is, the Messiah—was to rise for them, then the sun of idolatry was to set for them. 

The very outcome of events demonstrates that all these things have been fulfilled. For the Romans—who, partly because of their strength and

<margin>A</margin> lordship, and partly because Rome itself is under the sign of the Lion <note>a reference to the zodiac or potentially to the reigning Pope Leo X</note>, could truly be called "young lions"—were those who denied God through idolatry and ruled over all the nations of the globe. They darkened the day of the Jews when Titus first utterly overturned their temple and city, and finally when Hadrian destroyed them. But they sought their reward from God when, in the time of Constantine and Sylvester, they received the true faith. And then also the true Sun—the Messiah—rose for them, and the sun of idolatry set, as the preceding tradition so excellently shows. 

<margin>B</margin> Although from what we have just said it clearly appears that the "end of days" refers to the entire time of the last Temple up until its destruction, this is nevertheless most strongly suggested by the fact that the letter <term>He</term> <note>the Hebrew definite article 'the'</note> is prefixed to this word "days," when it is said *ha-yamim* <note>original: הימים</note>. This makes it an articulate expression, signifying something specific. It is exactly as if one were to say in Greek *tōn hēmerōn* <note>original: των ημερων</note>, "of the days." Indeed, this letter is called among them <term>He ha-yedi'ah</term> <note>original: הא הידיעה</note>, that is, the "*He* of knowledge," because it identifies the word to which it is prefixed as referring not to an unknown thing, but to a known one. 

<margin>C</margin> This is shown well enough where it is spoken through Moses in Deuteronomy 31 in this manner: <note>original Hebrew: ידעתי אחרי מותי כי השחת תשחיתון וסרתם מן הדרך אשר צויתי אתכם וקראת אתכם הרעה באחרית הימים</note> "I know that after my death you will be utterly corrupted, and you will turn aside from the way which I commanded you. And evil will meet you at the end of *ha-yamim*"—that is, of *those* days—"when you shall do evil against God <note>original: יהוה (YHWH)</note> or the Messiah, <margin>D</margin> to provoke him by the work of your hands." This evil met them, or occurred to them, when at the end of their days, having rejected the Messiah, the Son of God, they were either entirely destroyed or reduced to captivity—first through Vespasian and Titus, and later through Hadrian. And thus the answer is given to their first objection.

<margin>E</margin> ### CHAPTER III.

> *To the second objection of the Jews, that the Messiah has not yet come because the mountain of the house of the Lord has not yet been elevated above the mountains and hills.*

-> GALATINUS. <-

<margin>F</margin> **S**ECONDLY, we shall refute this objection of theirs: namely, when they infer from the words of the prophet saying, *The mountain of the house of God shall be prepared*, with the rest, that the Messiah has not yet come because they have not yet seen that mountain of the house of the Lord raised at the summit of the mountains.

# BOOK FIVE.

<margin>See chapter 60.</margin>...an old man, who had seen Jerusalem in its former state, told me that it was three leagues <note>A league is a historical unit of distance; here it suggests a city circumference of roughly 9 miles.</note> in circumference. And perhaps you will say that there will be difficulty in ascending it. But we are taught otherwise where it is said in Isaiah 60: <note>original Hebrew: מי אלה כעב תעופנה וכיונים אל ארבותיהם</note> "Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows?" Also in the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>An ancient Jewish commentary on the Psalms.</note>—that is, in the exposition of the Psalms—concerning that verse of Psalm 87: <note>original Hebrew: יסודתו בהררי קדש</note> "His foundation is in the holy mountains," it is said: <note>original Hebrew: אמר ר' פנחס בשם ר' ראובן עתיד הקב"ה להביא לתבור ולכרমেল וליתן ירושלם בראשן שנ' נכון יהיה הר בית יהוה בראש ההרים</note> "Rabbi Pinhas said in the name of Rabbi Ruben: In the future, the Holy and Blessed God will bring Mount Tabor and Mount Carmel and place Jerusalem on their peaks, as it is written in Isaiah 2: 'The mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established at the top of the mountains.'"

Therefore, younger Jewish scholars, misunderstanding such scriptures (for they interpret them literally rather than mystically, as they ought to be understood), argue that since this was to happen at the coming of the Messiah, and it is clear it has not yet happened, it is manifest that the Messiah has not yet come. To these people we respond: This elevation of the mountain of the Lord's house was to be understood not literally, but spiritually. This is clearly shown not only through the expositions of the ancient Talmudists but also through the commentary of **Rabbi Selomo** <note>Also known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note>. For he, explaining this passage in Isaiah, teaches that the aforementioned words of Isaiah and Micah are to be taken spiritually. For he explains them thus: <note>original Hebrew: והיה באחרית הימים לפי שיכלו הפושעים כמו שאמר למעלה נכון יהיה כל הענין עד לכו ונלכה באור יהוה כי נטשת חנני מסך הדיבור אל השכינה כי כל מה שנטשת את עמך בעונם היה כי מלאו וכל הענין כל הפרשיות סומכות זו על זו עד אשירה נא כשיכלו הפושעים ההם נכון מתוקן בראש ההרים בהר שהוא ראש לכל ההרים בחשיבות ונשא מגבעות יגדל יהיה נס שעושה בו מסיני סיני וכרמל ותבור וכולו</note> "And it shall come to pass in the end of days—that is, after the wicked have failed or after the sinners have been consumed, as was said earlier by Isaiah 1 when he says, 'And he shall crush the wicked and sinners together, and those who forsake God shall fail or be consumed'—the mountain shall be prepared. The whole passage follows this way until the words: 'Come and let us walk in the light of God.' I judge that the prophet's meaning refers to the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>. For the fact that the people were forsaken was caused by their sins, until the point where he says: 'They are filled.' And all things contained there, and all the chapters, are linked together until 'I will now sing.' Therefore, in the end—or the finality of days—when the sinners stumble, God will act kindly toward them, and the mountain of God will be prepared at the head of the mountains—that is, on the mountain that is the head of all mountains in terms of importance—and it shall be raised above the hills. This means that God will be magnified by a sign or miracle that will occur there, greater than the signs or miracles of Mount Sinai, Carmel, and Tabor." These are his words. Then, the same Rabbi, continuing the exposition of the prophet's words, says: "And many peoples shall go—that is, every nation will encourage one another with many words and exhort them, saying: 'Come to the great courtyard,

<column-break/>

which is in Jerusalem, because there are the judgments of the Lord. For out of Zion the law shall go forth to all nations. And the mountain itself shall judge between the nations, and shall rebuke their controversies and discords. And it shall say: "Why do you need weapons any longer to fight one another?" And they shall flow—that is, they shall gather themselves and draw themselves to him, like rivers—namely all the nations.'" Thus far Rabbi Selomo. Here he clearly asserts that the mountain of the house of the Lord was to be elevated above the mountains and hills not in terms of physical location, but rather in terms of dignity and the greatness of the sign or miracle to be performed there.

Finally, if one carefully inspects what he says—"And the mountain itself shall judge between the nations, and rebuke their controversies and discords; and it shall say: 'Why do you need weapons any longer to fight one another?'"—it will be plainly seen that he speaks of a *rational* mountain—that is, of the Messiah, who is called a "mountain"—and not of a terrestrial and unthinking mountain. **Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra** <note>A significant 12th-century Spanish-Jewish scholar and philosopher.</note> affirms this much more clearly in his commentary on Micah 4, explaining the same passage as follows: "And they shall flow to him," as if to say, "they shall run to him." And from this place until the end of the book, the prophet speaks regarding the matter of the Messiah, and of the impious who will act wickedly "at the heels of the Messiah" <note>This refers to the *Ikvei ha-Mashiach*, a Jewish concept regarding the period of great social and spiritual turmoil immediately preceding the Messiah's arrival.</note>—that is, after the Messiah or against his successors, as our Teachers have said. "And the Messiah shall judge between many peoples." These are the words of Rabbi Abraham.

The Messiah, therefore, is that mountain of whom these prophets speak, who was to be elevated above the "heads of the mountains"—that is, above the holy fathers. Furthermore, that the Messiah is called a mountain <margin>The Messiah is called a mountain.</margin> and the holy fathers (from whose seed he was to come) are called mountains, is found in the *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>An ancient midrashic collection of interpretations on the Book of Genesis.</note>—that is, in the exposition of the book of Genesis—concerning the statement in Genesis 28: "And Jacob went out from Beersheba." There it is said: "I will lift up my eyes to the mountains, from whence comes my help." This is what is written in Zechariah 4: "Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel?" This "great mountain" is the Messiah. And why does he call him a "great mountain"? Because he is greater than the fathers <note>The "fathers" or patriarchs refer to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.</note>, as it is said in Isaiah 52: "Behold, my servant shall understand; he shall be elevated and exalted, and shall be very high." This is the Messiah, who shall be elevated more than Abraham (of whom it is said in Genesis 14: "I will lift up my hands to the Lord"), and exalted more than Moses (of whom it is said in Numbers 11: "Because you say to me: Carry them in your bosom"), and shall be higher than the ministering Angels (of whom it is said in Ezekiel 1: "And their height was great"). Because of this, it is said in Zechariah 4: "Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel?" And why does it say "before Zerubbabel"? Because he is to come forth from Zerubbabel. And why does it say "unto equity"? Because he himself is to come to rebuke with equity, as it is said in Isaiah 11: "And he shall judge the poor with justice, and rebuke with equity the meek of the earth." 

Another exposition: "I will lift up my eyes to the mountains, from whence comes my help." On the day when the Holy and Blessed God sits in judgment with Israel, they will look to the fathers so that they may speak for them; but there will be no father to rescue his son, nor any to deliver his brother. And this <margin>The Saints are called mountains.</margin> is: "I will lift up my eyes to the mountains." These are the fathers. As it is said in Micah 6: "Hear, O mountains, the Lord's controversy." Thus far the tradition. From which it is clear that both the Messiah and the holy fathers are rightly called "mountains."

### CHAPTER IV.

->Regarding the third objection of the Jews: That Jesus of Nazareth was not the Messiah, because all nations did not flow to him.<-

->**GALATINUS.**<-

Concerning their third objection, from which they conclude that our Lord Jesus of Nazareth was not the Messiah because all nations did not "flow" to him, this response is given: The Hebrew word <term>all</term> <note>original Hebrew: כֹּל, transliterated as "Col"</note>, which is the same as "every," "each," "the whole," or "the universal," is not taken as strictly by the prophets and theologians as it is by the logicians. Although many examples of this can be found in Holy Scripture, it is enough to bring forward a few. For in the Second Book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Samuel in modern Bibles.</note>, chapter 16, we read: <term>And Absalom went in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel</term> <note>original Hebrew: וַיָּבֹא אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶל פִּלַגְשֵׁי אָבִיו לְעֵינֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל</note>. And again in chapter 17 of the same book: <term>And Absalom and every man of Israel said: The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel</term> <note>original Hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם וְכָל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל טוֹבָה עֲצַת חוּשַׁי הָאַרְכִּי מֵעֲצַת אֲחִיתֹפֶל</note>. Behold, then, how the Scripture uses this word "all" in both places. Yet no one would be so foolish as to say that not a single person of Israel was missing there, or that every single person saw Absalom when he committed that outrage, or that every single man approved the counsel of Hushai the Archite. For although the Scripture says "all Israel" and "every man," it is reasonable to believe that far more people of Israel were absent than were present, considering those who were with David and those who remained in all the borders of Israel. This is also clearly evident from the words of Hushai himself, when he said to Absalom in the same place: "Gather to yourself all Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba." Also in Psalm 42, it is said: <term>All Your waves and Your billows have passed over me</term> <note>original Hebrew: כָּל מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ</note>. And in Psalm 118: <term>All nations surrounded me; in the name of the Lord I will cut them off</term> <note>original Hebrew: כָּל גּוֹיִם סְבָבוּנִי בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה כִּי אֲמִילַם</note>. In these cases, a person would be considered of unsound mind (in my opinion) if he asserted that every single wave and billow that God possesses—whether of tribulations or of the sea—had passed over David or anyone else, or if he said that every nation in the entire world (with none missing) had surrounded him. Therefore, when

<column-break/>

the Scripture speaks in this way, the word "all" is very often understood not to mean every single individual, but rather "many." Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi, a medieval grammarian and commentator.</note> explains this excellently in his *Book of Roots* <note>original: "Sefer Shorashim"</note>, saying: <term>all</term> (*col*) is a word that encompasses individuals, but sometimes refers only to a part of a multitude. As in Genesis 41: <term>And all the earth came to Egypt</term> <note>original Hebrew: וְכָל הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה</note>. And again in chapter 24: <term>And all the goods of his master were in his hand</term> <note>original Hebrew: וְכָל טוּב אֲדֹנָיו בְּיָדוֹ</note>. Likewise in 4 Kings 8 <note>2 Kings 8 in modern Bibles.</note>: <term>And he took a gift in his hand, even all the good things of Damascus</term> <note>original Hebrew: וַיִּקַּח מִנְחָה בְּיָדוֹ וְכָל טוּב דַּמֶּשֶׂק</note>. These are the words of Rabbi Kimhi. The same is also clearly evident from the *Midrash Shir HaShirim*—that is, the commentary on the Song of Songs—where, on that verse in chapter 2, "The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills," it is said: "The 'mountains' here are nothing but idolatry." This is also what is said in Hosea chapter 4: "They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills." Rabbi Yoden and Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: "The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills—this is the King Messiah. For in the hour when he comes, he shall say to Israel: 'In this month you shall be redeemed.' But they will say to him: 'Our master, King Messiah, when shall we be redeemed? Did not the Holy and Blessed God swear that He would make us serve 70 nations?' He, however, will give them two answers, saying: 'One of you was taken captive among the Sarmatians, and another in Africa; it is just as if all of you had been taken captive.' Not only this, but also this wicked kingdom—that is, the Roman Empire—enrolls in its service <note>original: "in tyrocinio suo"</note> people from all the nations of the world, and from every one of them. Thus, a Cuthæan comes and presses you into service; a Saracen comes and presses you into service; an Ethiopian comes and presses you into service; one from Persia comes and presses you into service, until every nation has pressed you into service and made you serve. Therefore, it is as if you had served 70 nations. And in this time, namely at Passover, you shall be redeemed. Just as it was said in Exodus 12." This is the tradition. From these things, therefore, it is clear that this Hebrew word <term>all</term> (*col*) is frequently used not for each and every one, but for many. Indeed, this way of speaking is commonly used by everyone. For when a large part of the people of a city goes to some spectacle, we say that the "whole city" or "all its people," or even the "whole world," has flocked there. We have shown that this manner of speaking is found throughout Holy Scripture. That it should be understood this way in this passage is clearly shown by the words of Isaiah himself. For when he had said, "And all nations shall flow to him," he immediately added, as if explaining himself: "And many people shall go." Hence Micah, who prophesied at the same time as Isaiah, relating these same words, shows that Isaiah spoke in this sense, saying in his fourth chapter: <term>And peoples shall flow to him</term> <note>original Hebrew: וְנָהֲרוּ עָלָיו עַמִּים</note> and <term>many nations shall go</term> <note>original Hebrew: וְהָלְכוּ גּוֹיִם רַבִּים</note>. And note that wherever the word <term>peoples</term> <note>Hebrew: amim</note> is used in the plural among the Hebrews, it is always understood to mean the Gentiles. From these things which have been said, it is openly clear that this saying of Isaiah which they oppose to us—"And all nations shall flow to him"—should be understood as referring to many nations.

He who belongs to the unity of the Church approaches this house of God. In this house, Christ himself—the "mountain of mountains" and the "holy of holies"—is adored by the faithful. In this house, sins are also forgiven.

<meta>This page continues the argument that the conversion of the Gentiles fulfills Messianic prophecy. # 303 BOOK FIVE 304

[Augu]stine of Africa <note>Saint Augustine (354–430 AD), a foundational Latin Church Father.</note>, and almost countless others, turned the languages, words, and cleverness of arguments—with which they fought most fiercely against our faith in debates before their conversion—toward the utter uprooting of the crime of idolatry, the radical tearing out of human vices, the expansion of the worship of the true God, and the nurturing of virtues in the hearts of both Jews and Gentiles. Therefore, if the Sacred Scripture is understood here spiritually (as it ought to be), we will find beyond doubt that in the days of our Lord Jesus Christ, these kinds of weapons of war were most excellently changed into instruments of agriculture. Consequently, we believe that saying from Isaiah chapter 61 was fulfilled, which had been prophesied long ago regarding Peter and Paul and the others from among the Jews who believed in the Lord Jesus himself as the true Messiah: <note>original Hebrew: ועמדו זרים ורעו צאנכם ובני נכר אכריכם וכרמיכם ואתם כהני יהוה תקראו משרתי אלהינו יאמר לכם חיל גויים תאכלו ובכבודם תתימרו</note> That is: "And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the foreigner shall be your farmers and vinedressers. But you shall be called the Priests of God; it shall be said to you, ‘Ministers of our God.’ You shall eat the strength of the nations, and in their glory or honor you shall be made lords." Just as language and words are often called a sword, spears, and hunting-poles—especially when someone uses them to cause harm, according to that text in Psalm 57: <note>original Hebrew: בני אדם שניהם חנית וחצים ולשונם חרב חדה</note> That is: "Sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword." And again in Psalm 55 according to the Hebrew truth (but 54 according to our edition <note>Galatinus notes the difference between the Hebrew Masoretic numbering and the Latin Vulgate numbering of the Psalms.</note>): <margin>That is: "His words were softened above oil, and they are hunting-spears." <note>original Hebrew: רכו דבריו משמן והמה פתיחות</note></margin> That is: "His words were made softer than oil, and yet they are spears." <margin>Because of the sword and arrow.</margin> Likewise in Proverbs chapter 25: <margin>A man answering against his neighbor with false testimony.</margin> <note>original Hebrew: שנון איש עונה ברעהו עד שקר</note> That is: "A club and a sword and a sharp arrow is a man who speaks false witness against his neighbor." So too, language itself and words can, not without reason, be called plowshares, hoes, and sickles, when someone uses them for the instruction of others and for the worship of God.

### CHAPTER VII.

->To the sixth objection: That the Messiah has not yet come because peace without end has not yet arrived.<-

->GALATINUS.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop-cap letter S depicting a scholar seated at a desk with books.</image-desc>
Their sixth objection is also easily refuted through their own scriptures. For they infer that the Messiah has not yet come from what the prophet says: "Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore," because peace without end has not yet come to the world; even though the words of the prophet himself seem to sound as if a peace that will last forever must happen in the days of the Messiah. One must respond to them according to how these words are explained in the <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism.</note> by their wise men. First, it should be noted that this word *od* <note>original Hebrew: עוד</note>, which we translate as "anymore" or "further," although it is sometimes and rarely taken to mean "never" or "ever" (as in that saying from Genesis chapter 8: "I will not *anymore* [od] add to curse the earth"; and again in chapter 9: "And there shall not *anymore* [od] be water for a flood...

<column-break/>

<page-num>304</page-num>
<header>THE FIFTH [BOOK].</header>
<meta>catchword: nation</meta>

<margin>A</margin> ...for a flood"), it nevertheless frequently signifies a very brief time. This is taught by <term>Rabbi Kimhi</term> <note>David Kimhi (1160–1235), also known as Radak, a famous medieval Hebrew grammarian and commentator.</note> in the *Book of Roots* <note>Sefer HaShorashim, a dictionary of the Hebrew language.</note>, saying: "It happens that this word *od* (that is, 'anymore') signifies a small amount of time." As when it is said in Proverbs chapter 31: <note>original Hebrew: תני שכר לאובד ויין למרי נפש ישתה וישכח רישו ועמלו לא יזכר עוד</note> That is: "Give strong drink to the one who is perishing, and wine to him who is bitter in soul. He will drink and forget his poverty, and of his labor he will not record *anymore* [od]." For "anymore" there does not mean "forever" or "eternally," but only as long as the wine remains in him. Likewise, that saying in 2 Kings chapter 6: <margin>B</margin> <note>original Hebrew: ולא יספו עוד גדודי ארם לבוא בארץ ישראל</note> That is: "And the bands of Syria did not add to come *anymore* [od] into the land of Israel"—meaning, in that specific time. Likewise, it sometimes happens that *od* signifies *aden* <note>original Hebrew: עדן</note>, which means "still" or "yet." As in that text of Psalm 88: "Free among the dead, like the slain sleeping in the grave whom you have not remembered *od* (that is, yet)." <margin>C</margin> As if to say: you have not yet been mindful of them until the time comes in which the memory of the dead shall occur, so that they may rise again. And thus also is that text in Job chapter 2: "Do you *still* [od] retain your perfection?" Thus far Rabbi Kimhi. From his words it is clear enough that this Hebrew word *od* is indeed rarely taken for "ever" or "longer," but is frequently used for a determined or even a small amount of time. But since the Jews—as is their <margin>D</margin> custom—still contentiously object despite what has been said, we must again turn some of their own arrows back against them. Let one of these be what is found in Genesis chapter 35: <note>original Hebrew: ויאמר לו אלהים שמך יעקב לא יקרא שמך עוד יעקב כי אם ישראל יהיה שמך</note> That is: "And God said to him, 'Your name is Jacob; your name shall not be called Jacob *anymore* [od], but Israel shall be your name.'" Here let Jewish perversity look more sharply: because just as it is written <margin>E</margin> in Isaiah, "Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war *anymore* [od]," so it is said here, "Your name shall not be called *anymore* [od] Jacob." Yet immediately in that same chapter, he is called Jacob eight times, and Israel only three times. Another "arrow" is that which is read in 1 Samuel chapter 7 regarding the Philistines: <note>original Hebrew: ולא יספו עוד לבא בגבול ישראל</note> That is: "And they did not add to come *anymore* [od] into the border of Israel. And the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of <margin>F</margin> Samuel." However, how that "anymore" is to be understood there is shown by what is said in chapter 13 of the same book: That when Samuel was dead and Saul was reigning, the Philistines went up to the land of Israel. For thus it is read there: "And the Philistines gathered together to fight against Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen or soldiers, and people like the sand which is on the seashore. And they went up and camped in Michmash before Beth-aven." From all these things, therefore, it is established that this Hebrew word *od* (anymore) <margin>G</margin> does not always imply eternity (as the Jews rave), but sometimes a long duration of time, and many times a very short time. From this it is clearly evident that in the time of our Lord Jesus Christ, this saying of Isaiah was fulfilled: "Nation shall not lift up..."

<summary>Galatinus argues that the weapons of pagan rhetoric were converted into tools for Christian teaching, and uses Hebrew linguistics (specifically the word 'od') to argue that prophecies of "no more war" can refer to specific periods of peace rather than an immediate, eternal cessation of all conflict.</summary>

[nation shall not lift up] sword against nation, nor shall they learn war anymore. <note>original Latin: "contra gentem gladium, nec discent ultra bellum"</note> "Anymore," that is, for a significant period of time. For Christ was born in a time of quite long-lasting peace, while Augustus was ruling the world. On account of which, it ought to be a doubt to no one that in such a long-lasting peace, many weapons of war were converted into hoes, scythes, and plowshares.

## CHAPTER VIII. ##

->Regarding the seventh objection: that the Messiah has not yet come because wild beasts have not yet abandoned the eating of meat, nor, having set aside all ferocity, have they lain down with gentle animals.<-

->GALATINUS.<-

That point which they also object to us from the words of the same prophet—namely, that they have not yet seen wild beasts abandon the eating of meat, nor lie down with domestic and gentle animals after setting aside all ferocity, from which they conclude the Messiah has not yet come—we refute this through their own writings. We say that Holy Scripture very often speaks mystically and parabolically, and even most frequently metaphorically, by calling things by the names of others, or even calling men by the names of irrational creatures according to what their actions, customs, or qualities require. It even does this to God himself, having respect for his operations. Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides (1138–1204), the preeminent Jewish philosopher.</note> explains this excellently in the book *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "More hannebochim"</note> near its beginning, as we saw more extensively in the sixth chapter of the first book of this work. Moreover, that the aforementioned words of Isaiah are to be understood differently than they say they should be understood is held by the same Rabbi Moses the Egyptian in his *Sentences* <note>original: "hallacoth," referring to the Mishneh Torah.</note> on the Book of Judges, speaking thus: "Let it not climb upon your heart <note>A literal translation of a Hebrew idiom meaning 'Do not imagine' or 'Do not think.'</note> that in the days of the Messiah anything from the way of this world ought to fail, or that something from the works of the six days [of creation] ought to be renewed; but rather that the world should go along its accustomed path." Therefore, what was said in Isaiah chapter 11, "And the wolf shall dwell with the ram," and so on, the sense is that Israel shall dwell confidently with the wicked of the age, who are compared to lions, wolves, and leopards. Just as it is said in Jeremiah chapter 5: <note>original Hebrew: הכם אריה מיער זאב ערבות ישדדם נמר שקד על עריהם</note> 

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin>
That is: "A lion from the forest has struck them; a wolf of the woods or the plains shall devastate them; a leopard watches or lies in wait near their cities." After the sinners have been consumed—about whom it is said in Isaiah 1, <note>original Hebrew: ועוזבי יהוה יכלו</note> that is, "And those who forsake the Lord shall be consumed"—and after everyone has been converted to the law of truth, then they shall not plunder nor destroy, but shall eat what is lawful in tranquility with Israel. As it was said by Isaiah: "And the lion like the ox shall eat straw." And thus in this manner, <margin>B</margin> the words written about the Messiah are parables. In the time of the King Messiah, however, it will be known regarding everything what thing and for what reason the parables existed, and what was signified through them. For the Sages said that there will be no difference between this age and the days of the Messiah, except for the subjection to kingdoms alone. All these things says the same Rabbi. The aforementioned points also take no small amount of strength from the Chaldean translation <note>The Targum, an Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible.</note> of Rabbi Jonathan son of Uzziel, whom it is considered a sin among them to contradict. For regarding that verse: "And a rod <margin>C</margin> shall go out from the stem of Jesse, and a branch, or a plant, or a shoot from his roots shall bear fruit, or sprout," he translated it thus in Chaldean: <note>original Aramaic: ויפוק מלכא מכנוהי, דישי ומשיחא מבני בנוהי יתרבי</note> That is: "And a king shall go out from the sons of Jesse, and the Messiah shall be nourished from his sons' sons." And regarding that verse: "And justice shall be the belt of his loins, and faith the girdle or loincloth of his kidneys," he interpreted it thus: <note>original Aramaic: ויהון צדקיא סחור סחור ליה ומהימניא יהון קריבין ליה</note> That is: "And the righteous shall be all around him, and those acting faithfully shall draw near to him." And regarding this also: "And <margin>D</margin> the wolf shall dwell with the ram," with the rest, he explained it thus: <note>original Aramaic: ביומוהי דמשיחא דישראל יסגי שלמא בארעא</note> That is: "In the days of the Messiah of Israel, peace shall be multiplied in the land." This interpretation indeed does two things against Jewish impiety. First, that the words of Isaiah themselves were spoken concerning the Messiah—for he expresses his name twice there. Second, that they are to be understood spiritually. <margin>E</margin> The glosses of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the famous French rabbi and commentator.</note> strongly support this interpretation as well, which explains these same words in this way: "The King Messiah will not judge by the sight of his eyes, but with the wisdom of the Holy God—blessed be He—which will be in him, he will know and understand who was guilty and who was innocent. And he will argue in equity, that is, with a quiet and tender tongue. And he will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; this is to be understood according to the Targum, that is, according to the Chaldean edition which is thus: <note>original Aramaic: ויקטל חייבי ארעא במימר פומיה</note> that is, "And he will <margin>F</margin> blot out the guilty from the earth by the word of his mouth. And by the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked," that is, "And by the speech of his lips the wicked man shall be dead. And justice shall be the belt of his loins," that is, "And the righteous shall be all around him, that is, adhering to him like a belt." These are the words of Rabbi Solomon. In the aforementioned <margin>Men are called by the names of beasts.</margin> manner of speaking, men are very frequently called by the names of wild beasts, cattle, birds, and reptiles in many places of Holy Scripture. For as one reads in Genesis 49, that patriarch Jacob, blessing his sons, called Judah <margin>G</margin> a "lion’s whelp"; <note>original Hebrew: גור אריה</note> and Issachar a "bony or strong donkey"; <note>original Hebrew: חמור גרם</note> and Dan a "serpent upon the way, a horned snake upon the path"; <note>original Hebrew: נחש עלי דרך</note> and Naphtali a "hind let loose"; <note>original Hebrew: אילה שלוחה</note> and Benjamin a "wolf that ravins." <note>original Hebrew: זאב יטרף</note>

of Israel." Thus said the Lord God. **CAPNIO:** The Jews, with a stubborn grip, as if faithless to this word of Ezekiel, cling to it because through him the Lord said, "And I will gather them into their own land, and I will not leave any of them there"—meaning, not a single person. Since, therefore (they say), not all of Israel was gathered into their own land in the time of Ezra, such that no one remained among the nations, it is clearly evident that this prophecy has not yet been fulfilled. **GALATINUS:** Ezra himself clearly shows them to be both speakers of falsehood and ungrateful to God in this matter, when at the end of the second chapter of his book and the beginning of the third he says: <note>original: "וישבו הכהנים והלוים ומן העם והמשוררים והשוערים והנתינים בעריהם וכל ישראל בעריהם"</note> that is, "And the priests and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the <term>Nethinim</term> <note>Temple servants or assistants of the Levites.</note> lived in their cities. And all Israel was in their cities. And the people were gathered as one man to Jerusalem." Wherefore even that saying from Isaiah chapter 11, which they frequently object against us, was fulfilled: <note>original: "ויוסף אדני שנית ידו לקנות את שאר עמו"</note> that is, "And the Lord shall set his hand a second time to possess the remnant of his people, which shall be left from the Assyrians, along with the rest." For the Lord extended his hand to possess them the first time when he led them out of Egypt. But the second time was when he brought them back from the Babylonian captivity. Finally, he has never hidden his face from those who believed in him since he poured out the Holy Spirit upon them on the day of Pentecost, as is clearly hinted at the end of the aforementioned words of Ezekiel.

### CHAPTER X.

#### Regarding the ninth objection of the Jews: That the Messiah has not yet come because the third temple has not yet been built.

### CAPNIO

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'D' featuring a building within a landscape and figures in the background.</image-desc>
They also often oppose us with what is read in Zechariah chapter 6, in this manner: <note>original: "כה אמר יהוה צבאות לאמר הנה איש צמח שמו ומתחתיו יצמח ובנה את היכל יהוה והוא יבנה את היכל יהוה והוא ישא הוד וישב ומשל על כסאו והיה כהן על כסאו ועצת שלום תהיה בין שניהם"</note>

<column-break/>

<page-num>310</page-num>
...and he shall rule upon his throne. And the counsel of peace shall be between the two of them. And a little further down: <note>original: "והיה אם שמוע תשמעון בקול יהוה אלהיכם"</note> That is, "And it shall come to pass, if you will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God." From these things, therefore, and from the words of Ezekiel in the last chapter saying that Jerusalem and the Temple ought to be rebuilt in the time of the Messiah, the younger Jews argue thus: Since these things were not fulfilled in the time of Jesus of Nazareth, nor has a third temple been built to this day, it is clearly established that neither was Jesus of Nazareth the Messiah, nor has the Messiah himself yet come. **GALATINUS:** A solution to these words of Zechariah is found in <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Commonly known as Rashi (1040–1105), the most influential medieval Jewish commentator.</note>, who explains them thus: "Branch is his name" refers to the Messiah. "He shall bear the glory," that is, he shall take up the horn <note>A symbol of power or kingship.</note>. "Between the two of them," that is, between Judah and Israel. And he says this entire building refers to the Second House <note>The Second Temple, built after the Babylonian exile.</note>. "And it shall come to pass if you will diligently obey," that is: "this deed or this thing shall be done for you, if you will diligently obey." These are the words of Rabbi Solomon. From which an argument is held that the Messiah was to come during the time of the Second Temple. Moreover, that the aforementioned words of Zechariah are understood to be about the Messiah is clearly evident through the <term>Targum</term> <note>The Aramaic translation and interpretation of the Hebrew Bible.</note>, that is, through the Chaldaic translation, which has the same words thus: <note>original Aramaic: "אמר יהוה צבאות למימר הא גברא משיחא שמיה עתיד דיתגלי ויתרבי ויבני ית היכלא דיהוה והוא יטול זיו ויתיב וישלוט על לורסוהי ויהי כהן רב על בורסוהי ומלכא ושלמא יהא בין תרויהון"</note> That is, "The Lord of hosts said, saying: Behold the man, Messiah is his name. It is future that he shall reveal himself, and he shall be increased. And he shall build the temple of God. And he himself shall take up the splendor, and shall sit, and shall rule upon his throne. And he shall be a great priest upon his throne. And the counsel of peace shall be between the two of them." And below: <note>original: "ויהי אם קבלא תקבלון למימרא דיהוה אלהכון"</note> That is, "And it shall be (namely, this) if you will truly receive the word of the Lord your God." Thus says the Targum. Where by "this word of the Lord God" (as has been proven more extensively elsewhere), the Messiah himself is understood. Furthermore, that a third temple was not 
<margin>The temple is not to be built a third time.</margin>
to be built is proved in many ways through their own scriptures. For in the <term>Bereshit Ketanna</term> <note>The "Lesser Genesis," a midrashic commentary.</note>, that is, the minor exposition of the book of Genesis, we find it written in this manner: Rabbi Abba said: "From the beginning of the creation of the world, the Holy and Blessed God saw the house of the sanctuary built and destroyed. And built indeed: just as it is said in Genesis 1: <note>original: "בראשית ברא אלהים את השמים ואת הארץ"</note> That is, 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.' Behold, it is built. Just as it is said in Isaiah chapter 51: 'That he might plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth.' But destroyed, when it is said: <note>original: "והארץ היתה תהו ובהו"</note> That is, 'And the earth was without form and void.' Behold, it is destroyed. Just as it was said in Jeremiah 4: 'I beheld the earth, and lo, it was without form and void.' It follows: <note>original: "ויאמר אלהים יהי אור ויהי אור"</note> That is, 'And God said: let there be light, and there was light.' Behold, it is built and perfected for the future. Just as it is said in Isaiah 60: <note>original: "קומי אורי כי בא אורך וכבוד יהוה עליך זרח"</note> That is, 'Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of God has risen upon you.'" It is also written thus in the <term>Bereshit Rabbah</term> <note>The "Great Genesis," a major homiletic midrash.</note>, that is, in the great exposition of the book of Genesis, upon that saying in Genesis chapter 27: "See, the smell of my son..."

...my sons are like a full field, which the Lord has blessed! <note>A reference to Isaac’s blessing of Jacob in Genesis 27:27.</note> Here he teaches that God showed him the house of the sanctuary built, destroyed, and built again. It was "built" in the phrase: *See the smell of my son*. Just as it is written in Numbers 28: *You shall keep a sweet-smelling savor*. It was "destroyed" in the phrase: *Like a full field*. Just as it is written in Micah, chapter 3: *Therefore because of you, Zion shall be plowed like a field*. But it is "built and perfected for the future" in the phrase: *Which the Lord has blessed*. Just as it is written in Psalm 132: *For there the Lord commanded the blessing and life forevermore*, or into eternity. Also in the book *Succa*, that is, the Book of Tabernacles, it is read as follows: *Rabbi Ezra* said, it is written: <note>original Hebrew: "ואת הצפוני ארחיק מעליכם והדחתיו אל ארץ ציה ושממה את פניו אל הים הקדמוני וסופו אל הים האחרון" — Joel 2:20</note> that is, *And I will remove the northern one far from you, and drive him into a parched and desolate land, with his face toward the eastern sea and his back toward the western sea.* And I will remove the northern one from you. This is the **evil inclination** <term>ietzer hara: the innate human impulse toward selfishness or evil</term>, which hides in the heart of man. *And I will drive him into a parched land*, that is, to a place where the sons of Adam are not found to dwell. *His face toward the Eastern sea*, because he set his eyes upon the first sanctuary and destroyed it, and killed the wise men who were there. *And his back toward the Western sea*, because he set his eyes upon the second sanctuary and overturned it, and slew the wise men who were in it. From these traditions, it is sufficiently and clearly hinted that a third temple was not to be built on earth. This is held more clearly by Jeremiah, speaking in chapter 7: <note>original Hebrew: "הטיבו דרכיכם ומעלליכם ואשכנה אתכם במקום הזה : אל תבטחו לכם אל דברי השקר לאמר היכל יהוה היכל יהוה היכל יהוה המה"</note> This is: *Make your ways and your actions good. And I will make you dwell in this place. Do not trust in lying or false words, to say: The Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord are these.* Because it is entirely false that a third temple of the Lord is to be built on earth, since there ought to be no other than the first and second temples of the Lord. This is confirmed in the book **Separation** <term>Geziruth: likely referring to a division of the Talmud or a specific rabbinic commentary</term>, in the chapter *Beth hammai*, where it is said regarding these same words of Jeremiah: "What is it that is written, The Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord? That is the first and second sanctuary." Therefore, through what has been said, it is openly shown that the temple will not be rebuilt a third time, nor can Jewish perversity prove by any evident reason that it must be rebuilt a third time; since, as has been made clear enough from the premises, there were only to be two temples on earth. Namely, the first which was constructed by Solomon and overthrown by Nebuchadnezzar; and the second, which was founded under Zerubbabel and finally destroyed by Titus. <margin>The third temple is to be placed in heaven.</margin> The third temple, however, is to be placed not on earth, but in heaven, and in the Jerusalem above, as the ancient Talmudists handed down. This is proven in many places in the Talmud itself. For in the *Great Genesis* <note>original: Beresith rabba, a homiletic commentary on the Book of Genesis</note>, that is, in the exposition of the book of Genesis upon that which is written in chapter 28 of the same book: <note>original Hebrew: "ויירא ויאמר מה נורא המקום הזה אין זה כי אם בית אלהים וזה שער השמים"</note> that is, *And he was afraid and said, How terrible is this place. This is none other than the house of God.*

And this is the gate of heaven. Thus it is read: Our master Joshua son of Nun said, on that day when the death of Moses approached, the Lord lifted him up to the highest heaven, and showed him the house of his reward, and what was to come to him. And Mercy stood by him and said: "Moses, I bring you good news, in which you will greatly rejoice. Look toward the throne of divine mercy and see." And Moses looked, and saw the Holy and Blessed God building the house of the sanctuary with His own hand out of precious stones and pearls. Between stone and stone He placed the glory of the **Divine Presence** <gloss>Hasschechina: the indwelling presence of God</gloss>, or rather the beauty or ornament, more noble indeed than pearls. And when the Messiah and Aaron saw him, they knew that the Holy and Blessed God had taught him His great name. Therefore, the Messiah and Aaron said to him, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." For unless the Holy and Blessed God had taught him His name, he could not have entered with them into the Divine Presence. And so Moses asked the Messiah son of David, saying, "Speak to me, I pray.
