If you hear (He says) I will not put it upon you. But if you do not hear, I will put every disease upon you, even though I am your physician.*" This is the tradition.

From all these things it clearly appears that all God's promises made to the Israelite people in the past were always conditional. That is, *if* those to whom some good had been promised—turning away from evil and persevering in good—obeyed Him, even if the Scripture sometimes did not explicitly state such a condition. For then the condition itself was to be understood just as if it had been explicitly stated. Otherwise Jacob and Moses, who after they had received such firm security from God feared greatly, could in no way be excused from the vice of unfaithfulness and unbelief. To even dream such a thing about such holy men is a sacrilege. Since these things are so, it stands clearer than the midday sun that all the promises made to the Jews concerning the Messiah and their salvation were conditional: namely, if they would receive him and obey him as God their Savior. The cause, therefore, why the Jews were not redeemed and saved through the Messiah is none other than because they did not receive him, nor would they listen to him, but rather denied him and killed him, according to that saying of the Psalmist in the 81st Psalm: **And my people did not hear...**

The haters of the Lord would have lied to Him, and their time would be forever.** <note>original Hebrew from Psalm 81:11-15: "לקולי וישראל לא אבה לי... ועליהם אשיב ידי : משנאי יהוה יכחשו לו ויהי עתם לעולם"</note>
*that is, And my people did not hear my voice, and Israel did not want me. And I let them go into the thought, or the stubbornness of their heart; they will go in their own counsels. ## CHAPTER II.

->*That very few of the Jews were to be saved, while the rest were to be killed, destroyed, and scattered.*<-

### CAPNIO.

<margin>A</margin>Although it is easily apparent from what you have said that the promise made to the Jews by God concerning their salvation in the time of the Messiah was conditional—namely, if they were to receive the Messiah himself and obey him. (For which reason, if the greatest part of them through Christ's coming and passion were not only spiritually unsaved but even temporally lost and scattered, it ought to seem the least bit strange, since they neither received the true Messiah himself nor wished to hear him, but rather killed him with a most shameful death.) Yet, so that their faithlessness may be more fully convicted, you would do something very fitting to our purpose if you proved from their own scriptures that not all Jews, but only a very few, were to be saved through the Messiah.

<margin>G. A. L.</margin>This is first of all clearly demonstrated through their tradition, which is placed in the book *Sanhedrin* <note>A major volume of the Talmud dealing with legal and judicial matters.</note> at the end of the chapter *Helec*: where it is read thus word-for-word: Rabbi <term>שמא</term> <note>Sammai: A famous first-century BCE Jewish scholar and founder of a school of law.</note> Sammai said, it is said in Jeremiah chapter 3: <term>ולקחתי אתכם אחד מעיר ושנים ממשפחה</term> <note>original: "And I will take you, one from a city and two from a family."</note> This is, **And I will take you, one from a city, and two from a family.** <note>Jeremiah 3:14</note> And again it is said, <term>והבאתי אתכם ציון</term> <note>original: "And I will lead you into Zion."</note> that is, **And I will lead you into Zion.** Therefore, their exit from Egypt was measured against their entry into the land. Just as their entry into the land was two out of six hundred thousand <note>Referring to the biblical account where only Joshua and Caleb among the original generation from Egypt entered the Promised Land.</note>: where the gloss of Rabbi Solomon says, "The rest (he says) died in the three days of darkness." <margin>F</margin> Rabba said, "And so it shall be in the days of the Messiah: as it is said in the second chapter of Hosea," <term>וענתה שמה כימי נעוריה וכיום עלותה מארץ מצרים</term> <note>original: "And she shall respond there as in the days of her youth, and as in the day of her coming up from the land of Egypt."</note> This is, **And she shall respond, or sing there, as in the days of her youth, or childhood, and as in the days of her ascent from the land of Egypt.** <note>Hosea 2:15</note> This is the tradition. From which it is clearly held that just as out of six hundred thousand Jews who had gone out from Egypt, none entered into the land of promise except only two, Joshua and Caleb: so also in the days of the Messiah (as tradition proves through the prophet Hosea) there were only two out of six hundred thousand Jews to be saved, as if one from a city and two from a family (as had been prophesied by Jeremiah) were to be taken, while all the rest were to be utterly destroyed and scattered.

<column-break/>

Nor does the aforementioned destruction of the Jews occurring in his days detract from Christ in any way; rather, it procures the greatest faith in him among all who are not ignorant of the truth: just as the ancient fathers of the Jews (by the testimony of their *Talmud*) understood the words of the prophets. For it is read in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter that begins <term>דיני ממונות</term> <note>Dine Mammonoth: "Judgments of Money," a section of the Talmud dealing with civil law and procedures.</note> *Dine mammonoth*, that is, judgments of riches: <margin>B</margin> That the sons of Rabbi <term>חייא</term> <note>Hiia: A third-century sage in the land of Israel known for his piety and teaching.</note> *Hiia* sat before the Rabbi at a banquet: and when they wished to say nothing of the secrets of the sacred scripture which they had received from their father, the Rabbi said to the servant: "Increase the wine for them, so that they will speak." When this had been done, one of them opened his mouth and said: "The son of David will not come until the two houses of the fathers of Israel have failed, which are the head of the captivity that was in Babylon, and the <term>נשיא</term> <note>Nasi: The Hebrew title for the Prince or Patriarch who led the Jewish community in the Land of Israel.</note> *Nasi*, that is, the Prince who is in the land of Israel." As it is said in Isaiah 8: <margin>Tradition of the sons of R. Hiia.</margin> <margin>C</margin> <term>והיה למקדש ולאבן נגף ולצור מכשול לשני בתי ישראל לפח ולמוקש ליושב ירושלם וכשלו בם רבים ונפלו ונשברו ונוקשו ונלכדו צור תעודה חתום תורה בלמדי וחכתי ליהוה המסתיר פניו מבית יעקב וקויתי לו</term> <note>original: "And he shall be for a sanctuary, and for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offense to both houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. And I will wait upon the Lord, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him."</note> This is: **And he shall be for sanctification or preparation, and for a stone of offense, and for a rock of scandal to the two houses of Israel, and for a snare and for a ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And many of them shall stumble, and shall fall, and shall be crushed, and shall be ensnared, and shall be captured.** <margin>D</margin> **Bind the testimony, and seal the law among my disciples. And I will wait for God, hiding his faces from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.** <note>Isaiah 8:14–17</note> The Rabbi said to them, "My sons, you are putting thorns in my eyes." Rabbi Hiia said to him, "Rabbi, let this not be an evil to you. Wine was given in 70, and the secret was given in 70. The wine entered, and the secret came out." <note>This refers to gematria, a system where letters have numerical values. The Hebrew words for wine ("yayin") and secret ("sod") both equal 70, suggesting that wine reveals hidden truths.</note> This is the tradition. But Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi (Radak), a celebrated medieval Jewish grammarian and biblical commentator.</note> upon that part of Isaiah, *And he shall be for a sanctification*, explaining it thus, says: "This is, he shall be a place to which a man shall go so that he may be saved in it." <margin>E</margin> There are also those who explain, *He shall be for a sanctification*, that is, for a preparation: as if he says for the preparation of vengeance, according to that which is said in Jeremiah chapter 12: <term>והקדישם ליום הרגה</term> <note>original: "Prepare them for the day of slaughter."</note> This is: **Sanctify them for the day of killing.** <note>Jeremiah 12:3</note> Thus says Rabbi Kimhi. Concerning this tradition, therefore, it must first be noted that those words of Isaiah, *And he shall be for a sanctification*, along with the rest, were spoken concerning the Messiah. Secondly, concerning the truth of this matter and the meaning of the verse <margin>F</margin> which precedes these words: namely, <term>את יהוה צבאות אותו תקדישו</term> <note>original: "Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself."</note> This is: **Sanctify the God of hosts himself.** <note>Isaiah 8:13</note> Thus says the Chaldaic translation <note>The Targum, an ancient Aramaic paraphrase used to explain the Hebrew Bible.</note> of Rabbi Jonathan: <term>והוא מוראכם והוא מעריצכם והיה למקדש</term> <note>original: "And he shall be your fear, and he shall be your strength, and he shall be for a sanctuary."</note> This is: **And let him be your fear, and he shall be your strengthener. And he shall be for a sanctification;** and so forth. From which it follows necessarily that the Messiah is not only man, but also God. Thirdly, it must be noted moreover that the Messiah was to be a sanctification and preparation not for all, but for some <margin>G</margin> of the Jews—that is, for those alone who believe in him and obey him—that is, so that he might make them holy and prepared for the reception of eternal life and glory. But for the non-believers, who were to be far more numerous, he would be for a manifold destruction and perdition.

<margin>A</margin> ...destiny (as their treachery required) it ought to have been. This is noted when it is said: *And many among them shall stumble,* <note>Isaiah 8:15</note> along with the other things that follow. And for this reason specifically, that Talmudic tradition was introduced in this place. Fourthly, it must also be observed that God was going to reject all the Jews who would not believe in the Messiah, and was going to take away from them the grace of understanding the Scripture, and bestow it upon the disciples of the Messiah themselves. And all this is hinted at when it is said: *Bind the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.* <note>Isaiah 8:16</note> And *I will wait for God, who hides his face from the house of Jacob,* <note>Isaiah 8:17</note> that is, from the Jews. Fifthly, it is also to be noted that this tradition, because it contained great secrets of the Messiah, was held in the greatest secrecy and preserved among the ancient fathers. Sixthly, that no secret remains hidden where wine prevails. <note>A reference to the proverb "In vino veritas," perhaps linking the "secrecy" mentioned above to a lack of sobriety or the revealing of truths.</note> Seventhly, finally, that after the destruction of the head of the Babylonian captivity—which was Zerubbabel and his sons, as well as Mattathias and his own, that is, the Maccabees, whom they call <term>Hashmonai</term> <note>original: חשמונאי; the Hasmoneans</note>—the Messiah was to come. For the Greeks <note>original: יונאי, *Yonai*, referring to the Ionians/Greeks</note> deposed the sons of Zerubbabel and utterly took away the dominion of the Jews from them. Indeed, this can be seen most clearly from the fact that Mattathias and his sons afterwards bravely wrested that dominion from the hand of the Greeks, and were made princes of the Jews until Herod the Ascalonite, who, later rising against them, seized the kingdom from their hands, as we have said more extensively elsewhere. And thus, according to the aforementioned tradition, the two houses of the fathers of Israel ceased, which were the head of the captivity that had returned from Babylon—namely, Zerubbabel and his line—and the princes who were in the land of Israel, who were the Maccabees. Therefore, after the destruction of the Maccabees, in the time of Herod the Ascalonite, who destroyed the Maccabees, it is certain according to this Talmudic tradition both that the Messiah came and that the Jews were destroyed in great part shortly thereafter. It is also certain that few of the Jews were to be saved, except for those who, being converted toward the end of the world, are to perform penance for their sin, according to what Isaiah witnessed in chapter 10, saying: <term>She’ar yashuv bo</term> <note>original: שאר ישוב בו</note> that is, *For if your people Israel were as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall return from it.* <note>Isaiah 10:22</note> Which Rabbi Jonathan translated into the Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note> language thus: *For if your people Israel shall be many, like the sand of the sea, the remnant that has not sinned, or that has repented of sin, shall return.* <note>original: ארי אם יהיה עמך ישראל כחול הימא שאר דלא חטון יתובו מטאתה</note> Furthermore, the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi</note> upon the aforementioned words of Isaiah says: *Even if Israel were like the sand of the sea for multitude, I will refine them like silver, and it shall be reduced to a small amount. The remnant of that small amount shall be converted to good.* To the preceding points, it must also be added that in the book <term>Sanhedrin</term>, in the chapter <term>Helek</term>, <note>A famous section of the Talmud discussing the afterlife and the coming of the Messiah.</note> it is written: *Johanan said: In the generation in which the son of David is to come, the wise teachers shall be diminished. The eyes of the rest, indeed, shall fail in mourning and sighing. And many troubles and harsh decrees shall be renewed against them. For while the first has not yet been put into execution, another will already be coming.* From all of which our purpose is clear.

### CHAPTER III.

->*That the Jews, who were not going to receive the Messiah, were going to lose the understanding of the scriptures, and fall into the deepest ignorance.*<-

504 BOOK IX.
CHAPTER III.

<margin>A</margin> **CAPNIO.** I would like you to show from their own scriptures that which you have already said in the preceding remarks: namely, that the grace of understanding the Scripture was to be taken away from the Jews and bestowed upon the disciples of the Messiah. And especially that those who were not going to receive the Messiah were to lose the understanding of the scriptures entirely. **GALATINUS.** This is clearly held, first, in the book <term>Sanhedrin</term>, in the chapter <margin>B</margin> <term>Helek</term>, where it is read: *Rabbi Judas said: In the generation in which the son of David is to come, the house of preaching shall be for fornication.* (The gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: *that is, the place where the wise teachers used to teach the law*) *and the men of Gazith* (The gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: *that is, the Sanhedrin, or the 70 ordinary judges*) *shall go around from city to city, and no one will have pity on them. And the wisdom of the scribes shall stink, and those who fear to sin shall be rejected. And the face of that generation shall be like a dog* (The gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: <margin>C</margin> *literally, they will be impudent as dogs*) *and truth shall be diminished.* Also, in the book <term>Siphre</term>, <note>An ancient legal commentary on Numbers and Deuteronomy.</note> that saying of Deuteronomy chapter 32 is explained thus: <term>Dor ikkesh u-petaltol halo l’Adonai tigmulu zot am naval v’lo hacham</term>, that is, *A wicked and perverse generation, do you thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?* <note>Deuteronomy 32:5-6</note> *O foolish people,* namely, in those things which have passed. *And not wise,* namely, in those things which shall happen in the world to come. And this is what was said in Isaiah chapter 1: <term>Yisrael lo yada ami lo hitbonan</term>, that is, <margin>D</margin> *Israel did not know, my people did not understand.* <note>Isaiah 1:3</note> *Israel did not know* those things which have passed. *My people did not understand* regarding the world to come. What did Israel deserve, that they should be infatuated and thickened in heart? Because they were not wise in the words of the law. And thus Job himself says in chapter 4: <term>Halo nasa yitram bam yamutu v’lo v’chochmah</term>, that is, *Does not their cord depart with them? They shall die, and not in knowledge or wisdom.* <note>Job 4:21</note> Thus far the tradition. Since, therefore, the "world to come" or "future world" in the Talmud is almost <margin>E</margin> always the time of the Messiah, it is quite clearly held according to the aforementioned tradition that the Jews were infatuated because they were not wise, nor did they understand the words of the law by which the Messiah is evidently shown, so that they might receive him. But their cord then departed with them when, denying the Messiah, God their Savior, they fell headlong—in this world into the whirlpool of the Roman Empire, and in the future into the pit of hell. It is like the one who lets himself down from a height by a rope, and when it is untied, he rushes with it into the precipice. According to that <margin>F</margin> prophecy of Isaiah said in the fifth chapter: <term>Laken galah ami mibali da'at...</term> that is, *Therefore my people are led away captive, because they were without knowledge, and their honorable men are dead of hunger, and their commoners parched with thirst. Therefore hell has enlarged its soul, and opened its mouth without limit. And its nobility shall descend, and its multitude, and its shouting. And he shall rejoice in it,* namely, hell. <note>Isaiah 5:13-14</note> Upon these words, *Hell has enlarged its soul,* with the rest, the gloss of <margin>G</margin> Rabbi Solomon says thus: *Measure for measure. For they themselves enlarged themselves to swallow down food and drink excessively, and they opened their mouths to deny God their Savior...*

...as it is said in Jeremiah, chapter 5: *They have denied the Lord and said, "It is not He."* <note>Jeremiah 5:12</note> Also in the book **Hagiga** <note>original: חגיגה; a tractate of the Talmud concerning festival offerings</note>, that is, *Of the Festival*, in the chapter that begins **Hakol Chayavin** <note>original: הכל חייבין; "All are Obligated"</note>, it is read in this way: It is written in Jeremiah, chapter 49:
<margin>A</margin> *Counsel has perished from the sons, their wisdom has become foul.* <note>Jeremiah 49:7</note> When did counsel perish from the sons and their wisdom become foul? When they were among the nations of the world. For the Devil (with God's

Therefore, the Savior spoke well of them in the 15th chapter of Matthew, saying: *They are blind, and leaders of the blind. If the blind leads the blind, both fall into the ditch.*

### CHAPTER IV.

#### Concerning the rejection of the Jews, and how they were to be expelled from the house of God as enemies of God.

#### CAPNIO.

Since God has cast away and rejected the Jews as rebels and enemies against Him, testimony must be asserted from their own scriptures to their confusion that these things were destined to happen to them. <margin>GALATINUS</margin> These things are most clearly evident by the testimony of Hosea, in chapter 9, speaking in the person of God: *Because of the wickedness of their deeds, I will drive them out of my house; I will no longer*

*love them.* <note>Hosea 9:15; original Hebrew: על רע מעלליהם מביתי אגרשם לא אסיף אהבתם</note> Which Rabbi Jonathan <note>The author of the Targum, the Aramaic translation of the Prophets</note> interpreted in Aramaic as: *Because of the wickedness of their works, from my holy house I will drive them out, nor will I continue to have mercy on them.* <note>original: על בישת עובדיהון מבית מקדשי אתרכינון לא אוסף לרחמא עליהון</note> Regarding this, the Prophet Amos also says in chapter 5: *She has fallen, she shall not rise again, the virgin of Israel.* <note>Amos 5:2; original Hebrew: נפלה לא תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל</note>

<margin>E</margin> translated into Aramaic as: *The Lord God established by His word (or through His word). Since, therefore, their rejection is compared to the shattering of such shards, which are worth nothing further except to be thrown away...

<margin>A</margin>outside, it is clearly given to be understood that they would fall into such great dejection in that captivity that as long as they remain in their unbelief, they can never return to their former liberty. This is according to what is <margin>said</margin> in Psalm 2: **תרועם בשבט ברזל ככלי יוצר תנפצם**, <note>Psalm 2:9</note> that is: *You shall break them with a rod of iron, and dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.* From these things which have been said, it is manifest that the Jews, on account of the malice of their works, were deservedly to be cast out by God Himself from the house of God, and were never to be loved by Him <margin>B</margin> as long as they remain in the malice of their unbelief. Foreseeing this, Jeremiah, at the end of his Lamentations, sought the cause, saying: **למה לנצח תשכחינו תעזבנו לאורך ימים** <note>Lamentations 5:20</note> that is: *Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long a time?* To which the Lord responded in the 8th chapter of the same Prophet, saying: **ואמרת אליהם כה אמר יהוה היפלו ולא יקומו אם ישוב ולא ישוב: מדוע שובבה העם הזה ירושלם משבה נצחת החזיקו בתרמת מאנו לשוב: הקשבתי <margin>C</margin>ואשמע לוא כן ידברו אין איש נחם על רעתו לאמר מה עשיתי כל השב במרצותו כסוס שוטף במלחמה: גם חסידה בשמים ידעה מועדיה ותור וסוס וענור שמרו את עת באנה ועמי לא ידעו את משפט יהוה:** <note>Jeremiah 8:4–7</note> that is: *You shall say to them, thus says God: Shall they fall and not rise again? If they turn away, shall they not return? Why then is this people of Jerusalem turned away with a persistent—even eternal—obstinacy? They have strengthened themselves in deceit, and refused to return. I attended and heard; they do not speak what they have in their hearts. There is no man who <margin>D</margin> repents of his malice, saying: "What have I done?" Everyone is turned to his own course, like a horse rushing headlong into battle. Even the stork in the sky knows her seasons, and the turtle-dove, and the crane, and the swallow have observed the time of their coming. But my people have not known the judgment of God.* From these passages, the proposition is clear.

### CHAPTER V.

*That the Jews are never more to return to their land, nor to possess it.*

### CAPNIO.

<margin>E</margin> THE more recent Jews, when they are convinced of being guilty of their crime through this captivity in which they now exist, immediately object to us that they are going to return to their land and possess it. Therefore, so that they may know not only that they are speakers of falsehood in this, but also that they hope in vain for what they are never to return to, nor ever possess, it must be <margin>F</margin> proven from their own scriptures. GALATINUS: This is best proven by what is held among them in the book **יבמות** *Yebamoth* <note>original: יבמות; a Talmudic tractate regarding "Leveirate marriages" or sisters-in-law</note>, that is, *Of the Sisters-in-law*, in the chapter that begins **הארץ** *Ha-aretz*, that is, *The Land*: where it is read thus word-for-word: "It is handed down in the book **סדר עולם** *Seder Olam* <note>original: סדר עולם; "The Order of the World," an ancient chronological work</note>, that is, *The Order of the World*, that it is written in Deuteronomy chapter 30: **והביאך יהוה אלהיך אל הארץ אשר ירשו אבתיך וירשתה** <note>Deuteronomy 30:5</note> that is: *And the Lord your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it.* For there was a first and a second possession for them, <margin>G</margin> but there will not be a third. Rabbi Johanan said: 'Who was the author of *Seder Olam*, that is, the book of the order of the world?' Rabbi Joses." This is the tradition. This same thing is also held in the same book *Seder Olam* in this manner—

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> it is written in Deuteronomy chapter 30: *And the Lord your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it.* Could it be that there will be a third possession in the future? It teaches what should be said to this by that which it says: *Which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it.* For they were to have a first and a second possession, but there will be no third possession for them. This is the tradition. Since, therefore, the Jews were only to possess their former land twice, as is clearly evident from these traditions: <margin>B</margin> and they have already possessed it twice (For they possessed it first from the time of Joshua until the destruction of the first temple, and second from the times of Zerubbabel and Ezra until the burning of the last temple, or until the times of the Emperor Hadrian <note>The Roman Emperor who crushed the Bar Kokhba revolt in 135 CE, leading to the mass displacement of Jews from Judea.</note>, as is clear in many ways from their scriptures); and since they are by no means to possess it a third time (the aforementioned traditions bearing witness): they themselves must necessarily concede that they will never again possess their land, and consequently will not <margin>C</margin> return to it. Therefore, whatever they object against us concerning their return to Jerusalem, the rebuilding of the temple, and a third possession of that land, is utterly false and entirely inconsistent with their ancient scriptures. But indeed, the third possession of their land, which they wait for in vain, was to be given to the Saracens <note>A medieval term for Muslims; Galatinus interprets the Islamic conquest of the Levant as a divine judgment against the Jews.</note> (according to Ezekiel) for a time, to their shame. For thus he says in chapter 7: **והבאתי רעי גוים וירשו את בתיהם והשבתי <margin>D</margin>גאון עזים ונחלו מקדשיהם** <note>Ezekiel 7:24</note> that is: *And I will bring the evil ones of the nations—that is, the Saracens—and they shall possess their lands; and I will make the pride of the strong to cease, and they shall inherit their holy places.* And below: **תורה תאבד מכהן ועצה מזקנים** <note>Ezekiel 7:26</note> that is: *And the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.* And this is so because they were to be without sacrifice, and without a Prince—indeed, even without God—on account of their unbelief, until the end of the world.

### CHAPTER VI.

*That the Jews were to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world.*

### CAPNIO.

<margin>E</margin> I WOULD wish that you would show through their scriptures what you said last: namely, that the Jews were to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world. GALATINUS: That is very well proven by what is said in the third <margin>F</margin> chapter of Hosea: **כי ימים רבים ישובו בני ישראל אין מלך ואין שר ואין זבח ואין מצבה ואין אפוד ותרפים** <note>Hosea 3:4</note> That is: *For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a King, and without a Prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an Ephod (that is, without the priestly garment), and without images.* Moreover, Rabbi Jonathan translated these things into Chaldean <note>Refers to the Aramaic Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel.</note> as follows: **ארי יומין סגיאין יתבון בני ישראל לית מלכא ולית רבנא <margin>G</margin>ולית דבחא ולית קמתא בשומרון ולית אפוד ומחוי** that is: *For the children of Israel shall abide many days in which they shall not have a King from the house of David, nor one exercising power over Israel, nor an acceptable sacrifice, nor one pleasing in Jeru—*

But it is most evident that they interpret this poorly and falsely from this: although the name *Elohim* (**אלהים**) <margin>E</margin> is sometimes found to signify "judges" in the sacred scriptures, in its primary meaning it signifies God—expressed in the plural on account of the divine Trinity of persons. And woe to me, who have exercised myself in the law alone." For as Rabbi Hunna said, whoever studies or exercises himself in the law only, is like one who does not have a <margin>D</margin> God. Just as it is written in the fifteenth chapter of the second book of Chronicles: *For many days Israel shall be without the true God, and without a priest, and without the law.* And what does "without the law" mean? Rabbi Hunna said: "Anyone studying in the law only, and not studying in works of mercy or piety, is like one who does not have a God." As it was said (in the place cited above): *For many days Israel shall be without the true God, or the God of truth.* And it should be noted that while Hosea had said a little earlier that the Jews would be for many days <margin>E</margin> without a King—along with the rest—he consequently shows that they would be without the true God and without the Messiah until the end of the world, when he immediately added in the same place: **אחר ישובו בני ישראל ובקשו את יהוה אלהיהם ואת דוד מלכם ופחדו אל יהוה ואל טובו באחרית הימים** <note>Hosea 3:5</note> that is: *Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their King, and shall fear the Lord and His goodness in the end of days.* Which Rabbi Jonathan turns into Chaldee <margin>F</margin> <note>Referring to the Targum, an Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> thus: **בתר כן יתובון בני ישראל ויתבעון ית פולחנא דיי אלההון וישתמעון למשיחא בר דוד מלכיהון** that is: *and after these things the children of Israel shall return, and seek the worship of the Lord their God, and shall obey the Messiah the son of David their King.* Now these things are to happen around the end of the world, when the remnant of the Jews shall be converted to our Lord Jesus, the true Messiah. Therefore, until that time, Jewish perfidy <note>Here "perfidy" is used in the medieval sense of "unbelief" or "refusal to accept the faith."</note> shall remain without a King and Prince, without sacrifice and priest, without the law, without the true God, and without the true Messiah and Savior. This was to be proven.

### CHAPTER VII.

->That just as the Hebrews were divided into Israel and Judah: so<-

### CAPNIO.

**A**lthough you have sufficiently proven in the preceding sections that few among the Jews were to be saved at the time of the Messiah, and the rest indeed were to be lost and scattered: it is nevertheless established that those who received our Redeemer, the true Messiah, were both saved and, with their name changed, called *Messihim* (**משיחים**), that is, Christians. However, those who refused to receive him happened neither to be saved nor to be called by another name. For to denote their perfidy, they have been called Jews until now, and will be called so as long as they remain in their perfidy. Therefore, to further convict them of their very perfidy, you ought to prove through their own scriptures that this division into treacherous Jews and true Christians was to occur in the time of the Messiah. GALATINUS: Just as a division continually flourished between Israel and Judah—with Israel, of course, worshipping two golden calves as gods—so the division between Christians and Jews never ceases to exist, with the Jews themselves denying the truth of our Lord Jesus Christ and the Christian faith. Regarding this, it must be known that the schism of the ten tribes imposed this name upon the Jews. For previously they were called Hebrews, or Israel, or Israelites. From the time, therefore, that the people were divided into two Kingdoms, whoever among them had Kings from the lineage of Judah, or from the tribe of Judah, were called Jews. But the ten tribes and whoever in Samaria accepted Jeroboam as their King were called Israel. For them, Jeroboam their King made two golden calves, placing one in Dan and the other in Bethel. And he said to them (as is held in 1 Kings, chapter 12): **רב לכם מעלות ירושלם הנה אלהיך ישראל אשר העלוך מארץ מצרים** <note>1 Kings 12:28</note> that is: *Do not go up to Jerusalem anymore. Behold your gods, O Israel, <margin>E</margin> who made you come up out of the land of Egypt.* On account of this and many other crimes, the following things show that they were rejected by God. And first indeed that which is read in 2 Kings, chapter seventeen: **ויעזבו את כל מצות יהוה אלהיהם ויעשו להם מסכה שנים עגלים ויעשו אשירה וישתחוו לכל צבא השמים ויעבדו את הבעל: ויעבירו את בניהם ואת בנותיהם באש ויקסמו קסמים וינחשו ויתמכרו לעשות הרע בעיני יהוה להכעיסו: ויתאנף יהוה מאד בישראל ויסירם מעל פניו לא נשאר רק שבט יהודה לבדו: גם יהודה לא שמר את מצות יהוה אלהיהם וילכו בחקות ישראל אשר עשו: וימאס יהוה בכל זרע ישראל ויענם ויתנם ביד שוסים עד אשר השליכם מפניו כי קרע ישראל מעל בית דוד וימליכו את ירבעם בן נבט** <note>2 Kings 17:16–21</note> that is: *They left all the precepts of the Lord their God, and made for themselves a molten image, namely, two calves, and they made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal; and they passed their sons and daughters through fire, and practiced divinations, and followed auguries, and sold themselves to do evil in <margin>G</margin> the eyes of God, to provoke Him. And God was vehemently angry with Israel, and took them away from His presence, and none remained except the tribe of Judah alone. Furthermore, Judah did not keep the mandates of the Lord its God...*

Therefore, the Lord rightly said: *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.* Furthermore, regarding what was said in the preceding tradition—namely, that the Israelites became *mamzerim* or bastards—it pertains to what is said in Zechariah, chapter nine: **וישב ממזר באשדוד.** That is: *And a bastard (or one of illegitimate birth) shall sit or dwell in Ashdod.* <note>Ashdod was one of the five major Philistine cities.</note> Rabbi Jonathan son of Uzziel shows in the Chaldean edition <note>Refers to the Targum, an Aramaic translation and commentary.</note> that this is to be understood regarding Israel, saying: *And the house of Israel shall dwell in Ashdod.* It also pertains to what is written in the book *Yebamoth* <note>The Talmudic tractate concerning levirate marriage.</note> (that is, *Of Sisters-in-law*), in the chapter that begins **נשים** *Nasim*, that is, *Women*, in this manner: It is a tradition that the daughters—that is, the women—of that generation of the ten tribes were rendered barren. ### CHAPTER VIII.

->That the Jews were to be destroyed because they were going to betray and deny the true God.<-

### CAPNIO <note>The Latinized name of Johannes Reuchlin, the famous German humanist and Hebraist who is a character in this dialogue.</note>

Although in the previous points you have sufficiently touched upon the cause of their rejection, nevertheless, so that the truth may shine more clearly and their own faithlessness be further confounded, I beseech you to reveal the cause of their destruction even more expressly through their own scriptures. **GALATINUS:** Regarding the destruction of the Jews, which was to happen through the Romans, and concerning the cause of that destruction and the malice of their remnants, it was foretold in these words in the fifth chapter of Jeremiah:

> <note>Jeremiah 5:1–3 original Hebrew: "Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in her broad places, if you can find a man, if there be any that executes judgment, that seeks the truth; and I will pardon her. And though they say, 'As the Lord lives,' surely they swear falsely. O Lord, are not your eyes upon the truth? You have stricken them, but they have not grieved; you have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction; they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return."</note>

And see, I pray, and know, and inquire in her streets, whether you find a man doing judgment and seeking faith, and I will be merciful to her—that is, to Jerusalem. And, if they say "The Lord lives," they will nevertheless swear to a falsehood. O Lord, are not your eyes toward faith? You have struck them, and they did not grieve. You have consumed them, and they refused to accept discipline, or correction. They have hardened their faces more than a rock, and refused to be converted. And a little further down it is added:

> <note>Jeremiah 5:10–13 original Hebrew: "Go up upon her walls and destroy; but make not a full end: take away her branches: for they are not the Lord's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says the Lord. They have belied the Lord, and said, 'It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine.' And the prophets shall become wind, and the word is not in them: thus shall it be done unto them."</note>

That is: Go up upon her walls,

<margin>A</margin>and destroy, but do not make a full end. Take away the shoots and branches, because they are not God's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously with me, says God. They have denied God (the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>) <note>The sacred four-letter name of God in Hebrew, YHWH.</note> and said, "It is not He, nor will evil come upon us, and we shall not see the sword or famine." <margin>B</margin>And the prophets shall be as the wind, or as spirit, and the word shall not be in them. This shall happen to them. That these things were foretold concerning the destruction of the Jews which was to come through the Romans is clear through their own commentators. For it is read thus in the <term>Beresith Rabba and Ketanna</term> <note>Midrashic commentaries on the Book of Genesis; "Rabba" means Great and "Ketanna" means Little.</note>, that is, in the major and minor exposition of the book of Genesis, upon that which is said in the 18th chapter of the same book: "And he [Abraham] said, 'I pray, Lord, let it not be displeasing, and I will speak even this once. What if ten are found there?' And He said, 'I will not destroy it for the sake of those ten.'" Why ten? Because already eight had remained in the generation of the flood, and God did not suspend His sentence on account of their merits. <margin>C</margin>Another exposition: Why ten? Because he thought ten were there—namely, Lot, his wife, his four daughters, and his four sons-in-law. **Rabbi Iodan** and **Rabbi Hanina** said: It is said "ten" here, but in Jerusalem, at least "one." For this is what is written in Jeremiah chapter 5: "Go around Jerusalem," and the rest. And thus it is said elsewhere, namely in Ecclesiastes chapter 7: "One by one, to find the account or number." **Rabbi Ishac** said: And up to what number is the finding of the number? Down to one. <margin>D</margin>Thus far the tradition. Therefore, the argument must be made here: if in the destruction of the First Temple there were many righteous people who could be found in Jerusalem—for Baruch the son of Neriah was there, of whom it is said in Jeremiah chapter 36: "And Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord." Also there was Abdemelech the Ethiopian, who pulled Jeremiah out of the cistern where he was dying, when he had addressed the King thus (as held in Jeremiah 38): <margin>E</margin>"My lord King, these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah the Prophet, whom they have cast into the pit to die." To whom, and for that reason, the Lord said (as written in Jeremiah 39): "Rescuing I will rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword, and your life shall be as a spoil to you, because you have trusted, or because you have hoped in me, says the Lord." There was also the house or family of the Rechabites, of whom it is said in the same Prophet: "Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak to them." And after a few words: <margin>F</margin>"There shall not be cut off a man from Jonadab the son of Rechab standing before me all the days." Furthermore, there was then Jeremiah the Prophet, and many other righteous and holy men who migrated to Babylon. If, therefore, so many righteous men were in Jerusalem at the time of the destruction of the First Temple, it is clearly shown from the conclusion of the aforementioned tradition—which says that no righteous man was found in Jerusalem when it says "Go around the streets of Jerusalem" <margin>G</margin>with the rest—that it does not speak of the first destruction of that city, which was done by Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon, but of the final one, which happened to be done by the Roman Princes Vespasian and Titus. Indeed, the reason why God destroyed and rejected the Jews through the Romans is shown...

...it is given, when it is said in the same place: *For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says God.* <note>Jeremiah 5:11</note> Now, what sort of treachery this was is clearly hinted at when it immediately follows: *They have denied God, and said, "It is not he."* Since, therefore, after the return from the Babylonian captivity, the Jews never denied the Lord God in word or deed through the worship of idolatry, it necessarily follows that they denied Him then—saying that He was not God—when they rejected the Lord Jesus Christ, the true God and Son of God, saying that he was not the Messiah. Instead, they appointed for themselves two false Messiahs, one after the other. For this reason, in the same chapter of the same prophecy, it is said: <note>original Hebrew: הכם אריה מיער זאב ערבות ישדדם</note> *Therefore a lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf of the deserts (or of the evening) shall spoil them, a leopard watches over their cities. Every one that goes out from there shall be preyed upon.* <note>Jeremiah 5:6</note> Which the gloss of **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Also known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator.</note> explains thus: *A lion from the forest has struck them*, that is, the Kingdom of Babylon; *A wolf of the desert (or of the evening) shall spoil them*, namely the Kingdom of the Medes; *A leopard watches over their cities*: the Kingdom of the Greeks; *Every one that goes out from there shall be preyed upon*, that is, by the Kingdom of the Romans. This is the view of Rabbi Solomon. Through this exposition, it clearly appears that from that passage in the words of Jeremiah where it says *Every one going out from them shall be preyed upon* by Edom <note>In medieval Jewish commentary, "Edom" was frequently used as a coded term for Rome or the Roman Empire.</note> (that is, by the Romans), all that follows must be understood as concerning the destruction of the Jews carried out by the Romans. For where else are these words found: *Take away her branches, for they are not the Lord's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says God. They have denied God, and said: "It is not he."* Now, the vine from which these branches or shoots were to be taken away because they were not of God was the entire house of Israel itself, according to what was said in Hosea 10: <note>original Hebrew: גפן בוקק ישראל</note> *Israel is a luxuriant vine.* From all of this, it is manifest that the Jews were to be destroyed by the Romans for this reason: because they would betray and deny God. Although there was also another cause for their ruin and eternal damnation, namely that they refused to receive the law of the Messiah.

Therefore it follows: "And he poured upon them the fury of his anger"—namely, the Romans and the "strength of battle"—along with the other things that follow. Responding to the sixth petition of Antoninus, the consul of the city of Rome, he said among other things: "From Israel, those who do not believe in his words—that is, the Messiah's—God, moved by anger, will pour it out upon them; and He will swear by His holiness that they shall not have salvation, nor shall they remain with Him in paradise, as it is said in Psalm 95: **Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways: Unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest.**" <note>original Hebrew: ארבעים שנה אקוט בדור ואומר עם תעי לבב הם והם לא ידעו דרכי אשר נשבעתי באפי אם יבאון אל מנוחתי</note> Likewise, in this world they shall be separated from God and lose their sovereignty; and dispersed throughout the entire world, they shall be sub-

### ## CHAPTER X.

->That they were also to be rejected and remain in God's hatred because they would deny and blaspheme Jesus the true Messiah and Mary his mother.<-

->CAPNIO<-

<margin>C</margin>
**I**S there another cause for their rejection besides those already mentioned? **GALATINUS:** There is indeed, and it holds a strong position among the greatest secrets of our faith, which until now have lain hidden in the books of the Jews. **CAPNIO:** I beseech you, explain what this one is as well. **GALATINUS:** Thus Rabbi Nehumias, in the epistle of secrets which he calls **The Letter of Secrets** <note>original: *Ighereth hassodoth*</note>, explaining the words of that Doctor whom they call "Our Holy Teacher," says: "This is the primary rock from which the Messiah is to come forth." He says among other things: "This primary rock is the mother of the King Messiah." And a little later he says: "When you know the name of this rock and of her son by the method of arithmetic <term>Gematria: a system where Hebrew letters represent numbers to find hidden meanings in words</term>, you will find they add up to the number of **Covenant** <note>original: *Berith*</note>." And then you will understand the secret of that text written in Deuteronomy chapter 31: **Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers; and this people will rise up, and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land, whither they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.** <note>original Hebrew: הנך שכב עם אבתיך וקם העם הזה וזנה אחרי אלהי נכרי הארץ אשר הוא בא שמה בקרבו ועזבני והפר את בריתי אשר כרתי אתו</note> Thus says Rabbi Nehumias, who preceded the coming of our Redeemer by nearly fifty years. To explain this, it must be noted that this Hebrew word **Covenant** <note>Berith</note>, by the method of arithmetic, contains the number 612 among the Hebrews. For it is written with four letters, each of which represents a number for them. For **B** (Beth) signifies 2, **R** (Resh) signifies 200, **I** (Yod) signifies 10, and **T** (Tau) signifies 400. Therefore, **Covenant** <note>Berith</note>, which is composed of these, contains 612. As we have shown elsewhere, the names of the mother of the Messiah and her son also contain this same number. For the name...

<margin>A</margin> Indeed, the name of the mother of the Messiah (as previously shown by the same <term>Rabbenu Haccados</term><note>Hebrew: *Rabbenu Ha-Kadosh*, "Our Holy Rabbi," usually referring to Judah the Prince, though here used in a mystical-pseudepigraphical context</note>) was destined to be <note>original Hebrew: מרים</note> **Miriam**, that is, Mary. Truly, the name of her son, the Messiah, by which he was to be called by the Gentiles who would accept his faith, was destined to be <note>original Hebrew: ישוע</note> **Yeshua**, that is, Jesus, as the same Rabbenu Haccados had shown before. These names, namely Mary and Jesus, by the method of <term>arithmetic ratio</term><note>This refers to Gematria, the practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew words to find hidden connections.</note> among the Hebrews, also contain the number **612**. For the letter *mem* denotes 40; *resh*, 200; *yod*, 10; *mem*, 40; then the connector *waw*, 6; *yod*, 10; *shin*, 300; and *waw*, 6. And so the names of the mother of the Messiah and her son, which <margin>B</margin> are **Mary and Jesus**, contain the same number that the word <note>original Hebrew: ברית</note> **Berith** (Covenant) contains, which is 612. This same number is also carried by the words in the aforementioned text of Deuteronomy brought forward by <term>Rabbi Nehumia</term><note>A reference to Nehunia ben Ha-Kanah, a 1st-century sage associated with early Jewish mysticism.</note>: <note>original Hebrew: אלהי נכר הארץ</note> **Elohe nechar ha-aretz**, which means "the foreign gods of the land." For *aleph* signifies 1; *lamed*, 30; *he*, 5; *yod*, 10; *nun*, 50; *kaph*, 20; *resh*, 200; *he*, 5; *aleph*, 1; *resh*, 200; and *tsadi*, 90. All of these together make **612**. 

From these things, therefore, the previously mentioned words of Rabbi Nehumia are clear when he says: *When you know the name of this rock, that is, the mother of the Messiah, which is Mary, and the name of her son, that is the Messiah himself, which is Jesus, and see that by arithmetic ratio they rise to the number of the "Berith" or Covenant (which is 612), then you will understand the secret of that text:* **Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers**, and the rest. 

It was, therefore, a very great mystery that the Lord then revealed to Moses in Deuteronomy chapter 31, <margin>Deuteronomy chapter 31</margin> saying: **Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and this people, rising up, shall go whoring after foreign gods.** The sense of these words is this: after you have departed from this life, this people of yours will rise up and "go whoring," that is, they will go astray. Their error will be this: they will say that Jesus and Mary are "foreign gods of the land," that is, idols. In this they will err, and they will forsake me, and they will make void my **Berith**, that is, my Covenant—which is to say, my Jesus and my Mary—blaspheming them and saying they are foreign gods. 

Because of this, it follows immediately in the same place: <note>original Hebrew: והרה אפי בו ביום ההוא ועזבתים והסתרתי פני מהם והיה לאכל</note> **And my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured.** Because God repays a man according to the measure of his sin, he added a little later <margin>Deuteronomy chapter 32 says:</margin> **They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.** 

This means: Since they will provoke me by saying I am not God, and will provoke me with their vanities—that is, the lies, blasphemies, and abominations they impiously tell about me and Mary my mother—I will therefore avenge myself by the same measure. For I will move them to jealousy with those who are "not a people," that is, I will cause them to no longer be my people. And I will provoke them with a "foolish nation," that is, I will cause them to be called a foolish nation by everyone—a nation without faith, without truth, without God, which betrayed and denied its own God. From all these things we have set forth in the preceding chapters, it appears clearly 

<column-break/>

enough how just was the destruction, scattering, captivity, and rejection of the Jews. Nevertheless, if they were willing to repent of their sin and lay aside their faithlessness, God would immediately spare them and receive them back into grace; they would be immediately redeemed, freed from captivity, and would have their Messiah.

### CHAPTER XI.

#### *That if the Jews were willing to repent of their sin and lay aside their faithlessness, they would be immediately redeemed and freed from captivity, and would have the Messiah as their Savior.*

#### CAPNIO.

<margin>C</margin> <note>The letter T is decorated with leafy vines and architectural scrollwork.</note> So that their obstinate faithlessness may be further exposed, and be more confounded and convicted, prove from their own scriptures that what you said last is true. ### CHAPTER XIII.

->That the Gentiles receiving the Messiah were to be loved by God and become God’s chosen and special people.<-

### CAPNIO.
<note>Capnio is the Hellenized name of Johann Reuchlin, a famous Christian Hebraist and character in this dialogue.</note>

**A**S a greater confusion, therefore, to the Jews—who have been so shamefully rejected by God and held in hatred—it must also be proved through their own scriptures that the Gentiles, who were to be converted to the worship of the one and true God in the time of the Messiah, were to be loved by God and made into and called his chosen and peculiar people. **GAL.** <note>Referring to Galatinus, the primary speaker and author of the work.</note> This is primarily evident from the fact that, as a figure of this very thing, God himself commanded in the Old Testament that <term>proselytes</term><note>original: proselytos; individuals from the nations who converted to the worship of the God of Israel.</note>—that is, those coming from Gentility to the worship of the one God—be loved. Therefore, it seems by no means should we overlook what is read in the book <margin>E</margin> *Mechilta*—that is, in a certain exposition upon Exodus—in this manner, regarding that which is said in the 22nd chapter of the same book: <note>original Hebrew: וגר לא תונה ולא תלחצנו</note> "And you shall not wrong a stranger, nor shall you oppress him," namely, in money matters. You shall not say to him, "Yesterday you were a worshiper of Bel <note>A Mesopotamian deity frequently used in Jewish texts to represent idolatry.</note> and you were worshipping his hollow shrine, and look, the meat of pigs still remains between your teeth. From that place where it is said in Exodus chapter 22: "A stranger"—that is, a convert—"you shall not wrong," and so forth. Hence Nathan used to say: "The blemish that is in yourself, do not speak of it to your neighbor." For the strangers—that is, the converts—are beloved. For in every place, a warning is given regarding them, as in that passage of Exodus 22: "And the <term>gher</term><note>Hebrew: stranger or convert</note>, that is, the convert, you shall not oppress." And "A stranger"—that is, a convert from Gentility—"you shall not wrong." Rabbi Eliezer said: "Since the turning away of a stranger—that is, a convert—is a very bad thing, therefore a warning is given for him in many places." But Rabbi Simeon said: "Behold, God himself says in Judges chapter 5: 'And you shall love him as the sun going forth in its strength.'" For who is greater of the two: he who loves the King, or he whom the King loves? Behold,

<margin>A</margin> undoubtedly they say: "He whom the King loves." And "keeping" is also said of the *gherim*, the converts, as in that passage of Psalm 146: "God keeps the *gherim*, that is, the converts." What more? Abraham called himself a *gher*. Just as it is said in Genesis chapter 23: "And he spoke to the sons of Heth, saying: 'I am a *gher* and a dweller among you.'" <margin>A</margin>...he shall be surnamed by the name of Israel. These shall be those who "fear heaven," that is, God. Thus far the tradition. In it, three reasons are assigned as to why those converted from Gentilism to the worship of the one true God were to be loved. The first is because they are loved by God. The second is because in Holy Scripture they were named in all things just as Israel and were treated as such by God. The third is because the holy fathers and prophets, such as Abraham and David, called themselves "sojourners," that is, converts. <margin>B</margin> Furthermore, the gloss of <term>Rabbi Solomon</term><note>Referring to Rashi, the famous 11th-century commentator.</note> explains those same words of Isaiah, which were introduced at the end of this tradition, as follows: *This one shall say: I am God’s.* These shall be the perfectly righteous. *This one shall call on the name of Jacob:* These shall be the young children of the wicked. *And he shall write with his hand to God:* These shall be the men who are repentant. *And he shall be surnamed by the name of Israel:* These shall be the <term>hagherim</term><note>original: הגרים; the Hebrew term for converts or proselytes.</note>, that is, converts from the Gentiles. Thus says Rabbi Solomon. What is written in <term>Vaelle Shemoth Rabba</term><note>original: ואלה שמות רבה; Exodus Rabbah, a midrashic commentary on the Book of Exodus.</note> is also most aptly connected to the preceding, specifically regarding what is said in chapter 12 of that same book: *This is the law of the Passover.* For it is said there: This is what is written in Isaiah chapter 56: *And let not the son of the stranger who has joined himself to God speak, saying: God will surely separate me.* For Job said in chapter 31: <margin>C</margin> *The <term>gher</term><note>original: גר; Hebrew for "stranger" or "convert."</note> shall not lodge outside,* meaning the convert shall not be excluded by God, who is holy and blessed. Why? Because the holy and blessed God does not exclude any creature, but receives everyone. For His gates are open <margin>D</margin> at every hour, and whoever wishes to be gathered in enters and is gathered. Because of this, it was said by Job: *The convert shall not lodge outside.* And again He says in the person of God, who is patient toward His creatures: *I will open my door to the traveler.* Rabbi Berachias said: On behalf of whom did Job say, *The convert shall not lodge outside*? He said this, without a doubt, because it is to be that the <term>gherim</term><note>original: גרים; plural of ger.</note>, that is, converts from the <margin>E</margin> Gentiles, shall be <term>kohanim</term><note>original: כהנים; Priests.</note>, that is, Priests ministering to the holy and blessed God. Just as it is said in Isaiah chapter 14: *And the convert [ha-gher] shall be joined to them, and they shall be gathered unto the house of Jacob.* Now, "to be gathered" refers only to priests. Just as it is said in 1 Kings chapter 2: *Gather me [adjoin me], I pray thee, to one of the priestly offices.* For it is to be that the *gherim*, that is, converts from the Gentiles, shall eat of the *bread of the presence*<note>original: לחם הפנים (happanim); the "Showbread" kept in the Temple, which was legally restricted to the priests.</note>. And thus he questioned the Masters, saying: What is it that is said in Deuteronomy chapter 10: *And God loves the convert [gher], giving him food and clothing*? Behold the total confidence or promise with which God makes the convert trust, that food and clothing will be given to him. They said to him: Jacob, whose name is Israel, asked this of God in Genesis chapter 28: *And if He gives me bread to eat and clothing to put on.* And for you, who have come to us, is it not enough to be like us? Let it be enough for you to be like us. Let it be sufficient for you to be like Jacob, the firstborn of God. Finally, however, do not let it enter your thought that Jacob asked for bread and clothing, or

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> food and clothing alone. For he said further: God makes me confident that He Himself will be with me, and will make an age stand from me. It follows: And this is what is written in Zechariah chapter 2: *Sing, or praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith God. And many nations shall be joined to God in that day, and they shall be my people.* All this is the tradition. From these things it is clear enough that the Gentiles converted to God in the time of the Messiah were to be loved by God Himself and <margin>B</margin> called the chosen people of God.

-> ### CHAPTER XIV. <-

-> *That all the dignities once granted to the Jews were to be taken away from them, and granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as the true and chosen people of God.* <-

-> CAPNIO. <-

<margin>C</margin> <note>The letter H is decorated with floral patterns.</note> THEREFORE, I consider that it should by no means be omitted here that it is proved through the Jewish scriptures that all the dignities once granted to the Jews were to be taken away from them, as from unworthy possessors, and were to be granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as the true, peculiar, and chosen people of God. GALATINUS: This <margin>D</margin> is shown most of all by what is read in the *Midrash Tehillim*<note>original: מדרש תהלים; a rabbinic commentary on the Psalms.</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Psalms, regarding what is said in Psalm 75: *And all the horns of the wicked I will break; but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.* For there it is said: *It did not say "horn" but "horns." For there are ten horns that the holy and blessed God gave to Israel. Namely, the horn of Abraham, of whom it is said in Isaiah 5: "My beloved had a vineyard on a horn of the son of oil." The horn of Isaac, of whom it is written in Genesis 22: "And behold, a ram caught in a thicket by its horns." <margin>G</margin> The horn of Joseph, that is, the horn of the Kingdom, of which it is said in Deuteronomy 33: "And his horns are the horns of a rhinoceros." The horn of Moses, of which it is said in Exodus 34: "Because the skin of his face was horned [shining]." The horn of prophecy, of which it is said in 1 Kings 1: "And Hannah prayed and said: My heart has exulted...*

At any time when the horns of the nations of the world are healthy, the horns of Israel will be broken. These things are set down in almost the same words in <term>איכה רבתי</term> <gloss>Echa Rabbethi</gloss><note>original: איכה רבתי; Lamentations Rabbah, a classical collection of Jewish midrashic interpretations of the Book of Lamentations.</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Lamentations of Jeremiah, regarding that saying in the second chapter of the same book: *He has broken in his fierce anger every horn of Israel.* This is excepted only in that in the tenth place, the horn of the Messiah is not mentioned, but only the horn of Israel. But then the same horn, as far as the moral laws are concerned, was given to the Romans and other Gentiles to be kept more perfectly, when the Gentiles themselves received the law of the Lord Jesus, the true Messiah, as divine.

# ON THE INSTITUTION OF THE NEW DI-
# VINE LAW WHICH WAS TO BE BROUGHT
# ABOUT THROUGH THE MESSIAH.

### CHAPTER ONE.

->That the Messiah was to institute a new divine law, more perfect than the old, which the Gentiles were meant to receive.<-

---

### CAPNIO.
<note>Capnio is the humanist name for Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous scholar of Hebrew and Greek.</note>

**S**ince, therefore, the Gentiles were to receive the new law of the Messiah as divine—those who (with the Jews largely rejected on account of their unfaithfulness) were destined to adhere to the Messiah himself, as you have already proved—it is now quite appropriate, in order to further subdue the stubborn neck of the Jews, to speak of the institution of that same new divine law. I ask first that you show through Hebrew testimonies that the Messiah himself would establish a new divine law more perfect than the old, and that the Gentiles would receive it. <margin>GAL.</margin> Indeed, that God would give a new law, different from the one he had given through Moses on Mount Sinai, was prophesied long ago through Jeremiah in chapter 31, in these words: <note>Jeremiah 31:31–33</note> *Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will strike a new covenant or pact with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. Not according to the pact that I struck with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, for they made void my pact, and I neglected them, says the Lord. But this will be the pact that I will strike with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their midst, and I will write it upon their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people.* <note>original Hebrew: "הנה ימים באים... ועל לבם אכתבנה"</note> Now, that <term>berith</term> <note>Hebrew: ברית, meaning covenant or pact</note>, that is, a pact or treaty, is the same thing as "law" in the preceding passages, is clearly shown in the book <term>Mechilta</term> <note>An ancient Jewish commentary (Midrash) on the Book of Exodus</note>: where, regarding that statement in Exodus chapter 12, "In the tenth of this month," it is said: "There is no <term>berith</term>, that is, treaty or pact, except the Law." Just as it is said in Deuteronomy 24: *These are the words of the <term>haberith</term>* <note>the covenant</note> *which the Lord commanded Moses to strike with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the <term>haberith</term> which he struck with*

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> *them in Horeb.* <note>Mount Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai.</note> Likewise, in Exodus chapter 24: *And he wrote upon the tablets the words of the pact, the ten words* <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>. This is the tradition. Furthermore, that the Messiah would bring this new divine law and give it to the Gentiles is evident first from what is read in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>A Jewish commentary on the Psalms.</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Psalms, regarding that statement in Psalm 21: *To the victor, or for the victory, a Psalm of David. The King shall rejoice in your strength, O God, and in your salvation how greatly shall he exult!* <note>Psalm 21:1–2</note> For there it is said word for word: "This is what is written in Isaiah chapter 11: <margin>B</margin> *And it shall be in that day, the root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples.*" Rabbi Hanina said: "The King Messiah is not coming except to give new precepts to the Gentiles, such as the <term>succa</term>, that is, the little booth, and the <term>lulav</term>, that is, the branch, and <term>tefillin</term>, that is, the phylacteries <note>Religious items used in Jewish prayer and festivals.</note>. But Israel shall learn the law from God, holy and blessed." <margin>C</margin> Just as it is said in Isaiah chapter 45: *And all your children shall be taught by God.* <note>Isaiah 54:13 is likely intended here.</note> And why? Because it is said in Isaiah chapter 11: *To him shall the Gentiles seek.* Rabbi Hanina, in the name of Rabbi Aba, said: "What is it that immediately follows in the same place in Isaiah: *And his rest shall be honor or glory*? Because the holy and blessed God will be bestowing upon the King Messiah some of the heavenly glory and honor." Thus far the tradition. Moreover, in Isaiah chapter 42, we read: <margin>D</margin> *Behold my servant, I will uphold him, or I will lean upon him, my chosen one, whom my soul or my person has willed, or in whom it has delighted. I have put my Spirit upon him; he shall bring forth judgment to the nations.* <note>Isaiah 42:1</note> Which Rabbi Jonathan, son of Uzziel, explained in Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note> as follows: <margin>E</margin> *Behold my servant the Messiah, I will bring him near, namely to myself, my chosen one, in whom I have willed my word to be. I will put my Holy Spirit upon him, he shall reveal judgment to the nations.* It follows in Isaiah chapter 42: *He shall not cry out, nor shall he shout, nor shall he make his voice heard outside.* Where the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi, the famous medieval commentator.</note> says: "He shall bring forth judgment to the nations: as it is said in Micah 4: *And he shall judge between many peoples, and shall rebuke strong nations even far away.*"

He shall not cry, nor shout aloud: because he will have no need of shouting to convince <note>original: *arguendum*, implying both rebuking and proving</note> and persuade the nations. For they shall come of their own accord to learn. There follows in the same place in Isaiah: <note>Isaiah 42:3: "A bruised reed he shall not break, and the smoking flax he shall not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth."</note> <margin>A</margin> That is: *A bruised reed he shall not break, and the dim or dark flax he shall not quench; he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.* Here, the gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), a preeminent medieval commentator.</note> says: Jonathan <note>Refers to the Targum Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation and commentary on the Prophets.</note> interpreted this thus: <margin>B</margin> *Those who are fragile like a bruised reed, he shall not break, and the dark, or dim, or clouded ones, whose light is faint, he shall not quench; he shall produce judgment according to the truth.* It follows in the same prophet in the same place: <note>Isaiah 42:4</note> *He shall not be dimmed, nor crushed, until he has set judgment in the earth, and the islands shall hope for, or expect, his law.* The "islands," according to the gloss of Rabbi Solomon, <margin>C</margin> refer to the Gentiles. Furthermore, the following testimony supports this application, as written in the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>The Midrash on the Psalms, a collection of homiletic interpretations.</note> regarding that which is said in Psalm 21: *For you set him as blessings forever.* For there it is said: This is what was spoken in Jeremiah 4: *And the nations shall be blessed in him, and in him shall they glory.* It follows in the same Psalm: *You shall make him glad with joy with your countenance.* Rabbi <margin>D</margin> Berachiah said in the name of Rabbi Samuel: One scripture says of the Messiah in Daniel 7: *Behold, in the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man came, and he reached even to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him, or applied him, or made him draw near before him.* But another scripture in Jeremiah chapter 30 says: <margin>E</margin> *And I will cause him to draw near, and he shall adhere, or be joined, to me.* Behold, in what manner the Angels shall introduce him into their midst. But God, holy and blessed, shall stretch out His hand and introduce him to Himself. Because of this, it is said of the King Messiah: *And I will cause him to draw near, and he shall adhere to me.* Thus far the tradition. By these things, therefore, it is clearly shown that Isaiah spoke in the person of the Messiah when he said in chapter 51: <note>Isaiah 51:4</note> *Attend to me, my people, and my mother, listen to me. Because a law shall go forth from me, and I will cause my judgment to rest as a light for the peoples, or I will make it frequent.* In this place where I have translated "my mother," the Hebrews have "my people" <note>original: *plebs mea*</note>. But it is a <term>tikkun soferim</term> <note>A "correction of the scribes," a term used in Hebrew tradition for a minor textual emendation made by ancient copyists for theological or clarity reasons.</note>, that is, a correction, or rather a depravation of the scribes. For it was not originally written as *le'ummi* <margin>F</margin> ("my people"), but *immi* ("my mother"), as Rabbi Elazar ben Jose says in the *Midrash Shir HaShirim* <note>The Midrash on the Song of Songs.</note> regarding that which is said in the 3rd chapter of that book: <margin>G</margin> *In the crown with which his mother crowned him.* Why God called the Jewish nation His mother was discussed in chapter 24 of the third book.

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> Furthermore, it is clear that this new law, which the Messiah was to institute, was meant to be promulgated from Jerusalem to the nations throughout the whole world; this is evident through Isaiah chapter 2, saying: *Because out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of God from Jerusalem.* This cannot be understood as the law of Moses, since the law of Moses itself did not go *out* of Zion or Jerusalem, but rather came *from* Sinai *to* Jerusalem. Therefore, it must be understood as the law of the Messiah, which, through the Apostles and <margin>B</margin> his other disciples, went forth from Jerusalem to the nations. For the Messiah himself, the Son of God according to his divinity and the Wisdom of the Father, descending from the highest heights and from the seat of his majesty for the redemption and salvation of the human race, being sent by the Father, came to Zion and Jerusalem. There he fulfilled his new law, that is, the Gospel, by teaching, admonishing, persuading, rebuking, performing miracles, suffering, dying, rising again, ascending to the heavens, and sending the light of the Holy Spirit to the apostles. Then, therefore, this prophetic saying was fulfilled when the Apostles, after <margin>C</margin> receiving the Holy Spirit, first promulgated the Gospel law in Jerusalem, and afterward, departing from there, published it everywhere on earth to the Gentiles. That the nations of the world were to receive this new law and doctrine with joy from the chosen disciples of the Messiah is held from what is said in Isaiah 12: *And you shall draw waters with joy from the wells of Jesus <note>original: *Iesu*, which also means "salvation" in Hebrew</note>, or of salvation.* For Rabbi Jonathan translated this into Aramaic thus: *And you shall receive a new doctrine with joy from the chosen righteous ones,* that is, of the Messiah. Therefore, all the Jews of our time are infatuated, and entirely wandering <margin>D</margin> and alienated from the truth of divine scripture, who assert that the Messiah would be bound by the laws—he whom we have proved in many ways in the preceding parts to be God. For he himself is the Wisdom of the Father, to whom the laws belong. He himself gave the old law <margin>E</margin> on Mount Sinai. He himself established the new law in Jerusalem. He is the creator of the men to whom the laws were delivered, and the supreme craftsman of all things in heaven and under heaven. For that reason, it was both fitting and worthy that in his descent, he should reserve for himself greater and better things to give than those he had delivered through Moses on Mount Sinai. And this is a sufficient argument against the Jews of our age. For if anyone seeks a more necessary reason in matters of will than the acts of will themselves provide, he is entirely unteachable, according to the opinion of Aristotle in the first book of the *Ethics*. This reasoning, however, concerns matters of will, and therefore it is quite sufficient. For we see this happen in the governments of men, that <margin>F</margin> Kings and Princes, in their arrival, reserve the very best things to be bestowed upon the cities. And this is for a twofold reason: First, so that they may make their arrival more honorable with more honorable gifts. Second, so that they may make themselves more welcome and pleasant to the cities and the Kingdom. Therefore, it is no wonder if, at his arrival, the Lord himself wished to reserve the perfection of the <margin>G</margin> law for himself. Just as he also reserved for all the righteous and chosen the opening of the heavens.

It uses philological evidence to argue that God refers to Israel as His "mother" in this context and asserts the Messiah's divinity as the author of both the old and new laws.</summary>
