### 735 KABBALAH 736

<margin>A</margin> ...that is, the confession of praise <note>original: *Hod*</note>, **Foundation** <note>original: *Yesod*</note> that is, the base, and **Kingdom** <note>original: *Malkhut*</note> that is, the reign. Above the **Crown** <note>original: *Keter*</note>, however, is placed **Infinity** <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note>, which is the abyss. Shall I speak or remain silent? This is surely a matter of profound speculation, an immense sea into which all our contemplation is submerged, <margin>B</margin> and being submerged, is swallowed by a certain gaping void. Do you not remember how much the modern scholars of almost all nations, the "God-taught" <note>original: *theodidascali*</note>, sweat day and night? They labor almost exclusively over the concepts of attributes, which some call "divine perfections" and others call "attributes"—whether negative, affirmative, absolute, relative, or connotative. You can easily learn of these now (as I judge) from the Kabbalistic book called the *Compendium of the Gates of Light* <note>original: *Portae Lucis*</note>, which Paulus Ricius—an exceptionally learned man, formerly one of our own [Jews] and now a Christian—collected from a certain Castilian Rabbi <note>referring to Joseph Gikatilla</note>, and from the *Introductions* he wrote on the Kabbalah. Likewise, on this same matter, that great Master of Kabbalah, Rabbi Joseph, son of Gikatilla, wrote the book <margin>C</margin> **Gates of Justice** <note>original: *Sha'are Tzedek*</note>. Many commentators have written extensively regarding the **Tree of the Ten Numerations** <note>the Sephirot</note>, who unroll this tangled cause and reduce almost the entire Old Testament to these ten numerations, and through them to the ten names of God, and through those back to the single name of the Tetragrammaton <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>. They affirm that **Infinity** <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note> is the Alpha and the Omega, he who said: "I am the first, and I am the last." <margin>D</margin> And that the **Crown** <note>original: *Keter*</note>, the reign of all ages, is the bottomless fountain and the **Father of Mercies** <note>original: *Ab Ha-Rakhamim*</note>. Its mystery is this: that **I Shall Be** <note>original: *Ehieh*</note> seals through **Truth** <note>original: *Emeth*</note>, which is to say, Essence through Truth. As that noble author Eliezer Ha-Kalir says, "**Truth** is His seal." Arithmetical logic <note>the practice of Gematria, where letters have numerical values</note> proves this: if we multiply **I Shall Be** <note>Ehieh = 21</note> by **I Shall Be** <note>21 x 21</note>, there arises four hundred and forty-one, which is the sum of **Truth** <note>Emeth: E=1, M=40, Th=400</note>, <margin>E</margin> or "the True"; just as "The Lord is Peace" <note>original: *Adonai Shalom*</note>. They reduce many things to this: the "Great Aleph," the fear of the Lord, the inaccessible light, the days of eternity—as in that verse: *His going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.* So writes the distinguished Kabbalist Tedacus Levi <note>Todros Abulafia</note> in his book on the ten numerations.

<margin>F</margin> To the **Second Numeration**, which is **Wisdom** <note>original: *Khokhmah*</note>, the following attributes or properties are referred: the Firstborn; *Yesh* <note>original: *Ies*, meaning "Being" or "Is"</note>; the primitive Law; the letter *Yod* (the first letter of the Tetragrammaton); the Land of the Living; the thirty-two paths; the seventy faces of the Law; War; Judgment; Amen; the Book; the Holy; the Will; the Beginning; and other things of that kind. And perhaps it is surprising that the second numeration is called the "Beginning." For we read in Recanati <note>Menahem Recanati</note>, the excellent Master of Kabbalah, regarding the start of Genesis, <margin>G</margin> in this way: *And perhaps you will ask, since Wisdom is the second numeration, why is it called the "Beginning?"* <note>original Hebrew: ואולי תשאל שחכמה היא ספירה השנייה ולמה קראת ראשית</note> For it is written in the book *Bahir*: *Nothing is the "Beginning" except Wisdom.* <note>original Hebrew: אין ראשית אלא חכמה</note> To which I would seem to answer rightly: that the infinity of the three highest numerations of the Kabbalistic tree (which you are accustomed to call the three divine persons of the most absolute essence), since it is withdrawn in an abyss 

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> of darkness, immanent and at rest, or (as they say) looking toward nothing, is therefore called **Nothing** <note>original: *Ayin*</note>, that is, non-being or "not-end" <note>a pun on *Ein Sof*</note>. This is **Infinity** <note>original: *Ein Sof*</note> because we, punished by such a slender poverty of intellect regarding divine matters, judge those things which do not appear just as we judge those things which do not exist. But when God shows Himself so as to be "something" and truly <margin>B</margin> subsists, then the "Dark Aleph" is converted into the "Bright Aleph." For it is written: *As is its darkness, so is its light.* It is called the "Great Aleph" when it desires to go out and appear as the cause of all things through the letter *Beth*, which follows immediately. Concerning this, Menahem Recanati writes: *Thus you will find this operation of all things...* <note>original Hebrew: על כן נמצאת זאת פעולת הדברים כלם</note> that is, you will find this letter, namely *Beth*, making all things. Wherefore *Aleph* receives this same letter as its closest and most fertile companion, and it is named **Father** <note>original: *Ab*, spelled Aleph-Beth</note>, the father of all generation and production. Then, it sends the assumed *Beth* back into the universe of beings, <margin>C</margin> desiring to attain its end from the infinite **Nothing** <note>original: *Ayin*</note>. Therefore, by joining *Beth* to the final letter *Nun*, it generates the **Son** <note>original: *Ben*, spelled Beth-Nun</note>, which is the first production in the deity and the principle of "otherness." Hence it is nicknamed the **Beginning** <note>original: *Reshit*</note>, even though it is the second emanation from infinity—that is, the second Kabbalistic numeration through which all things were made. For it is written: *You have made all things in Wisdom.* In this way, the first outflow becomes the second numeration, because the goal of generation <margin>D</margin> is the Son. 

Thirdly, there remains the middle between *Aleph* and *Nun*, which is *Yod*, the mark of the holy name **Yah**. If you interweave both characters of that name with the name **Son** <note>original: *Ben*</note by turns, it becomes **Intelligence** <note>original: *Binah*</note>—that is, prudence or providence. This is the third emanation in the divine, to which are attributed: *Adonai*; Spirit; Soul; Vow; the Mystery of Faith; the Mother of Sons; the King sitting on the throne of mercies; the Great Jubilee; the Great Sabbath; the Foundation of Spirits; the Wonderful Light; the Supreme Day; <margin>E</margin> the Fifty Gates; the Day of Atonement; the Interior Voice; the River flowing out of Paradise; the second letter of the Tetragrammaton <note>the letter *He*</note>; Repentance; Deep Waters; "my sister"; "the daughter of my father"; and other titles. 

Thus far we have noted the three numerations which are called by the Kabbalists (according to Rabbi Isaac in his commentaries on the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>) the **Highest Numerations, One Throne** <note>original Hebrew: ספירות העליונות כסא אחד</note>. <margin>F</margin> In this throne sits the "Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Hosts."

To the **Goodness** <note>original: *Ati*?</note>, or **Clemency** <note>original: *Chesed*</note>, which is the **Fourth Numeration**, along with the divine name **El**, these are also appropriated: Grace; Mercy; the Right Arm; the Innocent; the Third Day; White Fire; the Face of the Lion; the First Foot; Abraham the Elder; the East; the Upper Waters; the Silver of God; Michael; the Priest; the Angel in the appearance of amber <note>original: *Hasmal*</note>; White Garments; the South; and others. 

In the **Fifth Numeration** <margin>G</margin> of **Severity** <note>original: *Gevurah*</note>, the divine name is **Elohim**. To it are applied: Fear; the property of rigor or weight; the negative precepts of the Law; the Left Arm; fire proceeding from the waters (as in the *Book of Creation*); likewise the Fourth Day; the West; Gabriel; Isaac the Elder; Night; Fortitude; the Golden Altar; the Second Foot; Sanctification; Darkness; Metattron; the North; the Dark Hue. The Sixth...

### BOOK THREE

->Hh iij<-

To the **Sixth** [Sephirah] <note>Tiferet or "Beauty"</note> is applied *Eloha* <note>God; original: *Eloha*</note>, the illuminating speculation, the tree of life, delight, the middle line, the written law, the high priest, the rising of the sun, and the color purple. And Todros Levi <note>original: *Tedacus Leui*; likely Todros ben Joseph Halevi Abulafia, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note> writes that from this place the seventy nations on earth are explained; its seal is *Emeth Adonai* <note>The Truth of the Lord; original: *Emeth Adonai*</note>, and it is called "Peace." Its form is figured in the moon, and its mystery is the third letter of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH; the third letter is 'Vav'</note>. This mystery is "Our Father who is in heaven," the supernal man or the heavenly Adam, judgment, sentence, Michael <note>the Archangel</note>, Israel the Elder, and the God of Jacob. <margin>B</margin> To the **Seventh** [Sephirah] <note>Netzach or "Victory"</note> are referred *Adonai Sabaoth* <note>Lord of Hosts; original: *Adonai Sabaoth*</note>, the leg, the foot, the column, the right side, the great wheel, the vision of prophecy, Moses, and the rest. To the **Eighth** [Sephirah] <note>Hod or "Splendor"</note> belong *Elohe Sabaoth* <note>God of Hosts; original: *Elohe Sabaoth*</note>, the mystery of the column and the left foot, and *Boaz* <note>One of the two pillars of Solomon’s Temple</note>; from here is drawn the ancient serpent, the discipline of the Lord, the branch, Aaron, the Cherub, the sons of the King, the grinding mills, and other things. <margin>C</margin> To the **Ninth** [Sephirah] <note>Yesod or "Foundation"</note> is appropriated *Shaddai* <note>The Almighty; original: *Sadai*</note>, the foundation of the world, Zion, the fountain of pools, the Just One, the Living God, the complete Sabbath, the middle point between "Keep" and "Remember," the fiftieth day of Leviathan, the Ram, Joseph the Just, Solomon, justice, strength, the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the covenant of the Lord, the bow of the witness, the glory of the Lord, the foundation of the prophecy of David, redemption, and the world of souls. Finally, they are reduced to the **Tenth** numeration <note>Malkhut or "Kingdom"</note>, *Adonai* <note>Lord; original: *Adonai*</note>, kingdom, life, the second Cherub, non-illuminating speculation, the "back parts," the End, the Assembly of Israel, the Bride in the Song of Songs, the Queen of Heaven, the Virgin of Israel, the mystery of the law given by mouth <note>The Oral Torah</note>, the Eagle, the fourth letter of the Tetragrammaton, <margin>D</margin> the kingdom of the house of David, the Temple of the King, the gate of God, the Ark of the Covenant and the two tables within it, and the Lord of the whole earth.

<margin>E</margin> You have heard a brief accounting of the ten properties, or notions, or attributes in divine matters. These are called by the Kabbalists *Belimah* <note>original Hebrew: בלימה</note>. Some understand this as *Beli-mah* <note>original Hebrew: בלי מה</note>, which means "without" or "beyond" <note>original: *absque*</note> and "what" <note>original: *quid*</note>; as if one were to say: "Ten beyond the 'whatness'"—that is, excepting the very essence <note>quiddity</note> of God. Hence they usually interpret *Belimah* as being beyond that which is ineffable. Others derive it from the phrase <note>original Hebrew: בלום פיך ולשונך מלדבר</note> "restrain your mouth from speaking and your tongue from talking," regarding them as sacred words that must not be betrayed to the common folk.

<margin>F</margin> It would now be time to speak of the angelic princes and the demonic prefects, whom the Kabbalists place at the sides of Mercy and Severity. This is a matter truly requiring much speech, and we would be carried into the evening having already passed midday. For who could explain such great things in so short a time? Who could so quickly finish describing the thirty-five princes of purity and the seventy princes of Ishmael on the side of the fourth numeration <note>Chesed/Mercy</note>? Who, likewise, in the fifth numeration of gravity and fear <note>Gevurah/Severity</note>, could sufficiently explain the thirty-five princes of guilt and the seventy princes of Esau in such a passing and perfunctory way? These things require their own volumes, and quite large ones at that; therefore, setting these aside for the present, let us proceed to the Art.

<margin>G</margin> I say that the blessedness of the most contemplative men depends—according to the choice of meditation on the Law (that is, the twenty-four books <note>The Hebrew Bible, often called *Esrim ve-Arba* in Hebrew; the text uses a Latinized *Ephrim Varba*</note>)—on a day and night devotion, as is gathered from the sacred letters. For it is written: "Blessed is the man..." (among other things)

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> "...who will meditate on His law day and night." It does not say "who reads," nor "who writes," nor "who speaks," but "who meditates." This is lest, perhaps, the writing or reading of the law might eventually reach a conclusion and cease, thereby compelling blessedness also to cease and end. But he, at last, who compels the thoughts in his heart toward that place—so that, having dismissed carnal things, he meditates on the spiritual things of the law—he (I say), he is blessed, for with a pure heart he shall see God. <margin>B</margin> For in my judgment, there was not so much need for diligence regarding the histories of Sacred Scripture, which are as plain to the Hebrews as Titus Livius is to the Latins. Likewise for the commandments and precepts, which have a set number, and for the religious rites and ceremonies, which are performed even by the unrefined and unlearned common folk—often not without vice or sin. Therefore, these things do not deserve such great blessedness, consisting as they do in bodily senses, such that they would require so constant, so continuous, and so diligent a meditation day and night.

<margin>C</margin> But it is demonstrated that a far greater blessedness can be found in the higher levels of theory, which tends toward the Kabbalistic understanding of the law to such an extent that it imbues our minds with spiritual meditation and forms them, as it were, into its own likeness. This, we conjecture, is the meditation on the law which was delivered from the mouth of God to Moses after the law was given in fire, and after the stone tablets were broken and then repaired. For first, as the Kabbalah asserts, God wrote His law in a fiery globe, using dark fire upon white fire. For Ramban of Girona <note>The 13th-century scholar Nachmanides; original: *Ramban Gerundensis*</note> says: <margin>D</margin> "What appears to us through Kabbalah is that the writing was in black fire upon the back of white fire" <note>original Hebrew: שבא לנו בקבלה שהייתה כתובה באש שחורה על גבי אש לבנה</note>. From this comes that passage in Deuteronomy 33: "From His right hand a fiery law for them."

And then the letters were (as they say) confused and massed together. Those who were most studious, looking upon them speculatively and considering them diligently, led by the Holy Spirit, could easily choose from here and there—up and down, back and forth, forward and backward—to read, collect, and <margin>E</margin> form into any words a sentence signifying good for the good, and evil for the evil. However, Moses, having been taught by God, reduced them all into the order to be published to the people, so that everyone might know and observe the things that belonged to the law. And from that, the law was divided into books and placed in the Ark, just as he received it from the Lord.

Yet the Art of ordering and varying the letters, and of interpreting the Sacred Scripture most sweetly for the elevation of the mind—which was received then from the Divine Majesty <margin>F</margin> as a most divine thing imperceptible to the unrefined—he did not reveal to the common people. Instead, by command, he delivered it "mouth to mouth" <note>orally</note> only to the chosen seventy elders, from whom afterwards the most elite always received it. And that reception, as you heard before, was named Kabbalah <note>literally "Reception"</note>. Even the most learned Christian Doctors agree with this somewhat; I have read many of them, for although I am a Jew, I gladly creep into foreign camps as a scout. <margin>G</margin> Concerning our Moses, Gregory Nazianzen <note>4th-century Church Father</note>, that Greek surnamed "the Great Theologian," says in his book *On the State of Bishops*: "He receives the law: for the many, that which is in the letter; for those above the many, that which is in the spirit" <note>original Greek: δέχεται νόμον, τοῖς μὲν πολλοῖς, τὸν τῷ γράμ-ματι τοῖς δὲ ὑπὲρ τοὺς πολλοὺς, τὸν τῷ πνεύματι</note>.

It then introduces the "Art" of Kabbalah as the spiritual meditation on the Hebrew letters of the Torah, which were originally given as a mass of "black fire on white fire" to be rearranged by those with divine insight.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion on the methods of Kabbalah. ### ON KABBALAH

<margin>A</margin> [Moses] receives the law: for the many, he receives the law of the letter; but for those who are above the many, he receives the law of the spirit. And in the first book of *Theology*, <note>likely referring to the *Oration on the Law* by Gregory of Nazianzus</note> it says: "He will engrave it upon tablets that are solid and made of stone, and these on both sides, because of that which is manifest in the law and that which is hidden; the former for the many who remain below, the latter for the few who reach the heights." <note>original Greek: "βαλεῖ τῷ πλαξὶ σεῤῥαῖς καὶ λιθίναις ἐγγεγραμμένῃ... πρὸς τοῖς ὀλίγοις καὶ ἄνω φθάνουσι."</note> That is, he wished it to be written on solid, stone tablets on both sides to represent the manifest and the secret aspects of the law—the one for the many staying below, the other for the few who ascend. <margin>B</margin> From these words, it appears to some very learned men, even among your own people, that Moses delivered the text of the law to the common people, but reserved the mysteries, parables, and symbols for himself and the more excellent men. 

We have learned that this art of Kabbalah was divided into three paths, according to the testimony of Solomon, who says in Proverbs 22: "Have I not written to you in a threefold way, with counsel and knowledge, that I might make known to you the certainty of the words of truth?" <note>Proverbs 22:20-21</note> For our people are accustomed to speak this way when Kabbalah is mentioned, calling it <margin>C</margin> *Words of Truth* <note>original Hebrew: אמרי אמת / Imrei Emet</note>, written namely *according to the way of truth* <note>original Hebrew: על דרך האמת / Al Derech HaEmet</note>, which is Kabbalah. This custom was frequent with the Egyptian <note>likely Maimonides</note>, the man of Gerona <note>Nachmanides</note>, and others. Others, however, presented five parts of Kabbalah, such as Rabbi Hamai in his *Book of Speculation*, which he names: Ordering, Combination, Discourse, Generalization, and Calculation. <note>original Hebrew: תיקון וצירוף ומאמר ומכלל וחשבון / Tikkun, Tziruf, Maamar, Michlal, Cheshbon</note> 

Your Mirandulanus <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, the famous Renaissance philosopher</note> wrote in his *Nine Hundred Conclusions* in these words: <margin>D</margin> "Whatever other Kabbalists may say, I would distinguish the science of Kabbalah in its primary division into the science of *Sephirot* and *Semoth*—that is, of numbers and names—as if into practical and speculative branches." But Rabbi Joseph bar Abraham of Castile <note>Joseph Gikatilla</note> and by far the greatest part of Kabbalists follow King Solomon, believing that one can not only speculate but also clearly practice that art in a threefold way, according to the triple condition of all things: number, figure, and weight, reducing those five parts into these three. 

Since the whole business is allegorical, and one thing is understood for another through a third—just as one meaning stands for another—we shall say openly that either a word is put for a word, or a letter for a word, or a letter for a letter. First, a word is taken for a word, either by transposition (which is called *metathesis*) or by an equal number included in the words <note>This is Gematria: calculating the numerical value of letters to find hidden connections.</note>. <margin>F</margin> A letter is put for a word, either at the beginning, at the end, or anywhere else, by a mark placed above it <note>This is Notarikon: using letters as acronyms.</note>. A letter is put for another letter through a complete alphabetical revolution, so that every proportion—arithmetic, geometric, and musical—is finally completed <note>This is Temurah: substituting letters according to a cipher.</note>. 

For example, take that verse of Psalm 21: "Lord, in your strength the King shall rejoice." We understand this Kabbalistically as referring to the Messiah, saying: "Lord Tetragrammaton, in your strength the Messiah King [comes or works]." For the Messiah is the power of God and works in the power of the Tetragrammaton. I am led to this by the word *ismach* <note>original Hebrew: ישמח / "he shall rejoice"</note>; if its letters are transposed, it becomes *mashiach* <note>original Hebrew: משיח / Messiah</note>. 

Likewise, in another place, the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, my Angel shall go before you" (Exodus 23). Who is that Angel according to the Kabbalists? Some say it is Michael, by transposing...
<meta>catchword: enim (for)</meta>

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> ...for by transposing the letters of *Maleachi* <note>Hebrew: מלכאי / "my messenger" or "Malachi"</note> one gets *Michael*. Others, taking this according to the method of the Kabbalistic art, affirm it is *Metattron* <note>Metatron, the highest angel in Jewish mysticism</note>, because God said, "For my name is in him." In the name *Metattron*, the name *Shaddai* <note>Hebrew: שדי / Almighty</note> is contained by an equal number included in both words <note>Both Metatron and Shaddai equal 314 in Gematria.</note>. This is wonderfully embraced by the man of Gerona <note>Nachmanides</note> in the place cited before. 

Do you now see two symbolic paths of Kabbalah? Would you also like to see the third, where a letter <margin>B</margin> is substituted for a word? Read Isaiah chapter 65: "He shall be blessed in God, Amen." Who is this God? The Kabbalists will answer that it is *Adonai Melekh Ne'eman* <note>Hebrew: אדני מלך נאמן / "The Lord, the Faithful King"</note>; for these three words are noted by their first letters in the three letters of *Amen* <note>A-M-N</note>, as Recanati wrote on Exodus 15. 

The fourth species and third part of Kabbalah is the literary commutation, where a word written with certain letters symbolically designates another word composed of other letters. <margin>C</margin> This happens through an alphabetical revolution according to Abraham's *Book of Creation* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*</note> in twenty-two variations, according to the number of alphabets read there. An example is given to us by *Mazpaz*, a name of God, which is written with these four letters: מצפץ. Your Mirandulanus says of this: "The four-letter name of God consisting of *Mem*, *Tsade*, *Pe*, and *Tsade* must be appropriated to the Kingdom of David." Since this is clearly not read in the text of Holy Scripture, of what, I ask, shall it be held to be a symbol? 

The Kabbalists answer that it is a symbol and seal <margin>D</margin> of the ineffable Tetragrammaton, and it proceeds from the last alphabet (which is the twenty-second of the book called *Sefer Yetzirah*), and it is called *Ath bash* <note>A cipher where the first letter is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>. There, *Yod* is exchanged for *Mem*, *He* for *Tsade*, and *Vav* for *Pe*, so that the Tetragrammaton <note>Y-H-W-H</note> becomes *Mazpaz* <note>M-TZ-P-TZ</note>. 

I have just spoken of things pertaining to the "Art," which involves crossing, transposing, or commuting words, syllables, or letters according to four methods by which the senses of the scriptures are ingeniously and artistically allegorized. <margin>E</margin> For regarding those things that exist without the Art, and are done by tradition alone as "unwritten" <note>Greek: ἄγραφα / agrapha</note>, I have made you more than sufficiently informed—even though both of you, by your profession, had already acquired no small amount of knowledge of them through your own study. Namely, how simple things are abstracted from the composite, and higher things from the lower, and how almost everything is referred to the intelligible world, or the supreme and incomparable world. 

Certain arguments of piety can also often come to our minds while reading the sacred letters, which first draw us into admiration of divine things <margin>F</margin> and then into love for them; yet these cannot be handed down by any certain "Art." For instance, the idea that Gabriel is of stronger power than Michael, because it is read of him in Daniel: "flying with a double power of flight," while of Michael it says only that he "came to help." Therefore, among the Intelligences, Gabriel is philosophically considered the power of the *Active Intellect*, and Michael the power of the *Passive Intellect*. So writes Rabbi Levi ben Gerson <margin>G</margin> (known by the Latins as Master Leo de Banolis). 

Philolaus said: "It seems to me, best Simon, that what you call 'unskilled' or 'without art' contributes a great deal to the Kabbalistic art; for unless the revelations of the elders are held in hand—which you rightly think do not strictly fall under 'Art'—the whole thing would be..."
<meta>catchword: quantum (as much as)</meta>

It distinguishes between the "Art" of letter manipulation and the "unwritten tradition" received from the elders.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of the "Art of Kabbalah." The previous page established that the Law of Moses has both a literal surface for the masses and a spiritual, secret depth for the enlightened. ### BOOK THREE

<margin>A</margin> ...however much a reckless license has been granted to everyone to explain and twist Sacred Scripture wherever they wish, just as we have seen certain common sophists do in this age. They seem, through their syllogisms, to have brought those most holy oracles of the Divine Spirit into nearly public contempt. But now, since all things are (as I believe) to be applied to what has been revealed, a certain line is drawn, which

<margin>B</margin> **B**eyond or before which right cannot stand,
<note>A reference to Horace, Satires 1.1.106: "There is a measure in things... beyond and short of which right cannot find a footing."</note> so that the works of the worst men, which belong to art, do not decline into laziness. Then Simon said, "You speak the truth openly. For there is almost nothing else that is more errantly twisted to each person’s own sense than the oracles, although this is not always done out of malice, but often more through ignorance. For who would intentionally commit a sacrilege against the sacred?" Thus Saul was once deceived by the ambiguity of a word and wandered from the oracle, when God promised in Exodus 17: "I will blot out the memory of Amalek" <note>original Hebrew: אמחה את זכר עמלק / Emcheh et zeker Amalek</note>. Saul believed that if he killed the males, the command would be satisfied, because the word *zakar* <note>זכר</note> signifies "male." However, God intended the "memory" of Amalek to be blotted out, using the word *zeker* <note>זכר</note>, which also designates memory. For at that time, there was not yet a distinction in the scripture through vowel points and accents, which first began in the years of Ezra.

<margin>C</margin> Therefore, the word *ZKR* without points, expressing both "memory" and "male," gave Saul the occasion for his ruin. To this Marranus added: "A similar thing happened to both the Italians and Greeks regarding the word *phōs* <note>φῶς</note>, which signifies both 'man' and 'light.' <note>In Greek, phōs with an accent on the omega means 'light,' but with an accent on the omicron, it is an archaic word for 'man.'</note> Whence formerly the worshippers of the Saturnalia, deceived by this ambiguity, sacrificed a man every year to Saturn, when that sacrifice could just as well have been performed by lighting lamps according to the oracle, to appease Saturn. Thus that foolish people finally came to their senses under the teaching of Hercules. And it is a pitiable thing even in our own age how much dull men and certain proud sophists err through their ignorance of languages; this might be bearable, if they did not insist they had not erred, and if they did not envy, even to the point of destruction, those who show them the way. But, O our leader, proceed more fully with the Kabbalistic art, the beginning of which you have already touched upon." Then Simon said, "It is the opinion of the more experienced, as we have said, that this art consists of three things."

<margin>D</margin> First, by the calculation of numbers, which is named **Gematria** <note>גנטריא / Ghematria</note>, that is, "Geometry," as if it were a numerical dimension of earthly characters in relation to one another. This, however, depends on that Arithmetic which, because of its abstract simplicity, is not tactile to the senses, and therefore is not subject even to the skill of novices. Thus, the first part is called Geometry rather than Arithmetic, although both in truth signify one and the same thing in this art.

<margin>E</margin> Second, sometimes syllables are transposed so that the word itself is changed, or the word is simply reversed. This is called **Notariacon** <note>נוטריקון</note> from the marks of the notaries, because there every letter is noted at its peak so that it acts as a sign for some whole word. <note>Essentially an acrostic or shorthand system where single letters represent entire phrases.</note>

<margin>F</margin> Third, this art consists in the mutation of letters, when one is ingeniously placed for another; this is called **Commutation** <note>תמורה / Themura</note>. Because of this, Rabbi Joseph the Minor of Salerno named the books he wrote on this art "The Garden," that is,

<column-break/>

### BOOK THREE

<margin>A</margin> **Ginat** <note>גנת</note>, because of the three letters of this word, each of which designates a portion of the Kabbalistic art. For the letter *Gimel* signifies **Gematria** <note>גנטריא</note>, *Nun* signifies **Notariacon** <note>נוטריקון</note>, and *Thau* signifies **Themura** <note>תמורה</note>. Thus, these are the parts of the whole craft: Arithmetic, Shorthand, and the Commutation of elements. Regarding this title, the author cites a verse of Solomon from the sixth chapter of the Song of Songs: "I went down into the garden of nuts." <note>Song of Solomon 6:11</note> For the first part, therefore, I shall begin

<margin>B</margin> from that which is the beginning. And it is written in Zechariah that the Lord of the Four-Letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> will be "one" <note>אחד / echad</note>, and his name "one" <note>אחד / echad</note>. Perhaps much more truly, the Lord God will be *Aleph* <note>א</note>, that is, the beginning—as you Greeks say, the "Alpha and Omega"—and *Aleph* also signifies "one," as He who is the beginning of the one. For He Himself is above all unity and is the eternal origin of all unity. And perhaps He is not called "one" just as He is not called "being," because He is above every being from which whatever exists emanates.

<margin>C</margin> Whence He is named by the most contemplative as **Non-Being** <note>אין / Ayin</note>, as read in Exodus 17: "Is the Lord among us, or not?" <note>Exodus 17:7; the Hebrew word for 'not' is *Ayin*, which the Kabbalists interpret as the 'Nothingness' or 'Infinite' from which all 'Being' emerges.</note> It is read, however, in the book *On the Way of Faith and Expiation*, that He is both **Being and Non-Being** <note>היש ואין / Ha-Yesh ve-ha-Ayin</note>: because those things which are, and those which are not, are from Him and are after Him. So also He is not "one," because He is the cause of all unity, and unity is after Him. He is none of those things, whether they are after Him or are not, as is said in the *Book of Speculation* by Rabbi Hamai, who after many words

<margin>D</margin> says this: "That all things are derived from His unity, yet He Himself is not like that 'one'." <note>original Hebrew: שבלם נאצלים מאחדותו והוא אינו דומה לאחד</note> Nor do our people alone confess this, but your own people also assert it, Marranus, whom you prove to be most wise. For Dionysius the Areopagite, in the book *On Mystical Theology*, subscribed to the same sentiment concerning God with these words: "He is neither number, nor order, nor one, nor unity." <note>original Greek: οὔτε ἀριθμός ἐστιν, οὔτε τάξις, οὔτε ἕν, οὔτε ἑνότης</note>

<margin>E</margin> What then is He? Simonides responded to Hiero: "The more I think, the less I understand." And a similar thing happens to me: when, having passed all created things, I ascend above every being, I find nothing other than an infinite sea of nothingness, and the fountain of all entity flowing perpetually from the abyss of darkness. O height! O depth! O our weakness! But it ought to seem sufficient that we know of Him what He Himself has revealed to us of Himself,

<margin>F</margin> because He is the beginning, which is *Aleph*, and the Four-Letter Name <note>Tetragrammaton</note>, which is signified by *Aleph*, and notes the divine essence—which is nothing else than "He is" <note>הויה / hovayah</note>, which is certainly almost the same as the essence of the Name <note>יהוה / YHWH</note>. For because of their equal numerical value, Scripture joined them both, as belonging to Him who is the first and the last. Exodus 9: "Behold, the hand of the Lord *is*..." <note>original Hebrew: הנה יד יהוה הויה / Hinneh yad Adonai hoyah</note> as if to say, "is"—namely, the end of the works and miracles of God, as is evident in the ten plagues of Egypt. For that word is not found elsewhere.

<margin>G</margin> Moreover, it indicates an infinite essence by the testimony of Solomon of Trecanis. The fact that the Four-Letter Name begins with the letter *Yod* was clearly done for our sake, so that we might recognize that He Himself is the infinite point and the origin of every number—that is, of every thing...

### OF KABBALAH

...of each fulfillment. For *Iod* <note>The Hebrew letter Yod (י)</note> signifies ten. And in the expansion of the name Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-lettered name of God, YHWH, considered too sacred to pronounce.</term> it is the tenth letter, thus: *Iod, Iod-He, Iod-He-Waw, Iod-He-Waw-He* <note>original: יוד יהוה יהו יה — these are the progressive stages of spelling out the Name</note>. Where, after the Tetragrammaton, is found *Iaho* <note>יהו</note>, which is the symbol of *Ehieh* <note>אהיה</note> itself—that is, of Being—by an equality of number. And nonetheless, it signifies the essence of the Creator, as in Exodus 3: *Ehieh* <gloss>I AM</gloss> sent me to you; not that which remains within, but that which flows outward. For *Iaho* <note>יהו</note> is the seal of God with which *Ehieh* sealed the world, and it is called *Emet* <gloss>Truth</gloss>, because it is born from itself by arithmetical multiplication. 

Then follows *Iah* <note>יה</note>, the name of the essence of merit and retribution, as in the Psalms: *If you, Iah, should mark iniquities.* Thus you see three essential names in the Tetragrammaton. The Ineffable Name denotes the primary essence; *Ehieh* denotes essence in things; and *Iah* denotes essence in merits. And they are predicated in the "whatness" of a thing. This is called *Mah* <gloss>What?</gloss>. For the Tetragrammaton <note>יהוה</note>, through an equality of number, signifies *Mah* <note>מה</note>, for both contain the value of 45 <note>In Gematria, the spelled-out letters of YHWH (Yod+He+Waw+He) equal 45, the same as the word Mah (What).</note>. And when Moses said, "What is His name, what shall I say?" He answered him, *Ehieh*. 

Then consider diligently the words of the Holy Spirit, which are not placed in that same Exodus 3 in vain: *Mah Shemo, Mah* <note>מה שמו מה</note>, that is: "To me, what is His name, what?" And look at their terminal letters; you will have the ineffable four-letter name <note>יהוה / YHWH</note> whose beginning is *Ehieh*, its middle is *Iah*, and its end is infinity. For its parts are *Iah* and *Iaho*, as if we divide it into three intervals. The first is *Iah*, the second is *Iaho*, the third is the Tetragrammaton—all serving "to be" and "essence." 

Of *Iah*, we read in Exodus 15: *My strength and my praise is Iah.* Of the Tetragrammaton in the same place: *And He has become my salvation.* Of *Yehi* <note>יהי</note> in the first chapter of Genesis: *Let there be light.* Both of these last words contributed greatly to the workmanship of the world and the existence of things, as in: *Let there be light, and there was light. And there was evening, and there was morning. Let there be a firmament, and let there be a distinction, and it was so. Let the waters be gathered, and it was so. Let the earth sprout, and it was so. Let the earth bring forth, and it was so. Let there be lights, and it was so.* Always adding this: *And there was evening, and there was morning.* In all these things (that they might truly be), we perceive that the Ineffable Name is present in a seminal and hidden way. 

We see only *Elohim* <gloss>God</gloss> expressed in those six days. But when the world now appeared to be perfect, after various and wonderful works of the most divine virtues were completed, and finally a triumph was to be celebrated for merit, and a festival day proclaimed: behold, when the Tetragrammaton *Elohim*, King of kings and Lord of lords, walked forth, it was said then for the first time: *These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Tetragrammaton Elohim made the heaven and the earth.* 

Here the Tetragrammaton first thundered publicly in the ears of all creatures, by which we understand the mercy of God joined with justice. For in whatever place of Sacred Scripture the Tetragrammaton joins itself to *Elohim*, there we notice the property of mercy and justice together. It is sometimes compounded with *Adonai* <gloss>Lord</gloss>, as in the prayer of Habakkuk: *The Tetragrammaton Adonai is my strength.* And we, by reading it thus, understand the power of the Tetragrammaton to descend to *Adonai* itself as it is uttered. But if it is found in the reversed order, *Adonai* Tetragrammaton, as in Ge-

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> nesis 15: *Adonai Tetragrammaton, what will You give me?* Then we conceive in the mind that the *Sefirot* <note>The author uses 'numerationes,' the Latin translation for Sefirot—the ten divine emanations.</note>, that is, the divine properties, ascending from the lower to the higher, take hold of the supreme light. 

It also happens sometimes that the name *El* is found joined. In Psalm 118: *El Tetragrammaton, and He has shone upon us*, and this signifies mercy. Not dissimilarly, when *Elohim* is added, and it is said thus: *El Elohim Tetragrammaton has spoken, and called the earth* <margin>B</margin> in Psalm 50; then it denotes the Ineffable Name clothed in grace and severity. Sometimes it is read—and this only in the Prophecies and the *Hagiographa* <term>Hagiographa: The 'Holy Writings' or Ketuvim, the third section of the Hebrew Bible.</term>—as *Tetragrammaton Sabaoth*. In Psalm 46: *The Tetragrammaton Sabaoth is with us, our protector is the God of Jacob.* This way of speaking suggests the property of judgment. And for that reason, the Prophets use that style in rebuking with severity. 

Regarding explanations of this kind, you will be able to search more broadly in the book *Gates of Light* <note>Sha'are Orah by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, and most extensively in the book *Gates of Justice* by Rabbi Joseph Carnitolis <note>Joseph Gikatilla, often called 'Chiquitilla' or 'Carnitolis' in Latin texts.</note>. Furthermore, concerning the thirteen <margin>C</margin> properties of the same Tetragrammaton, which the lawgiver Moses invoked in Exodus 34, in this sense: *Tetragrammaton, Lord God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, of much mercy, and true, keeping mercy unto thousands, taking away iniquity, passing over crime and sin, and the innocent shall not be innocent, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children unto the third and fourth generation.* 

I call upon you here, you best of men: for I am pleased to say this certainly without <margin>D</margin> falsehood, since there would be need of much study and many words for one who wished to publish all the mysteries of the name Tetragrammaton, of which no end is ever found, just as there is no end to the substance of God. Therefore, leaving aside the proper name of the divine essence, I will show a few derivatives in number. For it is customary, according to the decree of grammarians, that we form appellative names from proper ones. 

These are *El, Elohim, Eloha* <note>אל אלהים אלוה</note>, each of which has obtained its origin from the ineffable Tetragrammaton, <margin>E</margin> which contains four letters—behold, four—and designates 26—behold, twenty-six—all of which are one symbol of God—behold, one. Join these individual numbers, namely four, twenty-six, and one, and it becomes *El* <note>The Hebrew word 'El' (אל) has a gematria value of 31. Reuchlin's math: 4 letters + 26 value + 1 (the unity) = 31.</note>. If you add the termination of the Tetragrammaton, *Iah* <note>יה</note>, to this, *Eloha* will be born. 

Now concerning *Elohim*, it is said that its ending *im* <note>ים</note> is not a significance of the thing, but a grammatical inflection, which appears from this: for if it were to be read through an affix or a construct state, <margin>F</margin> there is no doubt that it would lack the letter *Mem* <note>ם</note>. Therefore, if you add *El* to the beginning of the Tetragrammaton *Iah* in reverse order, it soon becomes *Elohi*, and by assuming the grammatical declension, which is *im* at the end, it will be pronounced *Elohim*. This is also often written with the letters of the Ineffable Name, and yet pointed as *Elohim*. 

In Kabbalah, there is a frequent use of reversed order <term>Themura: The Kabbalistic art of permuting or transposing letters to find hidden meanings.</term>, and great is its virtue and the praise of its virtue. For in whatever way the syllables are transposed, the letters nevertheless remain the same without diminution, although the meanings are often not the same. <margin>G</margin> Abraham mentions this matter in the *Book of Formation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note> when he says: *Male and female; male in Emes, and female in Esem* <note>original: זכר ונקבה זכר באמש ונקבה באשם</note>, where the transposition of letters indicates a change in the thing as well. For example, *El* <gloss>God</gloss> and *Lo* <gloss>Not</gloss>...

<margin>A</margin> Not so. This will be more manifest to you by its use: if the name Tetragrammaton be resolved into twelve variations (for we cannot proceed further), then whatever is found will serve nothing other than that Essence, whose symbols are these:

These twelve names, therefore, are considered as one name among the Kabbalists, as signifying a single thing, although there are twelve explanatory versions. For instance, if I were to say, "Attend and hear, Israel, today," which is read in Deuteronomy chapter 27. <margin>C</margin> You will note the first letters of these four words, and they form **יהוה** <note>YHWH</note>, which is the Name of the Essence and the resolution of the Tetragrammaton; let the others be formed from the rest in like manner. <margin>D</margin> God, before creation, was **Ineffable**; in creation, He was named *Elohim*; and after creation, dwelling in the world as if in His temple, He is called **אדני** *Adonai* <gloss>Lord</gloss>. Whence it is read in Psalm 11: "The Tetragrammaton is in his holy temple, the Tetragrammaton’s throne is in the heavens"—as He who rules in His works. For He is, as the Scripture says in Deuteronomy 10, "The God of gods and the Lord of lords, the Great One." Therefore, the "Temple" <note>original: היכל — Hekhal</note> is a Kabbalistic sign for *Adonai*, and vice versa, through an equality of number <note>In Gematria, both Adonai (אדני) and Hekhal (היכל) equal 65.</note>. Just as in *Adonai* as if in His own temple, the Ineffable **Tetragrammaton** is to be adored,
<margin>E</margin> and God is to be loved in God, according to the triple world, as in Jeremiah 7: "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord." There remains another appellative name, **שדי** *Sadai* <gloss>Shaddai</gloss>. In Exodus 6: "I am the Tetragrammaton, and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as *El Sadai* <gloss>God Almighty</gloss>, and my name Tetragrammaton I did not make known to them." Here, only this is called His name which is Ineffable, because this alone 
<margin>F</margin> is proper to the Most High God, insofar as He is nothing of those things that exist, but is above all things, having no regard outside Himself. Other names are appellatives of other properties and relations, such as *Sadai*, which the Latins translated as "Omnipotent" <gloss>Almighty</gloss>, but is more aptly signified in Hebrew as "Self-sufficient," content in Himself and needing nothing, which the Greeks more correctly interpret as **αὐτάρκης** <gloss>autarkes / self-sufficient</gloss>. For grammatically we say *She* (ש), that is "who" or "which," and *Dai* (די), "suffices" or "is enough."
<margin>G</margin> Furthermore, if you hear the word **שם** *Shem* <gloss>The Name</gloss> used alone in the sacred texts, let the Tetragrammaton immediately come to your mind, which *par excellence* <note>original Greek: κατ’ ἐξοχὴν</note> and hyperbolically is called the "Name above every name,"

He did not, however, let them know that the name Tetragrammaton is that name in which a man, as a co-operator and delegate of God, can perform miracles. <margin>B</margin> To this is added another name, **Sabaoth**, which is read in Hebrew as **צבאות**, and thus are called the "hosts" or "armies." The first of these is of entirely separate Intelligences and Angels. The second is of the movers of the spheres and the assisting Virtues. The third is of the souls informing bodies. <margin>E</margin> on account of the primary confusion of letters that had appeared in the fiery globe, so that it was permitted to draw letters out as if from chaos, and to read them here and there, forwards and backwards; thus the first species of the first part is completed. Rebecca therefore conceived fire and stubble, which the sacred utterances prove by the testimony of Obadiah, who says: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Esau stubble." Similarly, when

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between Simon, a Kabbalist, and Marranus, a skeptic, regarding the mystical properties of the Hebrew language. The previous page discussed the permutations of the Divine Name; here, the text explores "Gematria" (numerical values) and "Notarikon" (acronyms), specifically regarding the 613 commandments and the origins of the name "Maccabee."</meta>

...the term is **חסד** <note>Chesed: Hebrew for "Mercy" or "Loving-kindness".</note>, that is, the Wisdom of all the commandments of God. For when you pronounce the four elements of that word from their own writings—**חית סמך דלת** <note>These are the names of the letters spelled out: Cheth (Heth), Samekh, and Daleth.</note>—there will be forged from them the number of six hundred and thirteen commandments of God, which our teachers call **תריג** <note>Taryag: The traditional count of the 613 mitzvot (laws) in the Torah.</note>. To reach the peak of this kind of speculation, it will be worth remembering: first, that the characters, elements, and letters of the Law were originally placed in a state of confusion, yet these and those were still legible. Second, they were distinguished by no accents or vowel points. Third, each primordial letter of the alphabet signifies a specific number—even the five terminal letters <note>Final forms of letters used only at the end of words.</note>, which the wise Ezra found long afterward, together with the vowel points. For there are twenty-two primitive letters, by which alone all scripture was depicted from the beginning; the Kabbalists to this day place and displace these for the beauty of any pleasant contemplation. Finally, we must aim for this universal goal: although it is the Kabbalist’s duty to read one thing and understand another, let everyone nonetheless inviolably observe this canon: good things for good, evil things for evil, lest he apply black to white, or day to night. 

Then Marranus said: "I would think of that kind of art as being no different than if someone called some 'Dorotheus' by the name 'Theodorus,' or 'Demonicus' instead of 'Nicodemus,' or 'Philodemus' instead of 'Demophilus'—just as the Greeks are accustomed to say, a <term>body-lover</term> <note>original Greek: σωματόφιλον</note> or a <term>lover of bodies</term> <note>original Greek: φιλοσώματον</note>."

To this Simon replied: "Certainly, what you say is not without merit, but you will be exhausted quite quickly in enumerating examples because of the poverty of other languages. Compared to Hebrew, which is the fountain of all languages, they are poor and impatient with their own lack, as they must adopt the idioms of other nations. They neither accept the full numerical value nor admit a useful composition. Therefore, this art cannot be translated into the speech of another nation at all. Unless I knew you were equally skilled in Hebrew, I would have discussed these few matters of Kabbalah with you in vain, or would be doing so now. But let us proceed quickly to the second part of this instruction, which is called **נֹוטָרִיקֹון** <note>Notarikon</note>, that is <term>notariacon</term> <term>Notariacon: A method of shorthand or acronyms where single letters represent entire words.</term>. This is a certain convention secretly accepted among the Kabbalists so that individual letters, without the joining of syllables, designate specific words. This is just as is the custom for notaries and actuaries, and as the secret writings of military commanders once brought forth the secrets of the mind through single letters placed in a disorganized way. There is even a commentary by the grammarian Probus <note>Marcus Valerius Probus, a Roman grammarian.</note>, as Aulus Gellius writes, quite carefully made concerning the hidden meaning of letters. Perhaps it happens in the pursuit of this art much like those who agree among themselves that the letter *Yod* <note>י</note>—because of the shape of its indivisible point—signifies the ineffable **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Name of God, YHWH.</note>, which we commonly interpret as 'Lord.' Just as they are accustomed to mark that same Name with three points because of the three **עליונות** <note>Elyonot</note>, that is, the summits in the ten numerations <note>The Sephirot, or divine emanations.</note>, which are one and the same **עטרה** <note>Atarah</note>, that is, one crown. For the Kabbalists say: <term>because for this mystery they write the Name as three yods, like this: י"י</term> <note>original Hebrew: כי לסוד זה כותבין השם ג' יודין כזה י"י</note>. Here, the single four-letter Name is written with three single letters, which is approved by daily use. 

Long ago, in the days of Antiochus Eupator, there was Judas

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> the son of Mattathias, a noble warrior and a most fierce leader of the war for the laws, the temple, the city, the fatherland, and the citizens of the Jews. When Antiochus and his whole army were already rushing against them, Judas, warned by an Angel, gave to his fellow soldiers this noble sign as a watchword of war: **מ.כ.ב.י.** <note>M.K.B.Y.</note>, so that they might bravely exhort themselves in battle with these four letters. He promised that it would be a sign of God's victory. The Jewish soldiers accepted this with a joyful heart as a source of great consolation, and fighting strongly under that 
<margin>B</margin> seal, they slew fourteen thousand men in the camp of Antiochus, along with a huge number of elephants and those who had been placed upon them. Thus it happened that the leader of the war, Judas, who was previously called by that name, was thereafter surnamed **Maccabee** <note>original: Machabaei</note> by everyone, because these four characters sounded that way syllabically. Since they believed themselves to have been the victors of so many battles by the power of that sign, the military tribunes and the 
<margin>C</margin> wise men in Israel wondered, asking Judas how so many triumphs had occurred under this sign given to them? And Judas Maccabeus answered that in that sign was the presence of the ineffable Almighty God. He showed them the words of Moses in Exodus 15, saying: **מי כמוך באלים יהוה** <note>Mi Kamocha Ba-elim YHWH</note>, that is, "Who is like you among the strong, O **Tetragrammaton**?" For these four characters designate these words as their initials, where the letter *Yod* is clearly understood to signify the name Tetragrammaton. Thus, **מ.כ.ב.י.** <note>Maccabee</note> is in truth a memorable symbol of the 
<margin>D</margin> divine Name of 72 letters by numerical equality. Stirred by this, those who were of Judas's army, fighting again, struck down no fewer than 35,000 men, as the writings indicate, being wonderfully delighted by the presence of God and blessing the Almighty Lord **יהוה** <note>YHWH</note> in their native tongue. 

From this, therefore, you understand that an entire word can be signified by a single letter, whether it stands alone or collectively completes any other word—just as a whole phrase is said to mark an entire speech. For example, in **Daniel 5**: **מנא תקל פרסין** <note>Mene, Tekel, Peres</note>, 
<margin>E</margin> that is: "He has numbered, it has been weighed, it is divided." These things represented this to Belshazzar: "God has numbered your kingdom and finished it; it has been weighed in the scales and found wanting; your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians." Therefore, either one phrase dispersed through letters creates many, or many phrases retracted through certain of their letters collect into one; thus, one from many, and many from one. 

That this is by no means strange is shown by the frequent use of two monosyllables, as they say Virgil <note>original: Maronem</note> wrote in his poems: 
> "Yes" and "No": all frequent these well-known monosyllables. 
> Take these away, and there is nothing of human affairs that speech may revolve. 
Therefore, almost all conversations of all men signify "Yes" and "No." Why then, in this art, will anyone doubt that a whole phrase can be noted by one letter, and an extended speech by one phrase, and vice versa, that some chosen and intended word can be noted by one speech? From this arises a certain hidden and wonderful 
<margin>G</margin> <term>art of secret writing</term> <note>original Greek: τεχνογραφία (technographia)</note> which I have often imitated. In grave dangers and the greatest crisis of affairs, I wrote a letter in the German language which I desired to be understood by a Latin man in Tuscany or Etruria, and in reverse, I wrote in Latin what...

### THIRD BOOK.

...which I wanted a German man, unskilled in Latin, to know. I would like you to receive this, whatever it may be, with a grateful heart and in your deepest senses; it is no small thing, so store it away diligently. In our practice, if we work correctly, letters of this kind occur in four ways. For either they are taken from the beginning of a word to signify something else, as in the opening of Genesis: **יום הששי ויכלו השמים** <note>original: "yom ha-shishi vaykhulu ha-shamayim"</note>, that is, "The sixth day, and the heavens were finished" <note>Genesis 1:31–2:1. The first letters of these four words in Hebrew—Yod, He, Vau, He—spell the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter Name of God.</note>, behold the Tetragrammaton. Or they are taken from the end of any word, as in Psalm 1: **לא כן הרשעים** <note>original: "lo khen ha-resha'im"</note> which, when transposed, make **אמן** <note>original: "Amen"</note>, that is, "Amen." For he wanted this to be understood: "Not so the wicked," because they will not say "Amen," and therefore they shall be sent into Gehenna <note>An ancient term for a place of spiritual punishment or purification.</note>. Or there are those letters that present themselves individually, each one contained within a whole word, as in Psalm 3: "Many rise up against me." Who are these "many"? The Kabbalists answer: they are the **רומים** <note>original: "Romim"</note>, that is, the Romans, the Babylonians, the Ionians <note>The Greeks.</note>, and the Medes. Or finally, they are not intended in relation to the construction of other words, but each is taken according to the significance of its own property. For example, when mention is made of the "two worlds," the letter *Iod* signifies the future world, and the letter *He* signifies the present world, namely this world; as in Genesis 2: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth **בהבראם**" <note>original: "be-hibare'am," meaning "when they were created."</note>, that is, "with the letter *He* He created them." Surely this final consideration of the letters pertains to the substance of the character itself, and not at all to an accidental relationship (as in the three methods above). For in this way, by this designation, they signify either the things themselves as offered in their first position according to grammatical instruction, or numbers ordered by the discipline of arithmetic, or certain reasons applied to the words of our masters, or finally, every creature proceeding from the First Cause and reducible back to the First Cause. Concerning the primitive position of the letters, they demonstrate it thus:

* **Aleph** is a "way" or "instruction": whence it is said in Job 33, "I will teach," that is, I will instruct you in wisdom. 
* **Beth** is a "house," Psalm 23: "I will dwell in the house of the Lord." 
* **Gimel** is "retribution" or "recompense," Psalm 116: "Because the Lord has rewarded you." 
* **Daleth** is a "door," "folding-doors," or "gate," Genesis 19: "And they were near to breaking the door." 
* **He** is "behold," Genesis 47: "Behold, here is seed for you." 
* **Vau** is a "twisted hook," Exodus 26: "Of which the capitals shall be gold." 
* **Dsain** <note>Zayin</note> is "weapons," 1 Kings 22: "And they washed the armor according to the word of the Lord." 
* **Heth** is "terror," Job 7: "You terrify me through dreams." 
* **Teth** is a "declining" or "turning away" (by a transposition of sounds), Proverbs 4: "Do not decline to the right or to the left." 
* **Iod** is a "confession of praise," Genesis 49: "Your brothers shall praise you" <note>A pun on the name Judah, which begins with the letter Iod.</note>. 
* **Caph** is the "palm of the hand," Ecclesiastes 4: "Better is a palm full of rest." 
* **Lamed** is "doctrine" or "teaching," Psalm 143: "Teach me to do your will." 
* **Mem** is "waters," Isaiah 55: "All you who thirst, come to the waters." 
* **Nun** is "progeny" or "sonship," Isaiah 14: "Son and nephew." 
* **Samech** is "placing upon" or "support," Deuteronomy chapter 34: "Because Moses laid," that is, placed, "his hands upon him." 
* **Ain** <note>Ayin</note> is an "eye," Exodus chapter 21: "An eye for an eye." 
* **Pe** is a "mouth," Exodus 4: "Who gave a mouth to man?" 
* **Tsade** is "sides," Exodus 25: "Six branches shall come out of its sides." 
* **Kuph** <note>Qoph</note> is "revolution" or "circuit," Exodus 34: "At the return of the year," that is, the circuit of the year. 
* **Res** <note>Resh</note> is "want" or "poverty," Proverbs 10: "The fear of the poor is their poverty"; though others interpret it as "inheritance." 
* **Sin** <note>Shin</note> is a "tooth," Job 4: "And the teeth of the young lions are broken." 
* **Thau** <note>Tav</note> is a "sign," Ezekiel 9: "Mark a *Thau*" <note>A sign or mark</note> "upon the foreheads of the men." 

This is the letters'

<column-break/>

<page-num>750</page-num>
<margin>A</margin> grammatical exposition, showing how they are accustomed to assign names to things, whether primary or derivative. I believe nothing here is foreign to higher contemplation, if one remains a student of figurative speech. 

Then Philolaus said, "It seems to me that we are destined to become elderly 'elementary' students <note>A pun on "elementarius," meaning both a student of the alphabet and one who studies the basic elements of the world.</note>, needing the schoolmaster's rod once again. For in the meantime, with much study, we have been reduced back to the alphabet." 

And Marranus added, "Indeed, we are becoming children again! This, Philolaus, is that famous Pythagorean <term>palingenesis</term> <note>original: "palingenesia," meaning rebirth or reincarnation.</note> of yours." 

To which Simon said, <margin>B</margin> "Do not reject these things; it is a truly great matter and worthy of philosophers (if you trust your Plato), and not at all ridiculous. As it seemed to Socrates in the *Cratylus*, to know the letters is essential, for he says we have nothing better than this by which to judge the truth of first names, <term>since the imitation of essence happens through syllables and letters, it is most correct to first distinguish the elements</term> <note>original Greek: "ἐπείπερ συλλαβαῖς τε καὶ γράμ-μασιν ἡ μίμησις τυγχάνει οὖσα τῆς οὐσίας, ὀρθότα-τόν ἐστι διελέσθαι τὰ στοιχεῖα πρῶτον"</note>. <margin>C</margin> Whence I think the 'elements' were named, as if they were <term>hylements</term> <note>A wordplay on the Greek "hyle" (matter) and "elements."</note>, that is, the material things from which the greatest things are made from the smallest; as in that saying of Hesiod:

> If you add a little to a little, and put it all 
> together, eventually a great heap will be made.

"Proceed, Simon," said Philolaus, "for you speak truly; with your permission, we were only joking with that remark." 

Then Simon said, "I shall move on to the numbers of the arithmetic discipline which are designated by the Hebrew letters. For there is no other language in the whole span of the earth <margin>D</margin> whose letters show any numbers so perfectly. The later Greeks did try to imitate the Jews so that they might similarly express numbers with their alphabet. But it was necessary for them to insert two figures, both for the number six and the number ninety, which are not literally part of the alphabetical order. For these two signs <insert>ϛ. ϟ.</insert> <note>The Greek "stigma" and "koppa," used as numerals rather than letters.</note> are inventions of newer men led by a desire to imitate, a fact for which we cite the Homeric books as witnesses. To be sure, the Romans explain only a few numbers through letters, a subject about which <margin>E</margin> you once read Priscian of Caesarea writing to Symmachus concerning numbers, weights, and measures. 

Let us therefore make four grades of numbers: the first is of single digits, the second of tens, the third of hundreds, and the fourth of thousands. 

The first grade is marked by the shapes of the alphabet from *Aleph* to *Teth*. There are nine signs, representing the nine numbers individually: **אבגדהוזחט**, that is: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. 

The second order, of tens, also contains nine shapes of the alphabet: <margin>F</margin> **יכלמנסעפצ**, that is: Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety. 

The third grade, of hundreds, similarly has nine characters: **קרשתםןץף** <note>These include the five final forms of letters: Mem, Nun, Tsade, Pe, and Caph, used here to reach the value of 900.</note>, that is: One hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, nine hundred. 

The fourth grade is of thousands, in which one must return to the shapes of the earlier numbers, although they ought to be larger in stature; thus it is called a <margin>G</margin> "Great Aleph," like a wide *Aleph*, and it is pronounced *patha* according to the Italian 'a'. So also a "Great Beth" signifies two thousand. This continues up to nine thousand. Finally, a "Great Iod" signifies ten thousand. In this order, they are also accustomed to mark the shapes with tips or points according to their stature."

<summary>Simon explains the Hebrew alphabet's fourfold significance: as acronyms for divine names, as symbolic representations of physical objects (like 'house' or 'eye'), and as a perfect numerical system (Gematria). He defends this study by citing Plato’s belief that letters imitate the essence of reality.</summary>

# KABBALAH

Next, they do not use figures, but words: *ribo ribonim* <note>original: רבו ריבונים</note>
<margin>A</margin> that is, "a thousand thousands," "twice a thousand thousands," and so forth. This path of the Alphabet of Numbers was greatly embraced by the Kabbalists, who say that two thousand years of "Beginning" preceded the creation of this world. This is because before *reshit* <note>original: ראשית</note>, that is, "the beginning," the Scripture places a large **Beth**, saying **B'reshit** <note>The first word of Genesis begins with a notably large letter Beth (ב) in Torah scrolls.</note>. In this way, our sages explain that passage in Proverbs 8: *The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from that time.* Indeed, whatever exceeds thousands
<margin>B</margin> is held to be in the place of the infinite. For the limit of numbers in the sacred texts is thousands; thus, when David wished to show the infinity of value in Psalm 119, he said: *The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver*, which is to say, "without number." Let us now very briefly review the third species of the substance of letters, which refers to certain intentions of our masters; for example, *aleph*, *beth*, and *hillis* signify prudence, and *gimel daleth* signify the "rewarding of the poor," and *mem*, that is *Me amar*, signifies "open speech" and "hidden speech," and so on for the others, which
<margin>C</margin> we shall recite a little further below, though they are more frequent in Talmudic usage. The fourth species of these letters consists of all things established and created; it is especially useful to students of Kabbalah, so that they may more easily lead creatures back to the Creator—which is indeed the greatest and singular pursuit of that discipline. I shall therefore place the letters each in its own order, so that you may know each element individually, and thus I begin: From **Aleph** unto
**Iod**, the orders or choirs of Angels are signified. These are what the Philosophers call "separate intelligences" and "noble forms," incorporeal and ungraspable, proceeding and derived from the power of God, who has no form, nor image, nor likeness. For He said in the fortieth chapter of Isaiah: *To whom have you likened me, that I should be equal?* And a little before: *To whom then have you made God like? Or what image will you set up for Him?* Furthermore,
<margin>E</margin> this dwelling place is named *Olam ha-Malakhim* <note>original: עולם המלאכים</note>, that is, the Age of Angels or the Angelic World. Then, from the letter **Caph** to the letter **Tzade**, the orders of the heavens are designated; these are endowed by the power of God the Creator and are governed by the influence of the Angels. This is called *Olam ha-Galgallim* <note>original: עולם הגלגלים</note>, that is, the Age of Orbs or Spheres. Furthermore, from **Tzade** to **Tau**, there intervene the four elements with their forms, and simultaneously all mixed things, both living and non-living, which depend on the power of God, from whom being and life flow into them. As it says in Isaiah: *Creating the heavens and stretching them out, establishing the earth and those things that sprout from it, giving
<margin>F</margin> breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who tread upon it, or walk in it.* These things are directed by the influences of the Angels and the spheres; and all of this is called *Olam ha-Yesodot* <note>original: עולם היסודות</note>, that is, the Age of Elements. Within it is Man, who is called *Olam ha-Katan* <note>original: עולם הקטן</note>, that is, the Small Age, which the Greeks call a <term>microcosm</term> <note>original: μικρόκοσμος</note>, meaning "Lesser World," or more correctly, "Small World." For in man himself shine back the properties of all creatures, both the highest and the lowest. We shall perhaps repeat these things more usefully in memory if we demonstrate of which things the individual letters are said to be symbols—a truly delightful matter, celebrated by the most ancient authors—lest there should ever be those who

<column-break/>

mock this art as if it were thin and meager.
It is, therefore:
**א Aleph**, the mark of the highest and most lofty things, which subsist from the first outflow of divine goodness: such as the Angels, who are called *Haioth ha-Kodesh* <note>original: חיות הקדש</note>, that is, "living creatures of the sanctuary," or rather, "lives without intermediary below God." These Angels, by the power of God, purify, illuminate, and perfect those immediately below them, which in common parlance is called their "influence."
**ב Beth**, the second letter, signifies the second rank of Angels from God himself, who are called *Ophanim* <note>original: אופנים</note>, that is, "forms" or "wheels." They are derived in the second place from the power of God through the prior intelligence, and they themselves also flow from God into those below. The sages also said that **Beth** is the mark of Wisdom.
**ג Gimel** represents, from the superior essences, the Angels who are called *Aralim* <note>original: אראלים</note>, that is, great, strong, and robust Angels. They descend
<margin>C</margin> in the third order from the goodness of the Divine Majesty; they are illuminated by the power of God through the medium of the second intelligence, and they likewise flow into those below.
**ד Daleth** is the symbol of the fourth emanation among the heavenly beings, those who are called *Hashmallim* <note>original: חשמלים</note>. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the third intelligence, and by that power they flow into those below.
**ה He**, the letter designates superior beings of the fifth emanation from God himself, which are the *Seraphim* <note>original: שרפים</note>. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the fourth intelligence, and by that same power they flow into those below.
<margin>D</margin> **ו Vau** marks the essence of the heavenly beings of the sixth emanation, who are called *Malakhim* <note>original: מלאכים</note>, that is, Angels <note>In this specific hierarchy, Malakhim refers to a specific rank, though the word generally means "messengers" or "angels" as a whole.</note>. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the fifth intelligence, and by that same power they flow into those below.
**ז Zain** is the seal of the blessed spirits of the seventh emanation, who are named *Elohim* <note>original: אלהים</note>, that is, "gods" or "divine beings." They are influenced by the power through the Angels of the sixth order, and by that same power they flow into those below.
**ח Heth** is the sign of the superior beings of the eighth emanation, and these are the Angels called *Bene Elohim* <note>original: בני אלהים</note>, that is, "sons of God." They are infused by the power of *El* <note>A Hebrew name for God signifying Might.</note> through the Angels of the seventh order, and they flow into those below by that same divine power.
**ט Teth** is the mark of the Angels of the ninth emanation, who are called *Cherubim* <note>original: כרובים</note>. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the intelligence of the eighth order, and by that same power they flow into those below.
**י Iod**, the tenth letter, signifies the essence of the intelligences of the tenth emanation. They are called *Ishim* <note>original: אישים</note>, the "noble" and "patrician" ones. They are lower than all other hierarchies and are illustrated by the power of God through the ninth choir. By that same power, they flow into the sons of men the cognition and science of things, and a wonderful industry. Hence, those endowed with such a faculty are called *Bene Ish*
<margin>G</margin> <note>original: בני איש</note>, that is, "men of noble intelligence," of whom Psalm 49 speaks: *Both those of the earth and the sons of men*; which is properly read thus: "Both the sons of the common people and the sons of the patricians," as if one were saying, "both the rustics and the nobles." From this [choir] of intelligences...

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical properties of the Hebrew alphabet.
