->### THIRD BOOK<-

754

...of graces, we ourselves receive them. For there is within us an **active intellect**, the highest part of the soul, which Aristotle calls <term>nous<note>original Greek: νουν</note></term>, meaning the mind. This alone comes to us from the outside. From it proceed prophetic visions and all things great and holy; it is also called the **Active Intellect** <note>original Hebrew: שכל הפועl (Sekhel Ha-Po’el)</note>, which marks the boundary of the Angelic world. Following this:

<margin>A</margin> **כ** (*Caph*): This letter designates the **Primum Mobile** <note>The "First Moved" sphere in classical astronomy, which gives motion to all others.</note> originating from God Himself <note>original: El Shaddai</note> as the immediate First Cause. It is moved through the spirit of rational life communicated by the Angel **Metattron**. He is called the active intellect of the sensible world, providing a path for forms to penetrate all lower things; thus, he flows by divine power into everything that is capable of motion. **ך** (*Caph* final) signifies the circuit of the **fixed stars**, which is called the eighth sphere in relation to us, but in relation to higher things, it is the second orb divided into the twelve signs of the zodiac, which we call the <term>Mazalot<note>original Hebrew: מזלות (constellations or destinies)</note></term>. It receives influence from the power of God through the mediation of the intelligence of *Caph* itself, and similarly flows into lower things.

<margin>B</margin> **ל** (*Lamed*): This is the sign of the first sphere of the planets. They are called <term>wanderers<note>original Hebrew: לבת (Labbat); Greek: πλανῆται (planētai)</note></term>, just as the Greeks call them "planets" because they appear to stray. It is said to be the seventh orb, attributed to **Saturn**, whom we call **Shabbatai**. It both receives and gives influence.

<margin>C</margin> **מ** (*Mem* open): This marks the sphere of **Jupiter**, whom we name **Tzedeq** <note>meaning "Justice"</note>. It receives influence from the power of God through the mediation of the higher intelligence and, by that same power, flows into lower things. **ם** (*Mem* closed/final) is the symbol of the sphere of **Mars**, which we call **Ma'adim** <note>meaning "The Red One"</note>, the fifth orb. It receives influence from God the Creator through the angel immediately above it and flows into lower things by that same power.

<margin>D</margin> **נ** (*Nun*): This signifies the "greater light," which is called **Shemesh**, that is, the **Sun**. Its sphere is called the orb of **Hamah** <note>a poetic Hebrew term for the sun's heat</note>. It receives influence from God through the sixth intelligence and also flows into lower things. **ן** (*Nun* final) indicates the sphere of **Venus**, which we call **Nogah** <note>meaning "Brightness"</note>. It exists by the power of God and flows through the mediation of the seventh intelligence.

<margin>E</margin> **ס** (*Samech*): This is the symbol of the "chancellor," who is called **Kokhav** <note>literally "Star"</note>, and in Latin, **Mercury**. It receives influence from the power of God from those above it and flows into lower things by that same power.

<margin>F</margin> **ע** (*Ayin*): This is the mark of the sphere of the **Moon**, which we call **Yareah**. It appears as the "left eye of the world." It is the last of the star-bearing orbs, and because of its whiteness, it is sometimes named **Levanah**. We entrust all these matters to the faculty of astrology.

<margin>G</margin> **פ** (*Pe*): This signifies the **intellectual soul**, both individual and universal. It is directed by the "separate intelligences" <note>Angelic beings that exist apart from physical matter</note> which are infused by God into the spheres, the stars, and all animate beings, both higher and lower, within the spheres and elements. **ף** (*Pe* final) denotes the **animal spirits** <note>The vital force that governs biological functions and movement</note>, which are directed by the higher intelligences by the power and command of God.

**צ** (*Tzade*): This symbolizes **matter**, both the intelligible matter of the heavens and the sensible matter of the elements, and of all mixed things. They are directed by divine power through the separate intelligences

<column-break/>

and through their own proper forms. **ץ** (*Tzade* final) shows the **forms of the elements**, which are Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. They are ruled by divine power through the Angels who are called **Ishim** <note>original: אישים; the "Man-like" angels, often associated with the governance of the sublunary world</note>, and by the power of the heavens and the power of "prime matter," which is the source and origin of all elements.

**ק** (*Koph*): This is the symbol of **inanimate things and minerals**, and those things called "elemental" or "mixed." They are directed by divine power through the celestial spheres and the separate intelligences called **Ishim**. They flow into the lower things in the region of the four elements.

**ר** (*Resh*): This signifies all **vegetation**, fruits, crops, and things born of the earth. They receive influence from the power of God through the celestial bodies and the separate intelligences named **Ishim**, as well as through the "complexions" <note>The specific balance of qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry)</note> of the elements.

**ש** (*Shin*): This designates all **sensitive creatures** <note>Beings with senses and movement but without human reason</note>, including the reptiles of the earth and walking animals, as well as the fish of the waters and the birds of the air, and whatever irrational things have vital motion. These are ruled by the power of God through the celestial bodies and the intelligences we call **Ishim**, and the complexions of the elements.

**ת** (*Tav*): This is the symbol of **Man** and human nature, which is the perfection and end of all creatures. He is directed by God through the complexions and qualities of the elements according to the influences of the heavens, and through the specific duties of the separate intelligences, the **Ishim**. These are of an Angelic condition; just as they are the end and consummation in the world of Angels, so is Man the end and perfection of creatures in the world of elements—or rather, in the world of all things. For he was constituted from two worlds, as it is written: <insert>The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.</insert>

***

These matters are treated more abundantly by our ancestors. To us, their descendants, their most ardent love for the created letters is clearly apparent, as they studied to give an account of even the smallest details. For example:

Concerning **Aleph**, it is written in the book <term>Bahir<note>original Hebrew: הבהיר (The Book of Brightness), an early and influential Kabbalistic text.</note></term>, where Rabbi Amorai sat and debated: "Why is *Aleph* placed at the head of the Alphabet?" The answer given is: "Because it existed before all things, even before the Law." Menachem Recanati mentions this regarding Rabbi Rahumai, the author of that book, in his first distinction on Genesis. Again: "Why does **Beth** follow immediately after?" Surely because it was the beginning of the Law <note>The first letter of the Torah is Beth (ב).</note>. And why was **Gimel** not named *Gidel*, since in the sacred letters the word *Gamal* <note>meaning "to ripen" or "to wean"</note> is placed first and followed in Genesis 21 by the phrase: *And the child grew and was weaned*? Wise men certainly did not disdain to scrutinize such things and their like. However, there are also some who, for the sake of brevity, passed over the explanations of certain things and wrote only what simply pertains to the matter, since they always strove with all diligence and study to hasten toward more sublime things—such as Rabbi Jacob Cohen in the book titled <term>The Exposition of the Holy Name<note>original Hebrew: פירוש השם הקדוש (Perush Ha-Shem Ha-Kadosh)</note></term>. For concerning the Alphabet, he speaks briefly in this manner:

These and other such things that remain, which you have heard from the records of the fathers, I have plucked as briefly as I could, so that I might offer you at least some taste of the literary profession. For the distinguished author Rabbi Akiba <note>A famous 1st-century sage and mystic</note> wrote about these things with great care, and many of our most learned men have followed his example, whom we deem worthy of much honor. For they have said that in the exposition of the Alphabet, many meanings lie hidden. And Rabbi Abraham Aben Ezra <note>A major 12th-century scholar and poet</note> says of this, in the book titled <term>סוד תורה</term> <note>Sod Torah</note>, that is, *The Mystery of the Law*: <term>ואמת, כי טוב הוא למשכיל שילמד מזאת החכמה</term>, which means: "And it is true, that it is good for the wise man that he should learn from this wisdom," because it is said that wisdom comes from them. Yet it is not so that we should labor in the literary art for the whole time of our life (as he himself says), or that we should be twisted day and night in the volumes of Rabbi Judah <note>Judah ben David Hayyuj, a pioneer of Hebrew grammar</note>, who is said to be the first Grammarian among the Hebrews; or in those twenty books which Marinus <note>The Hebrew grammarian Jonah ibn Janah</note> composed on literary instruction; or those twenty-two which Samuel Nagid <note>Samuel ha-Nagid, a statesman and scholar in 11th-century Spain</note> published on the same subject. Thus far speaks Rabbi Abraham Aben Ezra, nor did this most prudent man, so skilled in letters, think so in vain. For we are born for greater and higher things.

I have just spoken of the four considerations that pertain to the substance of the letter. Now, in my opinion, we must conclude that which we began some time ago regarding the accidental relation of letters, which is called <term>נוטריקון</term>, that is, *Notariacon* <note>A shorthand or acrostic method where letters represent whole words</note>, because we consider in part which letter signifies which word. It has, moreover, three types. For when it takes some sign from the beginning of a word, and (as is customary) is marked with points at the top, it is then called <term>ראש התיבה</term> <note>Rosh Ha-Tevah</note>, that is, the "head of the word," and it is usually written like this: <term>ל'ח</term>. Likewise, when it is taken from the term and end of some proposed word, it is then called <term>סוף התיבה</term> <note>Sof Ha-Tevah</note>, that is, the "end of the word"—

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> which they are accustomed to represent in this manner: <term>ס'ה</term>. But if individual marks are derived from the single letters of any word, we then call that by the general term *notariacon*. To these things Philolaus <note>A character in this dialogue</note> says: "O our Simon, how secret and hidden these things are to outsiders!" Then he replied: "I will show you perhaps much more hidden things in this third part of Kabbalah, which is named <term>תמורה</term> <note>Temurah</note>, meaning permutation, where there is a mutual positioning of letter for letter, and it happens as many times as the alphabets are permuted."

<margin>B</margin> They are permuted, moreover, twenty-two times according to the number of the letters, because we read that there are twenty-two letters of the Jews, and it will always be permitted to take one for another from any two paired letters; that combination is called <term>צירוף</term> <note>Tziruf</note>. For example, if from these six letters of the Latin Alphabet—a, b, c, d, e, f—I were to continually join them two by two, so that under the first yoke are **a b**, under the second **c d**, and under the third **e f**, and I wished through a letter to urge someone skilled in this art to fall before the feet of the prince to make a plea, I would write: **db ef**. He will understand this as **Cade** <note>Latin for "fall"</note>, and so it is with others.

<margin>C</margin> This whole workmanship arises from the revolution of the alphabet, so that letter succeeds letter by turn, combined in its own proper yoke—namely, **a** for **b**, and **b** for **a**, similarly **c** for **d**, and **d** for **c**, and likewise **e** for **f**, and **f** for **e**. This proceeds even more easily in Hebrew, with nothing standing in the way, because the sounds which the Latins call "vowels" are not placed in the order of the Jewish Alphabet. Therefore, in an ancient age, our father Abraham, moved by this,

<margin>D</margin> said (as is read in the second chapter of the book *Ietzira* <note>Sefer Yetzirah, the Book of Creation</note>): "*Aleph* with all and all with *Aleph*, no differently than *Beth* with all and all with *Beth*," and so with each one. Therefore, so that it may be made clearer by an example, I will bring forward into the midst twenty-two alphabets, which Abraham arranged quite skillfully and usefully in that same volume of creation.

# XXII. The Alphabets of Rabbi Abraham

<margin>A</margin> This mingling of the twenty-two elements <note>The Hebrew alphabet consists of 22 letters, here seen as the fundamental building blocks of the universe.</note> is by no means to be understood as something rustic or unlearned; for all things are <term>spiritus</term> <note>original: "spiritus"; refers to both "breath" and "spirit," suggesting the letters are living spiritual forces.</note>. Thus it is written in the book <term>Ietzira</term> <note>original: "Ietzira"; the *Sefer Yetzirah* or Book of Formation, an early and influential Kabbalistic text.</note>: "And God carved with that spirit twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples; and each of them is spirit." Therefore, these things have been handed down to us for spiritual contemplation with great joy—not for speaking against or mocking, but for embracing the mysteries of the Scriptures with pious faith. For by believing in the letters, we more easily contemplate higher things, and we trust that hidden truths can be found within the letters, just like the word of God in the midst of the darkness, who said to Moses: "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you." Indeed, through the number 22 <note>original Hebrew: כב (*Kaf-Bet*), which equals 22.</note>, they shall believe forever. For it is necessary for a Kabbalist to believe not like an old woman, but with strength, and to receive the commands of the fathers committed to letters with singular love and a joyful, glad mind—with joy and confidence, as in *Psalm* 70: "Let them exult and be glad in the 22 <note>original Hebrew: כב (*Kaf-Bet*). The author interprets the Psalm's reference to joy as being tied to the 22 letters of the alphabet.</note> who seek you." For you must know that the twenty-two letters are the foundations of the world and the Law, as is treated at length in the second book of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>original: "Horti nucis"; referring to *Ginnat Egoz* by Joseph Gikatilla, a classic of Kabbalistic linguistic theory.</note>, which you have either read or will read.

Then Philolaus said: "Certainly, I have never read nor seen such books, though I have spent no small effort up to this point searching for where they might be hidden."

And Marranus said: "I do not know why the Jews are so stingy with books of that kind, that they do not even freely give them to a friend, nor sell them for any amount of money."

Then Simon said: "It is decreed among us that the secrets of the Law are not to be given to strangers, but to a <note>original Hebrew: ליועץ חכם (*le-yoetz chakham*)</note> wise counselor—not even just to a household counselor, nor just to a wise man, but to one who is both a wise counselor, who is not an outsider, and who is not unlearned. I pray you, do not take this poorly. For often, because of the imminent danger during our long-standing dispersion, a council 

<column-break/>

of the fathers carefully and providently decreed <note>original Hebrew: ברח שהוא בורח וממה שנפל בו באחרונה (*Berach she-hu boreach...*)</note> by that law, that he should flee from that into which he fell later; according to our authority Moses the Egyptian <note>original: "Moyse nostro Aegyptio"; referring to the famous philosopher Maimonides.</note>, who enumerates the causes and recounts the outcomes in chapter 71 of the book *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "Perplexorum"; *The Guide for the Perplexed* (*Moreh Nevukhim*).</note>. But I hope you will take these and other things of our people in good part; therefore, setting aside that dispute, I will follow the third part of the Kabbalistic art."

"You have heard about the two hundred and forty-two combinations of letters, and the two hundred 

<margin>B</margin> and thirty-one permutations of pairings, besides the commonly used alphabet, whose letters they are also accustomed to connect in their own order, two by two, for mutual exchange. This matter is commonly seen as meager, and perhaps at first glance held in contempt by the unskilled, but it is something that should be greatly exalted among men. As is read in *Psalm* 12: <note>original Hebrew: כרם זלת לבני אדם (*Kerem zullut livnei adam*)</note> 'The things despised are exalted by the sons of men.' To which Rabbi Solomon <note>Referring to Rashi, the preeminent medieval commentator.</note> cites there what is said by the Psalmist: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the 

<margin>C</margin> head of the corner.' I pray you, consider it not negligently, for it is not written in vain: <note>original Hebrew: ברם גמטריא (*Beram Gematria*)</note> for the <term>Gematria</term> <note>original: "Ghematria"; a Kabbalistic system where words are interpreted by the numerical value of their letters.</note> of the word *Beram* <note>The Hebrew word for "but" or "truly."</note> signifies two hundred and forty-two; for that is the total of all the combinations described above. Venerate those two hundred and thirty-one variations with fitting honor. For all things that exist and all things that are spoken arise from them. Regarding those gates which they call such, our father Abraham (as it is in the book <term>Ietzira</term>) said: <note>original Hebrew: ונמצא כל הדבור וכל היצור יוצא מהן (*Ve-nimtza kol ha-dibbur ve-kol ha-yitzur yotze me-hen*)</note> 'And every word and every creature exists proceeding from them.' 

<margin>D</margin> Indeed, with their help, we can easily arrange these things for our salvation, since we are to be led back, through the consideration of all created things, into the knowledge of the one Creator—as far as human strength allows—which is our salvation and eternal life. This is done by God through His name, returning again into God. He is Himself."

It justifies the secrecy surrounding these Kabbalistic texts and introduces the numerical significance of letter combinations (Gematria) as a path to divine knowledge.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Alphabets of Rabbi Abraham," transitioning from the technical tables of letter permutations into a philosophical and narrative explanation of the Divine Names, specifically the 42-letter name of God and its legendary connection to the prophet Jeremiah and the creation of a golem.</meta>

<page-num>759</page-num>
<header>KABBALAH</header>

<margin>A</margin> His four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>, blessed forever and ever, which the Psalmist revealed when he said: "And they shall know that you alone, whose name is the Lord <note>original: Tetragrammaton</note>, are the Most High over all the earth." For this reason, this name alone is called *Shem HaMephorash* <gloss>שם המפורש, meaning the "Explicit Name"</gloss>, which is the name that explains the very essence of God. The proof of this is found in the first part of this mystical art. There is another name of God that takes the place of this one, written with twelve letters, the logic of which is found in the second part. Furthermore, there is another name which is most conveniently handled here in this third part of the Kabbalah: the name of forty-two characters. This does not mean that a single pronunciation of a name consists of forty-two letters. For it is known to any person of understanding (as Rabbi Moses Maimonides <note>A famous 12th-century Jewish philosopher</note> teaches) that a single name written with so many letters cannot be found anywhere. Rather, it is many names combined among and within themselves, gathered from many letters. These lead the Kabbalist through certain hidden reasons to the truth of the knowledge of the four-letter name of God, Y-H-W-H <gloss>יוד .ה. ו. ה.</gloss>, which similarly signifies forty-two through arithmetic <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of the spelled-out letters of the Tetragrammaton can be calculated to equal 42</note>. Characters of this kind, forty-two in number, joined through such names, are called "one name" because in the end they signify only one thing, just as, conversely, other composite and collective names are often many but signify a single thing. It could therefore happen in the present case that the logic by which our intellect is led to God could only be explained by many letters and words. This is not surprising, for skilled craftsmen are accustomed to track a spring through many and diverse streams. Thus, from the abyss of His own fountain, God caused all things to flow out and to flow back into that infinite whirlpool.

<margin>E</margin> "To bring forth a thing in a word, and a word in a thing... to establish all things in the spring of the flame, and the flame in the word, like a spring that has no searching out and no number for the light that hides itself in the increase of the darkness, which is concealed generally in forty-two letters." <note>This is a translation of the Hebrew text provided in the margin</note> These are the words of the most contemplative teacher, Hamai, in the book *Ha-Iyun* <gloss>העיון, the Book of Speculation</gloss>, to which he usefully cites the *Sefer Ma’ayon Ha-Chokhmah* <gloss>ספר מעון החכמה, the Book of the Fountain of Wisdom</gloss>, though a man of such integrity would not have needed a witness. Now I will try to see if I can translate these things into English <note>original: Latin</note>, at least so that the meaning suffers no loss: "To produce," he says, "the thing in the word and the word in the thing, until he restores all things into the fountain of radiance, and the radiance into the word, like a fountain which has neither limit nor number, toward the inaccessible light hidden by the increase of darkness in the universe of forty-two letters." Thus far Hamai. Moreover, the most excellent of the sages (whose memory is a blessing) call this name, so worthy of veneration and worship,

<margin>F</margin> designated by forty-two letters, "Holy and Sanctified" <gloss>קדוש ומקודש, Kadosh u-Mekudash</gloss>. Therefore, it was hidden from the unrefined and the unworthy through the mixing of alphabetical revolutions. It was revealed through an alphabetical combination to Jeremiah, who led a life of holy contemplation and who used to read often in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <gloss>Book of Formation</gloss>, as it is found written

<margin>G</margin> in the *Sefer Bitachon* <gloss>ספר בטחון, the Book of Trust</gloss>, the author of which is Rabbi Judah, who composed it. When Jeremiah

<column-break/>

<page-num>760</page-num>
<header>KABBALAH</header>

turned the pages of the *Book of Formation* much and often by hand, both day and night, it is said that a *Bat Kol* <gloss>בת קול, literally "daughter of a voice," meaning a heavenly echo or divine voice</gloss> came to him, commanding him to labor over that same volume for three years. After the end of three years, when the joining and handling of the characters finally pleased him so that he might work with them, a "new man" <note>A golem</note> was soon created for him and his companions. On the man’s forehead was written: "The Lord God is Truth" <gloss>יהוה אלהים אמת, YHWH Elohim Emeth</gloss>. Then that newly created man, feeling the writing on his forehead,

<margin>B</margin> did not delay further, but with a swift hand he suddenly moved and removed the first letter in "Truth" <note>Emeth</note>, which is *Aleph*. Thus, what remained were these words: "The Lord God is Dead" <gloss>יהוה אלהים מת, YHWH Elohim Meth</gloss>. ### BOOK THREE

<margin>A</margin>
Indeed, in this verse, while I count out each of the letters, immediately another part of the single word arises from any one of the seven disyllables. Each single word of this so precious name is known to consist of six characters, yet only in Hebrew, not in another language: for in Latin more characters would be needed, such as *Sagathbama*, *Sagaththecaz*, *Miathazab*, *Iemibatha*, *Zethaghabhaz*, *Thegazama*, *Zaazpapas*. These are found in the volumes of the ancients even to this day, foreign and unknown to the Roman speech <note>original: "Romano sermoni," referring to Latin</note>, but they should not be despised for being harsh and barbaric. For no one should use such bleary eyes in the sight of sacred things as to despise what is hidden. No one should indulge their ears with such delights in hearing divine things that they only venerate, praise, and follow those things which are pleasant to the senses, beautiful to the eyes, soft to the touch, and charming in sound; instead, let one grasp spiritual things more than physical ones, constant things more than fleeting ones, and true things more than those that are merely painted over.

Indeed, rough and terrifying things often precede the presence of God. Remember what happened to the Prophet Elijah when he lay hidden in the caves and the cavern on Horeb, the mountain of God. Was it not said to him thus? "Behold, the Four-Letter Name <note>original: "Tetragrammatus," referring to the name YHWH</note> passes by, and a great and strong wind, overturning mountains and breaking and crushing rocks before the Four-Letter Name; but the Four-Letter Name was not in the wind. After the wind, an earthquake; and the Four-Letter Name was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake, a fire; but the Four-Letter Name was not in the fire. After the fire, a still, small voice <note>original: "vox submissa tenuis"</note>, and in that voice the glory of the Four-Letter Name spoke to him," which is named <term>קוֹל, "Kol," meaning "voice"</term>. 

So you too, after the terrifying and thorny desert, after the mountain and the rocks, after the wind and the earthquake, after the fire, after the voice in the very entrance of the caves and caverns—once the multitude of secular preoccupations has been dismissed—you will hear the glory of God speaking to you. What are you doing here? Proceed further, as it is explained in <margin>1 Kings 19 <note>The text cites "3. Regum 19," following the older Vulgate numbering of the books of Kings</note></margin>. Therefore, we must not stand still here, but return with the Prophet Elijah to our path through the desert—that is, through these bristling revolutions of barbaric connections and tangled briars into the path of the sacred and canonical scripture, our truly own path which is the truth of the utterances of God, so that we may anoint the king in Syria who is called Messiah <note>original: "Messiha," the Anointed One</note> from his anointing. For we shall walk through the combinations <note>original: "conjugationes," referring to the permutations of letters</note> of the twenty-two alphabets for just as long as it takes to reach the supreme and first alphabet with vigilant concern and untiring diligence.

For it is necessary for us to run skillfully through each individual combination for as long as it takes for the voice of God to be revealed, and for the text of the most sacred scriptures to offer itself openly to us. Truly, that voice of God rains down its power and value abundantly upon all the alphabets from the first to the last—namely, the twenty-second—so that combinations which are considered non-significant might provide a somewhat greater efficacy than names with a primary meaning, just as a ray of the sun burns more strongly than the sun itself from which it flowed. ### CABALA

...his four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>, blessed forever and ever, which the Psalmist showed when he said: *And they shall know that your name is the Tetragrammaton, you alone are the Most High over all the earth.* For this reason, this name alone is called the **Shem HaMephorash**, that is, the name that explains the essence of God. The proof of this is taken from the first part of this art. There is another name of God succeeding in this one's place, which is written with twelve letters, the logic of which will be received in the second part. Furthermore, there is another name which is most conveniently treated in this third part of the Cabala: the name of forty-two characters. This does not mean that a single pronunciation of one name consists of forty-two letters. For it is known to any intelligent person (as <term>Rabbi Moses Maimonides</term><note>Maimonides (1138–1204), a preeminent Sephardic Jewish philosopher and scholar.</note> teaches) that a single name written with so many letters cannot be found anywhere. Rather, there are several names folded into one another and within themselves, gathered from many letters, which lead the Kabbalist through certain hidden reasons to the true knowledge of the four-letter God—*Yod, He, Vav, He* (יהוה . י . ה . ו . ה)—which likewise signifies forty-two in arithmetic <note>The author refers to a specific Kabbalistic method of expansion or gematria where the letters of YHWH are calculated to reach the number 42.</note>. These forty-two characters, joined through such names, are called "one name" because ultimately they signify only one thing, just as, conversely, other composite and collective names are often many things signifying a single unity. It could therefore happen in the present circumstances that the logic by which our intellect is led into God could only be explained by many letters and words. This is no wonder, since skilled craftsmen are accustomed to track a spring through many diverse rivulets. Thus, from the abyss of His own fountain, God caused all things to emanate and to flow back into an infinite vortex.

Thus far Hamai. The most excellent of the wise (whose memory is a blessing) call this name—so venerable and solemn, designated by forty-two letters—**Kadosh u-Mekuddash** (that is, Holy and Sanctified). <page-num>763</page-num>

...of the letters **AB, BEN, VE-RUACH HA-KODESH** <note>original Hebrew: אב בן ורוח הקדש</note>, that is, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. From this is derived the name of forty-two letters, which is pronounced thus: **AB ELOHIM, BEN ELOHIM, RUACH HA-KODESH ELOHIM, SHELOSHA BE-ECHAD, ECHAD BE-SHELOSHA** <note>original Hebrew: אב אלהים בן אלהים רוח הקדש אלהים שלשה באחד אחד בשלשה</note>; that is, Father God, Son God, Holy Spirit God, three in one and one in three. O, how great is this height! How great a depth, which is grasped by faith alone! Then **Philolaus** said: "Simon, what great thanks we must give to you, who shows us all these things so lucidly and clearly—if indeed anything in this art can be clear, and not rather the greatest part of these things hidden in wrappings, appearing to flee like shadows. And **Marranus** said: "Be silent, I pray, Philolaus! Let him proceed. Do you not see? Evening approaches, and he has almost completed his daily task. Speak on then, Simon, whatever remains."

Then Simon said: "I have completed the whole art and taught it, unless there are certain particulars you think remain concerning certain names of God, and of Angels, and of virtues, and consecrated seals, by whose force and power many have promised they would do many things which seem wonderful to the common people." And **Marranus** said: "Perhaps you have forgotten that you were also going to speak of the name of twelve letters, although you affirmed it was the subject of the second part, which has already passed." Then **Simon** replied: "There is little I need to explain about that, except that after the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> began to be devalued everywhere due to the frequent and common use by wicked men—having previously been handled with such care and anxiety, with such reverence and such prudent moderation, handed down only to suitable and chosen priests every seventh year so they might learn to bless the people through it in the sanctuary—at that time, to preserve the majesty of this name, the priests were forbidden to use it in common prayer. Its pronunciation was permitted only to the High Priests once a year on the days of fasting and atonement. Therefore, in its place, they substituted the name of twelve letters for others, which would be somewhat more sacred than the name **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>, and yet far less divine than the ineffable **Tetragrammaton**, for the priests to use in blessings. It was customary to write it with these four letters **H-K-B-H** <note>original Hebrew: הקבה</note> with marks at the top of each, signed by **Notarikon** <note>A Kabbalistic method of using initials to form words or phrases.</note>, and so pronounced as **HA-KADOSH BARUCH HU** <note>original Hebrew: הקדוש ברוך הוא</note>, that is, 'The Holy One, Blessed be He.' Through this, they later offered the blessing commanded by God in the sixth chapter of Numbers over the people, in place of the **Tetragrammaton**, like so: <margin>Numbers 6</margin> '*May the Holy One, Blessed be He, bless you and keep you. May the Holy One, Blessed be He, show His face to you and have mercy on you. May the Holy One, Blessed be He, lift up His face to you and give you peace.*' In this place, **Solomon Trecentis** <note>Referring to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki); "Trecentis" or "of the three hundred" is a Latin pun on the city of Troyes.</note>, the ordinary commentator on the Sacred Scripture, writes: 'Therefore the priests spread their palms because the Holy One, Blessed be He, stands behind us, as it is written: Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the fingers of the priests.' <note>A reference to Song of Solomon 2:9, interpreted as God's presence manifesting during the Priestly Blessing.</note> So I hold it written on the parchment of an ancient codex, although certain printed paper volumes

# KABBALAH

<margin>A</margin> lack these words. Our people most firmly believe, and in no way doubt, that a blessing expressed in this form is the cause of as much prosperity as it would have been if the name **Tetragrammaton** (which they now pronounce as **Adonai**) had remained in those prayers. For this change was made to honor the **Tetragrammaton**, lest it eventually fall into neglect by being repeated so often—which may God, the Best and Greatest, turn away from us above all things. <margin>B</margin> Now you have the entire Kabbalistic garden, that is, the **GINNAH** <note>original Hebrew: גנה; G-N-H, often used as a mnemonic for Gematria, Notarikon, and Hitemurah.</note>, divided into three flowerbeds, which are **Gematria, Notarikon, and Temurah**, growing with infinite roots, herbs, and flowers, with all its ornament looking toward one Gardener who waters, plants, and gives the increase: God, the Best, Greatest, incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnameable, to whom also belongs the incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnameable name, the **Tetragrammaton**, from which flows and derives everything that is made. <margin>C</margin> For the rest, if any are found, the symbols, notes, sacraments, and signs of divine things certainly take their origin from this very source. For example, **YODO** <note>original Hebrew: יודו</note> signifies **YHVH ECHAD** <note>The Lord is One</note>, working arithmetically through the first part of this art, **Gematria**, as was explained above; yet that same name **YODO** symbolically represents the entire name **Tetragrammaton** itself through the second part of Kabbalah, as **Joseph Bar Abraham** <note>Joseph Gikatilla, a 13th-century Kabbalist.</note>, a citizen of the district of Salem, writes in the second volume of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>Ginat Egoz</note>, in these words: <margin>D</margin> 'Y' its permutation is 'K', 'H' its permutation is 'V', and 'V' its permutation is 'Z' <note>This refers to the Atbash or similar cipher systems where letters are swapped.</note>. By this, we observe that God is one in His essence, most singular, than whom nothing is more one; although many things are said of Him according to other relations, because of which He is called **Elohim Kadoshim**, that is, 'Holy Gods' (in the last chapter of Joshua), and **Elohim Hayyim**, that is, 'Living Gods' (in Deuteronomy 5). And in Malachi 1, He speaks of Himself thus: <margin>E</margin> 'And if I am Masters, where is my fear?' <note>original Hebrew: ואם אדונים אני איה מוראי</note>. In this place, God calls Himself 'Masters' in the plural. Therefore, according to His immanence, He is one; but according to His outgoings, He is many, He who said, 'Let us make man in our image and likeness.' It was not merely the custom of the Holy Language that those established in the highest majesty should speak of themselves in the plural, as **Rab Saadia** writes in the book *Emunot* <note>The Book of Beliefs and Opinions by Saadia Gaon.</note>, that is, of 'beliefs.' <margin>F</margin> For this is a weak argument, since immediately afterward He speaks in the singular, 'I will make him a helper like unto himself.' The Kabbalists do not unwillingly admit this unity and this plurality in divine things for various reasons, whence they assert that the first three Kabbalistic numerations <note>The Sephirot: Keter (Crown), Chokmah (Wisdom), and Binah (Understanding).</note> **KETER, CHOKMAH, BINAH** are the one crown of the supreme King, as **Rab Affe** <note>Likely referring to a Kabbalistic source or a corruption of a name like Rabbi Akiva or Isaac the Blind.</note> writes in the book *Yechid* <note>The Book of the Unique.</note>, on singular unions or collections. You see by this example that we use all parts of Kabbalah back and forth indiscriminately: namely, the universal transposition of letters, syllables, and words; <margin>G</margin> then numerical calculation, capital notation, and literal permutation with each species, which I revealed in the previous discourse. So we transpose the name **Tetragrammaton**, so that it might be **Va** and **Ya**...

# BOOK THREE

<page-num>765</page-num>

...and let the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: יהוה (YHWH)</note> arise, which is to say, the Essence, which is the sum of all things, from which all true and good beings come. Whence **I Shall Be Lord** <note>original: Ehieh Adonai (אהיה אדני)</note> signifies arithmetically the same amount as **God** <note>original: Elohim (אלהים)</note>, the sum of which is eighty-six. Just as the **Tetragrammaton** is a sign of **God** himself, if it is expanded in this way: **Yod He Waw He** <note>original: יוד הא ואו הא - this is the "spelling out" of the letters of the Name</note>, this makes 12 <note>the number of letters in the expanded spelling</note> which is 86 <note>the numerical value</note>. And the **Tetragrammaton** is the four-letter name because it equals 26; but if it is expanded to 72, it makes 112, and it designates **The Lord God** <note>original: Tetragrammaton Elohim</note>. Concerning this, it is first written: *These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens.* <margin>A</margin> Furthermore, the beginning of the four-letter name is **Iah**, and the middle of **God** <note>Elohim</note> is **Iah**, and the end of **I Shall Be** <note>Ehieh</note> is **Iah**. All of this is the perfection of the **Tetragrammaton** itself, that is, the Essence, which signifies **He** <note>original: הוא (Hu)</note> and the divine **To Be** <note>original: יה (Ya)</note>. <margin>B</margin> Whence it is a common daily usage to say something is "divine" if it is necessary and incorruptible. Indeed, everything that exists, when it exists, must necessarily exist for this reason, nor can it then happen not to exist.

Therefore, the power of that Essence was led into operation through the Word of God, who said, **Let there be** <note>original: יהי (Yehi)</note>, by which word all things were created in one supreme Idea, as well as the most absolute intellectual virtues, through this: that He himself commanded thus, *Let there be light, and suddenly there was light.* <margin>C</margin> This universality was followed by the nature of the Angels assigned to ministries, when He said, **And it was so** <note>original: ויהי כן (Wayehi khen)</note>. This designates the prince and great priest who is named **Michael**, a shining proof of the angelic condition, which is constituted from unity and the number one hundred. <margin>D</margin> Whence they believe that on the first day, the Ideas were produced outside the First Cause, as most absolute forms in terms of being and operation. But on the second day, the Angels were created from this. For on the first day He did not say, **And it was so**, but on the second day, when the firmament of heaven was made. According to **Rabbi Eliezer**, they were created from the light of His garment. For God was clothed in ten garments when He created the world, as the Kabbalists say, and from the light of His last garment He took and created the heavens—not indeed the sensible ones, but those invisible and intellectual **Spiritualities** <note>original: רוחניות (Ruchaniyot)</note>, of which the Psalmist says: *The heavens declare the glory of God.* There it is not written **Heavens** <note>original: שמים (Shamayim)</note>, which are circular, as **Rabbi Ama** memorably noted in the *Book of Secrets* regarding Psalm 19, but **The Heavens** <note>original: השמים (Ha-Shamayim)</note>, to which the article *ha* is added. As it is read in the summary argument of Genesis: *In the beginning God created The Heavens* <note>original: Hasamaim</note>, that is, those distinguished heavens, those famous ones, those admirable ones, never seen nor to be seen by mortal eyes. <margin>E</margin> For other heavens, which are not written with the article *ha*, are indeed the firmament, but they are still called by the name of heaven; wherefore it is written: *And God called the firmament Heavens.* And it is called the firmament of that same invisible heaven—I mean, that which is called the **Heavens of heavens**. Whence it follows: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven.* <margin>F</margin> Surely that extension in the manner of a skin, inscribed with lights and stars as if with letters, is called **Firmament** <note>original: rakia (רקיע)</note> because of its local expansion, which we call "firmament" from its firmness. <margin>G</margin> For the invisible heaven did not need lights, since it is spiritually illustrious through itself and is mentally illuminated by the First

<column-break/>

<page-num>766</page-num>
<header>BOOK THREE</header>

Cause. Therefore they are named the "Separate Intelligences," of which the author of *The Book of Causes* says: *Every intelligence is full of forms*, which, while it understands, is said to hear and speak. Wherefore Moses says: *Hear, O heavens, the things I shall speak.* And David: *The heavens declare the glory of God.* And God says in Hosea: *I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.* Whence the prophetic light descends, which is called an **Illuminating Vision** <note>original: Aspaklaria Ha-Meirah (אספקלריא המאירה)</note>, which belonged to Moses. For the vision of other prophets was a **Non-Illuminating Vision** <note>original: Aspaklaria she-einah meirah (אספקלריא שאינה מאירה)</note>, and that is called "earth." Some mention of these things was made in the first discourse. <margin>B</margin> Indeed, I seem to myself rightly to believe that for this reason our sages said: *The appearance of Moses was like the appearance of the sun, and the appearance of Joshua like the appearance of the moon.*

Therefore, in the creation of sensible things, God uses this symbol of intelligible things, **Let it be so** <note>original: יהי כן (Yehi khen)</note>, so that the ministry of Angels might be designated as co-created with natural things under the common name of **Michael**, as a name for the angelic species. Through that prayer, **And it was so**, recited in the following works of the five days according to the first part of the Kabbalistic art, it is symbolically signified by an equality of number. By this it is established that all Angels are of the same species. Furthermore, individual bodies, whether celestial or terrestrial, have their own rulers of virtues and prefects of operations—both those that are rational, such as the heavens, stars, and men, and those that are irrational, such as beasts and elements. <margin>D</margin> To the philosophers, especially the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle</note>, it is proved that every spherical heaven, besides its essential form, has an assistant intelligence as the mover of its orb, which is called an "Angel." Because it is sent to this office, understanding and willing, it fulfills the commands of the Creator as a middle power between God and nature, from which operations are performed in things—operations which their nature either would not do, or would not do in that way. Others say these things come from a "hidden property," and others because "it is such." <margin>E</margin> For the motion of the heavens and stars, although naturally circular, is yet moved from East to West, or vice versa; this is not of nature, but of will. But an Angel has free will, while nature is restricted only to a certain instinct, whence it always acts in the same way. Angels, however, do not always move the orbs in the same way. Thus it happens that changes in these lower things do not always occur in the same way. For the angelic condition exercises the greatest force and power over corporeal things.

Therefore, the "Active Intellect," from which forms flow, is named an Angel, as **Rabbi Moses Maimonides** testifies, and is called the **Prince of the World** <note>original: Saro shel Olam (שרו של עולם)</note>, as our sages have said. He is called **Metatron**, by whom indeed all individual human, animal, and natural virtues are governed, which are likewise called Angels. Their multitude is somewhat infinite, but certain, terminated, and finite as far as the Creator is concerned. <margin>G</margin> *Genesis Rabbah* mentions this matter, where it is read that the Creator daily creates a company of Angels, whom others call "forms," because they are formal substances with which the entire sphere of things that can be generated and corrupted is full beyond number. Not otherwise did your own **Hesiod** accept this, for in *Works and Days* he says thus:

<meta>This page continues the discussion of divine hierarchies and the structure of the spiritual world. Having established the numerical relationships of the Names of God on the previous page, the author now transitions into the "Cabala" (Kabbalah) of spirits and angels, drawing parallels between classical Greek poetry and Hebrew mystical traditions to explain how the atmosphere and the human soul are populated by unseen forces.</meta>

# CABALA

> For thrice ten thousand are the immortals of Zeus upon the bountiful earth, 
> guardians of mortal men, 
> who indeed watch over justice and cruel deeds, 
> clothed in mist, roaming everywhere over the earth.
> <note>original: Greek quote from Hesiod’s *Works and Days*, lines 252–255</note>

That is to say: For there are three times ten thousand immortals of Jove <note>Jupiter/Zeus</note> upon the earth that feeds many, guardians of mortal men, who certainly observe both justice and wretched deeds; clothed in air, they go everywhere over the earth. Like these, within man, they <note>the Kabbalists</note> name two powers of the will as two Angels: the **Good Inclination** <note>original: יצר טוב (Yetzer Tov)</note>, that is, the author of good, and the author of evil, as is read in the **Midrash Tanhuma** <note>original: מדרש תנחומא, a collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah</note>, which Rabbi Assi cites in his collection. The Latins call these Hesiodic beings who assist the body "spirits"; whichever of them is assigned to the care of lower business is called **Mammona** or **Mammon**, which in Greek they call a **daemon**, though not always in a bad sense. 

Indeed, a "daemon" is one thing, and a "demonium" <note>a lesser spirit or "demon"</note> is another, which we consider to be a diminishing of divinity, and therefore it is excluded from divine things in a diminutive sense. However, I plainly admit that Homer and the oldest writers had a different use for that word; many of them preach laudable and venerable things about the **daemon of Socrates**, which Apuleius interpreted as the "God of Socrates." 

Furthermore, what the Latins called "Spirits" in the likeness of winds took its origin from us, who call them **Winds** <note>original: רוחות (Ruchot), which means both "winds" and "spirits"</note>. Concerning these, Rabbi Todros Halevi <note>original: Tedacus Leui</note>, in his book *On the Ten Numerations*, after explaining the four winds—North, South, East, and West—finally writes: **And for those four winds He created four angels, who are appointed over them by day and by night.** <note>original: ואלו ארבע רוחות ברא ארבע מלאכים דמונין עליהין ביומה ובלילה</note> Then it follows from the same author that **Michael**, who is of the side of clemency and mercies, is established as the **Mammona** (that is, the prefect) over the East wind until midday and until night. And **Raphael**, who is likewise of the side of clemency, rules the West wind. Then **Gabriel**, in the power of judgment and severity, is prefect with the North wind over the half of the night and two measures of the world. **Nuriel** truly presides over the South. So far Todros Halevi. 

Furthermore, those angels have many species under them, which the **Secrets** <note>original: סודות (Sodot)</note> contain; and in the **Gate of Light** <note>original: *Porta Lucis* or *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla</note> it is read thus:

> For from the earth even unto the firmament there is no empty space, 
> but all is full of hosts: some of them pure, some masters 
> of grace and mercy; and there are below many foul creatures, 
> harmful and accusing; and they all stand and fly in the air, 
> and there is no empty space from the earth to the firmament, but all 
> are hosts: some for peace, some for war, some for good, 
> some for evil, some for life, some for death. And all this is in the 
> lower dwelling in which we are.

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> These are the words of Joseph of Castile <note>Joseph Gikatilla</note>. But far be it from our holy purpose to continue disputing much concerning those squalid and most foul demons, the enemies of the human race, who are called "opposing strengths"—whether those who are thought to wander the upper region (fiery ones), or those who wander the air near us, or the earthly ones who terrify the land, or those who inhabit lakes and rivers and often shake the sea itself, or those under the earth who sometimes attack those who dig wells and mines, likewise provoking gaps in the earth, stirring up flame-vomiting winds, and shaking foundations; and finally, those who flee all light and splendor, inscrutable and deeply dark, who vex not only the human race but even the brutes, instilling their talk without sound. 

<margin>B</margin> Against their machinations there are some of our people who think themselves experienced in many things, and they do not hesitate to attract good spirits by soothing them, and to repel evil ones by opposing passions, being duly supported by sacred and divine names and characters. 

<margin>C</margin> They command a man exposing himself to future dangers to take a very thin parchment, which is called "virgin" <note>vellum made from the skin of a stillborn animal</note>, as being sincere, clean, and immaculate, to presage the purity of the actor; then to inscribe these characters: **TZMRKD** <note>original: צמרכד, a cipher made of the final letters of the first five verses of Genesis</note>. But on the outside, on the rougher part of the leaf, they also sign these marks: **KWZW** <note>original: כוזו, a cipher for YHWH used on the back of Mezuzahs</note>. By this binding, they instruct the one hoping most firmly in God the Creator of the universe to dread no machinations of perverse men. 

<margin>D</margin> They reveal the mystery in this way: these are symbols of the first five verses of Genesis, both the beginnings and the ends, according to the second part of the Cabalistic art. Costa Ben Luca <note>a 9th-century Melkite Christian physician</note> once wrote about "Physical Bindings," things not physical, yet proven (as they think) by experience; he says: "If the little finger of an aborted fetus is hung from a woman's neck, she will not conceive as long as it hangs there." But now, regarding the words by which the Almighty Creator 

<margin>E</margin> made heaven and earth, if they are bound <note>as an amulet</note>, will anyone (they ask) say they can do nothing? Surely the men of my sect believe much in the great master Rabbi Assi, who wrote in the **Book of Unity** <note>original: ספר היחוד (Sefer ha-Yichud)</note> that one wishing to ask for and obtain desired things should turn himself to the clemency and mercies of God, using these characters: **ANAKTAM PASTAM PASPASIM DIONSIM** <note>original: אנקתם פסתם פספסים דיונסים, the 22-letter Name of God</note>, which are found to be worthy memorials of Holy Scripture; of which kind many others are held, with which almost all the 

<margin>F</margin> books of the Cabalists are filled. Others also study to fashion illustrious seals from divine letters, which may prevail against men's ill health and other troubles, proven by long use. Such is that seal, for example, which Rabbi Hama composed in the *Book of Speculation* <note>original: *Sefer ha-Iyyun*</note> from four non-magical but solemn and common sacred names—or rather, he received it as composed by the fathers: **YHWH, Ehieh, Adonai, Yahu** <note>original: יהוה, אהיה, אדני, יאו</note>. In the Cabala, this is the same as **El** <note>God</note>. 

<margin>G</margin> The practitioners of that science take the first character of the first name <note>Y</note>, the first of the second <note>A</note>, the first of the third <note>A</note>, and the first of the fourth <note>I</note>, and the first seal becomes **YAAI** <note>original: יאאי</note>. Then they work in like manner concerning the second letters of the four most sacred names, and there arises **HHDA** <note>original: ההדא</note>. They fashion the third seal in the same way, from each of the third letters...

<meta>This page continues a dialogue on the practical and mystical application of sacred names and symbols. The speaker, Simon, is explaining how the Hebrew letters of the Tetragrammaton are combined into meditative "seals" to invoke divine power, transitioning from theoretical Kabbalah into its "applied" or "miraculous" form.</meta>

### BOOK THREE

...they join the letters, and the name **Yahweh** <note>original: יהוה, the four-letter Name of God</note> is born. Finally, in the same manner, they couple the last letters, and the fourth seal arises, which is **Yahweh**. The intention of these four seals is: **The Lord our God, the Lord is one** <note>original: יהוה אלהינו יהוה אחד, the opening of the Shema prayer</note>; and they say this should be the inscription for the four seals joined together. Finally, on the back of the parchment, they depict **ARLARITA** <note>original: ארלאריתא, a Kabbalistic acronym</note> which is interpreted as: *One, the Beginning of His unity, the Beginning of His singularity, His substitution, One.* <margin>B</margin> This "substitution" is understood to be a literary one, according to the third part of the Kabbalistic art <note>likely referring to Temurah, the art of rearranging letters</note>. Thus, they stand with these seals and inscriptions before the Most High with a soul devoted to God; whatever blessing they might ask for from those eighteen blessings, or those contained in other righteous prayers, they hope to unfailingly obtain. They trust they can break every fate often threatening from heaven, or mitigate the **Adrasteia** <note>original: ἀδράστειαν, a Greek term for the "inevitable" power of divine laws</note> by means of prayers made with these words. <margin>C</margin> For they believe a Kabbalist who is well-initiated, not only in characters and figures but also in words and songs, can accomplish any wonder, however admirable—something which even some of your own people confess can be done. Plotinus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher, c. 204–270 CE</note>, in his *Doubts of the Soul*, book two, chapter thirty-five, enumerates four things in which a miraculous power resides: namely, the hidden qualities of species, figures, harmonies, and vows. Porphyry and Iamblichus also say that we have command over the lowest spirits through God properly, and through the good Angels. Nor is there found in the entire circuit of the earth any race of men who more easily agree with this opinion than—as the story goes—the more divine Christians, who cast out demons by names and figures, lay hands on the sick and they recover, heal those who have taken deadly things, and perform similar miracles. But (to speak the truth as they assert it), they attribute all these things to faith instead, although <margin>D</margin> they also believe there is some power inherent in prayers. For they say and believe that the prayer of faith will save the sick; nor do capable Kabbalists think otherwise, for they likewise affirm that miraculous operations depend on God alone and on the faith of the man. Therefore, they pronounce those people to be liars and fools who grant such great force and power of miracles to the figure alone, the writing alone, the lines alone, or the voices born of broken air alone, as Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides, the famous 12th-century Jewish philosopher</note> testifies in the first book of *The Guide for the Perplexed*, chapter seventy-two. To this, Philolaus says: Not only <margin>F</margin> the Hebrew Kabbalists, but even the most outstanding of the Greeks, attributed much to the marks and seals of faith. For Antiochus, surnamed Soter <note>Antiochus I, a king of the Seleucid Empire</note>, when he was on an expedition against the Galatians—strong men fortified by an innumerable gathering of soldiers—was about to join a most difficult battle. When, as Lucian writes of him, **he was in very poor hopes** <note>original: πάνυ πονηρῶς εἶχε τας ἐλπίδας</note>, he saw in a dream at night <margin>G</margin> Alexander standing by him, ordering him to announce to his soldiers before the fight, as a military password, a certain sign of **Health**. It was of such a kind as would be marked on their clothing, as that same man of Samosata <note>Lucian of Samosata</note> noted regarding the error in greeting: **a triple**

<column-break/>

**triangle interlaced, the five-lined figure** <margin>v. Pier. Hierogly. lib. 47. c. 1.</margin>
<note>The text refers to the Pentagram, used here as a symbol of health.</note>
<image-desc>A five-pointed star (pentagram) containing the Greek letters Υ, Γ, Ι, Ε, Α at its points, spelling "Hygieia" or Health.</image-desc>
<note>original Greek: τριπλουν τρίγωνον δι' ἀλλήלων το πεντάγραμμον</note>, that is, a triple triangle interlaced with five lines. Antiochus, having raised that sign, achieved a wonderful victory against the Galatians. I myself have indeed often seen that symbol of the pentagon struck on the silver coinage of Antiochus; when resolved into lines, it shows the word **HYGIEIA**, or (which is exactly the same) **Health** in Latin. 
<margin>A</margin> Martianus says: Will it not be relevant to mention the sign of God (as they then called the cross) which once appeared from above to Constantine the Great in the midday hour before his entire army, inscribed with Latin letters thus: **IN THIS CONQUER** <note>original: IN HOC VINCE</note>? And Constantine did indeed conquer by that same sign, and was then chosen and hailed as Emperor by the applause of the Roman people, and was named the Most Invincible of all Emperors. Therefore, great men will be witnesses to how much power seals and marks have held: <margin>C</margin> for the Jews, Maccabees; for the Greeks, Antiochus; for the Romans, Constantine.
<margin>B</margin> Nor does it escape you, Simon, what you spoke of a little while ago concerning the Christians. For there is nothing under this heaven more wonderful than that race in the making of signs, characters, and words; they stay the seas, calm the winds, and repel lightning by the figure of the Cross and the name of **JESUS**. Moreover, there is nothing stronger than that character and image of the Cross, and nothing more health-bringing in dangers; although (to confess freely) <margin>D</margin> for no other reason than that they stand as a symbol of the true Savior, just as the name **Yahweh**, that **TETRAGRAMMATON**, is a symbol of God to you. And what the Kabbalists can do in the ineffable name, with the seals and characters recently shown by you, the faithful Christians can do in a much more powerful way through the pronounceable name of **JESUS** <note>original: IESV</note>, with the proper sign of the cross—since they consider themselves to pronounce the name Tetragrammaton far more correctly in the name **Yeshu'a** <note>original: ישוע</note> of the true Messiah. To this, they cite what is written in your **Midrash Tehillim** <note>original: מדרש תהלים, a commentary on the Psalms</note>: <margin>E</margin> *Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said in the name of... why do Israel pray in this world and are not answered? Because they do not know the **Explicit Name** <note>original: שם המפורש (Shem HaMephorash)</note>, that is, the name Tetragrammaton.* So it is said there. Then Simon replied: Perhaps you are right. But why use words? Certainly, the wiser Kabbalists <margin>F</margin> wish to refer this figure of the cross to the wood of the bronze serpent set up in the desert, though very silently and secretly; and this they do through **Gematria** <note>original: גימטריא, the practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew words</note>, that is, through equality of number. For the characters of these words, **Tzelem** <note>original: צלם, meaning image/figure, here used for Cross</note> and **Etz** <note>original: עץ, meaning wood/tree</note>, both symbolize one hundred and fifty <note>The author notes they sum to the same value, creating a mystical link</note>; wherefore a transition is easily made from one to the other, from the cross to the wood, and from the wood to the cross. But I press my finger to my lip. The shortness of time constrains me, best of friends, so that I have said less than I wished. And yet I reluctantly deprive myself of that joy of mine growing from the ornament and dignity of your speech, since in such a thick night when it is time to sleep, they have failed: we who have not acted like Sophists with common, trifling, and thin talk, nor in a gladiatorial combat of words or a contention of opinions with me until now...

<summary>This page explores the practical power of divine names and symbols, linking Jewish Kabbalistic seals with historical Greek and Christian signs like the pentagram of Antiochus and the cross of Constantine. It argues that miracles result from faith combined with these sacred forms, specifically connecting the name of Jesus to the Tetragrammaton through numerical and symbolic reasoning.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the third book of the dialogue. Simon, the primary teacher of Kabbalistic secrets, provides a final warning about the dangers of this spiritual path before the characters depart. The discussion moves from the specific use of divine names to the broader structure of the spiritual universe and the moral requirements of the practitioner.</meta>

# OF THE KABBALAH
772

<margin>A</margin> ...not with disputed matters, but with an accurate and sharp manner of speaking, and with thoughts suited and adapted to the subject at hand, so that I might wish longer spans of days were granted to us. For no one can speak sufficiently about the Kabbalistic art in a brief moment; such matters are so great, so deep, so innumerable, and so full of peril that anyone eager and studious of this cause must strive with the utmost powers of his intellect. One must look around not only to see with what industry it must be learned, but also with what danger it must be moderated and practiced. <margin>B</margin> For since this science is both *of* spiritual things and is *itself* spiritual, and since a man cannot easily pass judgment on spirits—even one who has been granted the power of judging between Angels and demons by some discrete weighing or even by a balanced rule—it is certainly not without much dread, nor without first purifying one’s morals, that this faculty and exercise should be properly undertaken. We must act so that we do not suffer the fate of the prophet Balaam <note>A biblical figure who, though a prophet, was led astray by greed and pride; see Numbers 22-24</note>, nor imitate the mother of the living <note>A reference to Eve and the Fall in Genesis</note>, nor follow darkness under the appearance of light. Fear for yourselves these spirits cast down by lightning and these most cruel enemies of ours; and believe me, just as the Angels carry their banners among us mortals, so too do the Devils. In the army of God there are four leaders: **Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael** <note>original: מיכאל גבריאל אוריאל רפאל</note>: just like the four elements, according to the four directions, or according to the four spiritual numerations <note>likely referring to the Sefirot</note>, just as formerly the children of Israel marched under four banners (Numbers 2): to the East <margin>D</margin> **Judah**, to the South **Reuben**, to the West **Ephraim**, and **Dan** to the North. Likewise, in the army of Satan, the avenging standard-bearers carry very wide sails: **Samael, Azazel, Azahel, and Mahazael** <note>original: סמאל עזאזל עזאל מחזאל</note>: about whom Menahem Recanati <note>A prominent 14th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> treats in his commentary on Leviticus 16 and in his first book on the Pentateuch; in which place he also cites the **Targum Jonathan** <note>An ancient Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> himself regarding Genesis. Furthermore, there still abound great crowds and legions of demons, all fugitives and escapees from Tartarus <note>The deep abyss of the underworld</note>, having their portion in the scapegoat; these I shall omit to list here because of their filth and horror, although a great many are included in Holy Scripture. But I now make an end of speaking with a proverb of the Kabbalists: **The prudent shall understand** <note>original: המשכיל יבין; a common phrase in mystical literature suggesting deeper secrets are hidden for the wise</note>: if I also add this, that **Michael** was **that high priest** <note>original: הוא הכהן הגדול</note>,

<column-break/>

<margin>A</margin> sacrificing in the upper world, who presents the spotless souls of men to the Blessed God, but sends those that are impure and burdened with vices to the Devil. Thus the high priest in the lower world, as it is written in Leviticus, is commanded to offer clean and innocent animals to God, but to hand over those burdened with crimes and a mass of guilt to Satan. The Kabbalists diligently approve of this, saying: **For all lower matters are counterparts to the higher ones, and as it is done below, so it is done above** <note>original: כי כל העניינים התחתונים הם מנגדיים לעליונים וכפי העשות למטה כך נעשה למעלה; this is a central tenet of Kabbalah and Hermeticism</note>. <margin>B</margin> These things portend something owed to both virtues and vices, so that each person must take care in what manner he lives and in what manner he dies. For this is our whole Philosophy: that by living well, we may die well—lest by chance we become the portion of the underworld and the avenging furies, with all hope frustrated, and then evil happens to the evil man. <margin>C</margin> Now, though it grieves me greatly, I think we must depart, since I have been chatting with you from morning until night, becoming more talkative than was proper. For just as I judge myself kindly, I do not judge you unworthily, as sleep urges you to go to rest. Then they said: "We are torn away from you so reluctantly, Simon, wishing to hear you forever; therefore, do not say a word about being 'too talkative.' But as you command, we obey you and depart, intended to return to you tomorrow, unless it is inconvenient for you." To this Simon said: "I cannot hide from you, my friends, what I have decided for myself. Tomorrow I shall migrate to distant parts, called away for the sake of a wedding, since my uncle has taken a wife in **Ratisbon** <note>Modern-day Regensburg, Germany</note>; may the matter turn out well." Then Philolaus said: "I would urge you with all my strength to stay, were it not unfair. Indeed, we are not born (I confess) for ourselves alone; we grant a portion of ourselves to our friends by their own right. Therefore, giving thanks to you, we pray for auspicious things for your journey and for your people." <margin>E</margin> Here Marranus, touched by sorrow at once, said: "Go prosperously and happily, dearest Simon, and best of men. Meanwhile, we are forced to wait for the end of the **Frankfurt fairs** <note>The Frankfurt Book Fair and trade fairs were major European events even in the 16th century</note>, so that with the merchants of our own country, we may each return more safely from this marketplace to our own fatherland." Then Simon, according to the custom of his people, said: "**Peace be with you**." To which both of them said: "Farewell. Go with God; go as one of ours."

### THE END OF THE DIALOGUE ON THE KABBALISTIC ART.

**LEONI** <note>A signature or printer's mark</note>

<meta>This page transitions from the philosophical dialogue of the "De Arte Cabalistica" to a formal dedication addressed to Pope Leo X. The author, Johannes Reuchlin (writing under his Greek pseudonym "Capnio"), defends his work and his character against the backdrop of the intense legal and theological controversy known as the "Reuchlin Affair," which involved the theologians of Cologne and the burning of Hebrew books.</meta>

# TO POPE LEO X.

## FROM CAPNIO.

<image-desc>A rectangular woodcut headpiece featuring intricate floral and foliate scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

<margin>A</margin>
You have here, Leo the Tenth, from Capnio <note>The Greek pseudonym of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), meaning "smoky," a play on his German name *Rauch*.</note> your humble servant, a brief compendium reciting the opinions and sentences of the ancients regarding the symbolic philosophy of Pythagoras and the wisdom of the Kabbalah. Though these are few in number, they offer the diligent student a much broader opportunity for reflection and investigation. Regarding these matters, I—a man of modest wit and minute prudence—would not dare to judge <margin>B</margin> anything, nor shall I indeed judge. Instead, I submit this entire book to your authority, to whose judgment the censorship of the whole world has been committed, so that you may reject what displeases you; then I shall rejoice that the rest has found favor. 

I trust that this effort of mine, which you may consider undertaken for the sake of both our people and the Commonwealth, will not seem entirely improper to you. This is partly because, through my labor, the works of others are opened to our people, and partly because during this half-year of reading them, I have sought to lighten—if it could not be avoided entirely—that five-year war which my enemies have waged against me with your knowledge. Finally, I did this so that you might possess something of mine, ensuring a more benevolent memory of me whenever my enemies strive to break or turn away your fatherly spirit toward me. 

For I know they do not cease daily to test your pious ears with whispers, sometimes through hired middlemen, sometimes through letters—such as the one I recently read, addressed to you on the fourteenth of the Kalends of October <note>September 18th</note> from Cologne <note>original: "Agrippina Colonia"</note>, whose title lies about its author just as it does with its false accusations. <margin>C</margin> For it was not that venerable University of Cologne that did this deed, but rather a "particularity"—a certain singular filth of enemies, a tiny and more insane part of the city—who affirmed to your Holiness things that are not true. They acted against Apostolic Prohibitions and against the peace commanded by the Emperor. 

You see also what audacity is in those same letters: they presume to prescribe laws to you as if they were the laws of Solon <note>An ancient Athenian lawmaker</note>, and to teach you the very source of law. They dictate the path the judgment must take according to their whim and will, so that they might more easily crush me with their slanders, as if my innocence were not already a certainty to almost the entire world. Hence, I cannot be led to suspect that you would have faith in those who—despising the Apostolic prohibition and scorning your censures—burned my little book while the lawsuit was still pending, showing the least possible regard for the path of the Law. 

You will instead believe the weightier men of Upper Germany, who are beyond all reproach, that I have caused no scandal nor provided any occasion for ruin before any of the German people. I am joined to them by the fellowship of a common language—a language unknown to those "Belgians" <note>Reuchlin often used the term "Belgae" to disparagingly refer to the theologians of the Lower Rhine/Cologne region.</note>—in which I published my "Chamber Council" <note>original: "Consilium meum illud Camerarium"</note> together with its plain declaration in a single context, as was fitting. You can certainly believe this securely, and all the more firmly because you have been informed of my innocence, piety, faith, and integrity by many most illustrious rulers of the widest

<column-break/>

lands of our nation, by magistrates, by the German people, and by the most holy Bishops of our dioceses, as well as by towns and cities, nearly three years ago through sealed and trustworthy letters. 

There exist in your possession testimonies offered three and four times over for my innocence from the unconquered elected Emperor of the Romans, Maximilian the Great, to you, Leo, and from the most reverend Cardinal, my Lord of Gurk <note>Matthäus Lang von Wellenburg</note>. After the Bishops, the most illustrious governors of provinces and Dukes born of the noblest blood also gave their support: the Electors of the Empire, Frederick of Saxony and Ludwig of Bavaria (the Regent), the Duke of Württemberg, the Margrave of Baden, and the most valiant Master of the Teutonic Order. 

Alongside these are the reverend and God-beloved Bishops of Germany: the Bishop of Worms, the Bishop of Strasbourg, and the Bishop of Constance, who acknowledges me as his own sheep. There is also the Bishop of Speyer, the judge assigned by your Holiness to this dispute, who, acting by your authority and with the counsel of experts, delivered a definitive sentence in favor of my innocence and that of my writings. Along with them, fifty-three towns of Swabia—all most dutiful, brave, and upright men—gave letters of recommendation and documents as witnesses to my right faith, probity, and harmlessness. 

The strength and weight of their testimony is increased by prelates of the Church noted for their distinguished learning and gravity. <margin>D</margin> To the most reverend judges of our cause, Cardinals Grimani and Accolti <note>original: "Anconitano," referring to the Cardinal of Ancona</note>—pillars of the Orthodox faith—you joined senatorial assessors as if they were a porch of columns: lights of the world, Archbishops, Bishops, Generals of Orders and their procurators, magistrates of Roman Wisdom, Penitentiaries, and other most choice Doctors of Theology and Law. These men, in the history of my times, deserve to be named according to their individual dignities. 

In so many public sessions held in your Majesty’s domestic sanctuary, which they call the <margin>E</margin> Pontifical Chapel, my case was always managed (as he does all things faithfully) by that most skilled orator of the law, Johannes Vanderbico <note>Jan van der Wyck, a lawyer who represented Reuchlin in Rome.</note>, a man as noble in his knightly rank as he is a fierce debater in the defense of causes, and my same Procurator. Finally, in the last session, after the cause was fully recognized, they decreed through written sentences that I should be freed and absolved from this injurious persecution. 

Nor is there any doubt that the definitive sentence of the same oracle <margin>F</margin> would have followed from the most reverend judges, as it ought to have, had the accusers not then obtained from you a mandate for staying the proceedings, as they claimed. If you will recall the testimonies and vows of all those whom I have now cited from every side, and if you will see to it that the acts of the judgments are read before you, you will find clearly that I am entirely foreign to every accusation of the informers. Nearly the entire city of Rome leaps to support my purity, as do those of all nations...

<summary>Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio) dedicates his work on Pythagorean and Kabbalistic philosophy to Pope Leo X, defending his character and work against the legal attacks of the Cologne theologians. He lists a vast array of high-ranking political and ecclesiastical supporters, including the Emperor and various German princes, to prove his orthodoxy and innocence.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the formal dedication to Pope Leo X. Reuchlin (Capnio) transitions from discussing the content of his work to a personal plea for protection, highlighting his contributions to Christian scholarship—specifically his pioneering work in Greek and Hebrew—as a defense against his theological opponents in Germany.</meta>

### BOOK THREE OF THE KABBALAH.

<margin>A</margin> all the most learned men, from whom I daily receive authoritative letters even from the ends of the earth, confirming that I have never been a source of scandal to any man through my writings. On the contrary, they affirm that I daily build up and plant the Church for the Holy Spirit—the same Spirit who, through the diversity of all tongues, gathered the nations into the unity of the faith. They surely observe that I was the first of all to bring Greek learning back to Germany, and the first of all to bestow and hand down the art and study of the Hebrew language <note>original: "sermonis Hebraïci"</note> to the universal Church. For this reason, I hope that I

<column-break/>

do not hope in vain that the Church of posterity will not be ungrateful for my merits. I hope that you, Pope Leo, as an evaluator of deeds rather than words, will justly restore peace and tranquility of mind to me in return for my many and so difficult labors contributed as a benefit to the Orthodox faith <note>Reuchlin uses "Orthodox" here in its literal sense of "correct belief," referring to the Catholic Church.</note>. <margin>A</margin> But if you truly wish for me to remain perpetually subject to the persecution of evil men in this life, I shall rejoice greatly to be seen as worthy to suffer such great injuries <margin>B</margin> for our **CHRIST**.

<note>A <term>ternion</term> (original: "terniones") is a printer's term for a gathering of three sheets of paper folded together to form six leaves. A <term>binion</term> (original: "duernio") is a smaller gathering of two sheets forming four leaves. This "register" helped the binder verify that no parts of the book were missing.</note>

<note>Pietro Galatino’s "On the Secrets of Catholic Truth" and Johann Reuchlin’s "On the Art of the Kabbalah" were often bound together in this period, as both sought to find Christian theological truths within Hebrew mystical and scholarly traditions.</note>
